Records intent for anyone reading the schema_config file. columns[].comment string no Attached as the output column's metadata["comment"] — the same schema-metadata key Delta/Unity Catalog read as a genuine column comment when the table is created, so it takes effect with no separate DDL step. Verify with DESCRIBE TABLE EXTENDED <table> after a real pipeline run.

{{catalog}}/{{env}} placeholders inside the file's own content (not just the path — e.g. inside a comment string) are substituted the same way the main onboarding spec is.

docs.title: Why nullable isn't enforced
docs.text:
Spark's .cast() cannot force a column to be non-nullable independent of the data actually flowing through it — nullability is derived from the expression, not something you can declare your way into. If you need genuine enforcement (fail or quarantine a row whose value is actually null), add a companion dq_config rule referencing the target name:

"dq_config": {
  "rules": [
    {"rule_id": "customer_id_not_null", "expression": "customer_id IS NOT NULL", "action": "fail"}
  ]
}

docs.title: schema_config_path: exact file vs. directory ("latest")
docs.text:
schema_config_path accepts either shape:

  • An exact file path — used directly, no resolution needed.
  • A directory path — resolved to the file inside it with the most recent modification time (resolve_schema_config_path in ingestion/schema_config.py), ties broken by the lexicographically-largest filename. This lets you drop a new schema version into a Volume directory (schema_v1.json, schema_v2.json, ...) without editing the onboarding spec's path on every change — the pipeline always picks up whichever file was written most recently the next time it runs.
/Volumes/{{catalog}}/landing/_schema_configs/customer/
├── schema_v1.json   (older modification time)
└── schema_v2.json   (newer modification time)  <-- this one is used

Concretely: os.listdir() the directory, keep only files (not subdirectories), sort by (modification_time, filename), take the last one. If the directory is empty, or the given path doesn't exist as either a file or a directory, FrameworkConfigError is raised immediately — a misconfigured path fails the pipeline update loudly rather than silently reading nothing.

Practical implication: if you want a specific, pinned version regardless of what else gets dropped into the directory later, point schema_config_path at the exact file, not the directory. Use the directory form only when you deliberately want "always the newest" behavior.

docs.title: Structural validation
docs.text: onboarding/spec_validator.py checks schema_config_path is a non-empty string at onboarding time — it does not read or validate the referenced file's own content at onboarding time (onboarding runs as a job task with no guaranteed Volume/workspace file access of its own to the path a pipeline will later read from; the file is only ever actually loaded at pipeline graph-definition time, inside 03_lakeflow_declarative_pipeline.py). A malformed schema_config file surfaces as a pipeline update failure (FrameworkConfigError), not an onboarding-time error — check the pipeline's own update logs if schema_config_path looks right in the spec but the pipeline still fails to start.

docs.title: Relevant files
docs.text:
• src/flowx/lakeflow_framework/ingestion/column_normalization.py — normalize_column_name (pure), normalize_column_names (DataFrame).
  • src/flowx/lakeflow_framework/ingestion/schema_config.py — resolve_schema_config_path, load_schema_config, apply_schema_config.
  • src/flowx/lakeflow_framework/onboarding/spec_validator.py — _validate_ingestion_source_config's normalize_column_names/schema_config_path checks.
  • onboarding_templates/schema_config_example.json / .yaml — the worked example above, in full.
  • notebooks/03_engine/03_lakeflow_declarative_pipeline.py — the exact call order.
  • tests/unit/test_column_normalization.py, tests/unit/test_schema_config.py — including the DataFrame-transform tests (live spark fixture, no table created — same convention as tests/unit/test_column_ordering.py).

docs.title: Test Pipeline: Continuous Event-Log → OTel Streaming Export
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md (Module 9: Observability & Telemetry Framework).

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Prove the new Design 1 capability: a genuinely continuous Lakeflow Declarative Pipeline that unions N other pipelines' published event-log tables into one streaming table (tagged with source_pipeline) and exports it continuously to an OpenTelemetry OTLP/HTTP endpoint via a custom dlt.create_sink/@dlt.append_flow pair — gated on/off by config, never touching the pre-existing batch observability engine (notebooks/08_observability/08_dlt_observability_engine.py).

This is new infrastructure, not a metadata-driven onboarded flow — there is no onboarding spec for this scenario; it is configured entirely through its own pipeline resource's configuration: block.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Read every table listed in dataflow.otel_streaming.event_log_tables (a JSON array of fully-qualified Unity Catalog table names) as a Structured Streaming source.
  • Tag every row with source_pipeline (the source table's own fully-qualified name).
  • Materialize the tagged union as one real streaming table, unified_event_log.
  • When dataflow.otel_streaming.otel_export_enabled is "true": register a custom otel_streaming sink Data Source and stream unified_event_log into it via @dlt.append_flow, which POSTs one OTLP ResourceLogs JSON payload per micro-batch to dataflow.otel_streaming.otel_endpoint. When "false" (the checked-in default): the sink/flow are never created at all — unified_event_log still materializes, but nothing is exported.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• This scenario has no ingestion/onboarding fixtures of its own. It reads whichever tables you list in event_log_tables — normally the published event log tables of other pipelines already deployed in this project (e.g. flowx_test_002_zerobus_pipeline, flowx_test_003_autoload_recon_pipeline). A source pipeline only has a queryable event-log table (as opposed to only the event_log(pipeline_id) TVF every pipeline already has) once you explicitly turn on Pipeline settings → Advanced → "Event log" → a catalog.schema.table destination for it — this is a one-time manual step per source pipeline, not something this new pipeline or its job can do for you.
  • resources/observability_otel_streaming_pipeline.yml's configuration: block ships with two placeholder table names (observability.event_logs.pipeline_1/pipeline_2) — replace these with your real published event-log table names before deploying if you want a live run; left as-is, databricks bundle deploy still succeeds and the pipeline starts, it just streams from tables that don't exist yet (which will fail at run time, not at deploy time — this is a config placeholder, not a working default).

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• {catalog}.observability_streaming.unified_event_log — the unified, source_pipeline-tagged streaming table. Always materializes, regardless of otel_export_enabled.
  • Output file / external artifact: when export is enabled, one OTLP ResourceLogs JSON HTTP POST body per micro-batch, sent to otel_endpoint — this is the "file" this scenario produces, except it's a request body delivered to an external collector, not a file written to a Volume (unlike the batch observability engine's .jsonl.gz Volume export — see docs/25_dlt_observability_module.md). There is no local artifact to inspect after a run beyond the collector's own ingestion record, since this design intentionally has no Volume fallback (that's the batch engine's job, untouched by this one).

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
resources/observability_otel_streaming_pipeline.yml:

configuration:
  dataflow.otel_streaming.event_log_tables: '["observability.event_logs.pipeline_1", "observability.event_logs.pipeline_2"]'
  dataflow.otel_streaming.otel_endpoint: https://otel-collector.example.com/v1/logs
  dataflow.otel_streaming.otel_export_enabled: "false"

continuous: true on the pipeline resource itself is what makes this genuinely always-on — every other pipeline resource in this project sets continuous: false (triggered/on-demand).

docs.title: Main execution flow
docs.text:
There is no job wrapper for this scenario (see the resource YAML's own header comment for why — a continuous: true pipeline's lifecycle is Databricks' to manage once started, not a job's):

databricks bundle deploy --target dev
databricks bundle run observability_otel_streaming_pipeline --target dev

Starting it launches an update that keeps running indefinitely — new files/rows arriving in any configured event-log table get picked up and (if enabled) exported continuously, with no --full-refresh/re-trigger needed between arrivals. Stop it via the Pipelines UI or databricks pipelines stop.

docs.title: Expected results — simulation notes (this pass was verified structurally, not live)
docs.text:
This environment has no live external OTLP collector and no already-published event-log source tables to point at, so this scenario was not run end-to-end against a real workspace as part of building it. What was actually verified:

  • ast.parse/import checks on every new/changed file (otel_streaming_sink.py, otel_payload_builder.py's new function, the new engine notebook) — all pass.
  • An offline unit test of build_resource_logs_from_event_rows against synthetic row dicts, confirming correct per-source_pipeline grouping, timestamp conversion, and graceful handling of a row with a null timestamp/level.
  • An offline end-to-end wiring test: synthetic rows → build_resource_logs_from_event_rows → a minimal DestinationConfig → dispatch_to_otlp with a fake post_fn, confirming a SUCCESS result and that the (deliberately-stubbed, should-never-fire) secret resolver is never actually invoked.
  • databricks bundle validate passes with this pipeline resource included.

Not verified: a real streaming run against live published event-log tables; whether the restricted "python streaming data source runtime" worker process that runs commit() genuinely permits outbound HTTPS via requests (a documented, reasoned assumption in otel_streaming_sink.py's module docstring, not a re-confirmed fact — the only restriction this project has hit live in that runtime is against spawning a dbutils gateway subprocess, not network calls in general). To actually validate this scenario: publish at least one real pipeline's event log to a table, point event_log_tables at it, set otel_export_enabled: "true" and a real reachable otel_endpoint (or a local test HTTP listener), deploy, run, and watch unified_event_log populate plus the sink's own driver logs for "committed microbatch" lines.

docs.title: Test Pipeline: Reconciliation Feature Test (Scenario 004)
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md (Module 7 & 11), flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Prove the new Design 2 reconciliation capabilities added this pass: 1. Conditional reconciliation_run_log/reconciliation_mismatch_log capture, gated per-flow by logging_config.run_log_capture/mismatch_log_capture. 2. The always-populated reconciliation_result summary table, independent of that gating. 3. task_run_id threading from a parent job into every log/result row for correlation. 4. recon_mode: "continuous" — a genuinely always-on streaming trigger, as opposed to today's default "triggered" (availableNow-drain) mode.

Hash key + hash value generation (__framework_hash_key/__framework_hash_value) is not new — it already existed in cdc/hashing.py/reconciliation/matcher.py before this pass; this scenario exercises it only incidentally (as a regression check), not as new functionality.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Reuse scenario 002/003's own already-onboarded bronze tables ({catalog}.bronze_excalibur.autoload_bronze / zerobus_bronze) as a source/target pair — reconciliation is not a Lakeflow Declarative Pipeline flow type (see flowx_test_003_autoload_recon_pipeline.yml's own header comment), so this scenario needs no dedicated pipeline of its own, only onboarding + 05_reconciliation_engine.py tasks.
  • Three reconciliation flows, all comparing the same table pair, all comparison_direction: "target_to_source" (audit-only — deliberately never mutates anything, unlike scenario 003's own flow, which already exercises the self-healing append path):
  • recon_004_logging_on — logging_config: {run_log_capture: true, mismatch_log_capture: true}.
  • recon_004_logging_off — both false.
  • recon_004_continuous — target read_mode: "streaming", run via the recon_mode: "continuous" widget.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• flowx_testing/004_recon_features_test.json — reconciliation-only onboarding spec (no ingestion_flows/transformation_flows).
  • Depends on scenario 002/003's own fixtures — flowx_test_004_recon_features_job re-runs their full setup/seed/onboard/pipeline chain itself first, so this scenario is self-contained (works from a clean environment, not only after 002/003 happen to have already run).

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• {catalog}.config.reconciliation_run_log — one new row for recon_004_logging_on only (not _logging_off, not _continuous unless it independently defaults logging on — it does, since its logging_config is both true).
  • {catalog}.config.reconciliation_mismatch_log — rows for recon_004_logging_on (and recon_004_continuous) if any VALUE_DRIFT/MISSING_IN_SOURCE records exist between the two tables; none for recon_004_logging_off.
  • {catalog}.config.reconciliation_result — one row per reconciliation_id, every time, regardless of the above — this is the "always populated" output file/table this scenario is specifically designed to prove.
  • All rows carry the same task_run_id (the job's own {{job.run_id}}) for the three tasks run together in one job execution.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: flowx_testing/004_recon_features_test.json's three reconciliation_flows[] entries (see file for full detail) — each sets logging_config explicitly (even the default-true case, for clarity in this test) and match_keys: ["customer_id"], compare_columns: ["customer_name", "status"].

docs.title: Main execution flow
docs.text:
databricks bundle deploy --target dev
databricks bundle run flowx_test_004_recon_features_job --target dev

Task chain: setup_control_tables → seed_flowx_testing_data → onboard_002 → run_002_pipeline → onboard_003 → run_003_pipeline → onboard_004 → {run_004_recon_logging_on, run_004_recon_logging_off, run_004_recon_continuous} (the last three run in parallel, all depending only on onboard_004).

run_004_recon_continuous does not finish on its own — recon_mode: "continuous" puts its one streaming target under an indefinite trigger (see reconciliation/streaming.py), so that task will show as still-running in the Jobs UI rather than completing, exactly as designed. Stop it manually (cancel the task/run) once you've confirmed it started successfully and its first micro-batch committed — do not expect this job run to reach a terminal SUCCESS state on its own while that task is included.

docs.title: Expected results — simulation notes
docs.text:
SQL assertions (after a run, replace {catalog} with your actual target catalog):

-- reconciliation_result: exactly 3 rows (one per reconciliation_id), all sharing task_run_id
SELECT reconciliation_id, task_run_id, status, matched_count, value_drift_count
FROM {catalog}.config.reconciliation_result
WHERE reconciliation_id IN ('recon_004_logging_on', 'recon_004_logging_off', 'recon_004_continuous')
ORDER BY run_at DESC LIMIT 3;

-- reconciliation_run_log: present for logging_on, ABSENT for logging_off
SELECT reconciliation_id, count(*) FROM {catalog}.config.reconciliation_run_log
WHERE reconciliation_id IN ('recon_004_logging_on', 'recon_004_logging_off')
GROUP BY reconciliation_id;
-- expect: recon_004_logging_on -> >=1 row; recon_004_logging_off -> 0 rows

This pass's actual verification status: see flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md for whether this job was actually run against the live workspace and what the real result was — this document describes what should happen structurally; the status tracker records what did happen, if anything, each time this scenario is executed.

docs.title: Real live-run results (2026-08-29)
docs.text:
recon_004_logging_on / recon_004_logging_off — fully verified live, exactly as designed. Real query results against flowx.config.* after a live run (job run id 830403105449437):

reconciliation_result:  recon_004_logging_on  -> SUCCESS, matched_count=7, task_run_id=830403105449437
                        recon_004_logging_off -> SUCCESS, matched_count=7, task_run_id=830403105449437
reconciliation_run_log: recon_004_logging_on  -> 1 row  (SUCCESS, task_run_id=830403105449437)
                        recon_004_logging_off -> 0 rows (correctly suppressed)

recon_004_continuous — code path executes correctly, but blocked by a real Databricks platform constraint, not a bug in this session's code. Running it live surfaced: [INFINITE_STREAMING_TRIGGER_NOT_SUPPORTED] Trigger type ProcessingTime is not supported for this cluster type. Use a different trigger type e.g. AvailableNow, Once. Root cause: Spark Structured Streaming's own default trigger (used whenever .trigger(...) is never called — which is what continuous=True, processing_time=None in reconciliation/streaming.py produces) is itself a ProcessingTime trigger under the hood — and Databricks serverless job compute (the environment_key: framework_env every job in this project already uses) rejects any unbounded streaming trigger outright, whether explicit or default. This is a platform-level restriction, not something fixable by passing a different processing_time value — the error message's own wording ("not supported for this cluster type") implies a non-serverless (classic) cluster would allow it, which this project doesn't use anywhere today.

What this run did prove working correctly: run_streaming_target_reconciliation(..., continuous=True) reaches the intended code path and genuinely attempts the continuous trigger (not silently falling back to availableNow); the failure propagated up cleanly through streaming.py's own except handling into 05_reconciliation_engine.py's outer error handler; because this flow's error_handling.on_failure is "warn", the job task still completed SUCCESS overall rather than hard-failing; and — the actual thing this scenario exists to prove — both reconciliation_run_log (run_log_capture: true) and reconciliation_result (always-on) received a FAILED row with the full real error message, confirming the failure-path logging/task_run_id threading works exactly like the success path.

Open follow-up, not fixed in this pass: making recon_mode: "continuous" actually run long-lived requires either a classic (non-serverless) cluster for that one job task, or restructuring continuous reconciliation to run inside a genuine Lakeflow continuous: true pipeline (the same mechanism Design 1 uses) rather than a plain serverless job task — a real architectural decision, not a quick patch.

Incidental fixes made to unblock this verification (pre-existing bugs, not introduced this session, but found and fixed while getting a real end-to-end run): * notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/02_seed_flowx_testing_data.py's seed_zerobus_style_table_from_csv() used whenMatchedUpdateAll()/whenNotMatchedInsertAll() (star merge), which fails the moment the target table has a column the fixture CSV doesn't (confirmed live: zerobus_source_bus had accumulated an extra updated_at column from scenario 003's own self-healing appends). Fixed to scope both clauses to source_df.columns, matching this codebase's own established dynamic-column MERGE pattern (onboarding/metadata_upsert.py). * onboarding/metadata_upsert.py's five control-table upsert functions all used whenNotMatchedInsertAll() — the same star-insert problem, confirmed live the moment a new nullable column (last_processed_cdc_version, logging_config_json — both added earlier this session) existed on an already-provisioned control table and a genuinely new row was inserted. Fixed all five to whenNotMatchedInsert(values={col: f"s.{col}" for col in source_df.columns}), consistent with their own whenMatchedUpdate clauses. * This workspace's flowx.config.* control tables (provisioned before this session) needed four manual ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMNS statements run once to pick up new columns added this session (reconciliation_run_log/reconciliation_mismatch_log.task_run_id, reconciliation_flow_spec.logging_config_json, ingestion_flow_spec/ transformation_flow_spec.last_processed_cdc_version) — CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS never retroactively adds a column to an existing table, exactly as flagged when those columns were first added. A fresh catalog would not need this step.

docs.title: Test Pipeline: Selective Glob Pattern ZIP Extraction (TC-ING-001)
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md (Module 1, TC-ING-001), flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Prove that source_config.source_zip_handling.zip_file_pattern genuinely filters which archives get extracted and ingested when the incoming Volume holds more than one ZIP file -- not just that ZIP extraction works in general (scenario 001 already proves that, but only ever lands one uniquely-named archive per flow, so it never exercises the filtering behavior itself). A non-matching archive must be left completely alone: not extracted, not ingested, and not deleted or otherwise modified in the incoming Volume.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Land 2 ZIP archives in the same incoming Volume:
  • customer_data_20260828.zip -- 100 rows, filename matches zip_file_pattern: "customer_*.zip".
  • vendor_feed_20260828.zip -- 50 rows, filename does not match that pattern.
  • One ingestion_flow (df_ing_001_customer_zip_filter_ingest) with source_type: "autoloader" and source_zip_handling.enabled: true, zip_file_pattern: "customer_*.zip", delete_source_after_extract: false (so both the matching and non-matching archive's post-run state in the incoming Volume can be inspected).
  • cdc_load_strategy: "APPEND" -- this scenario is about ZIP/file selection, not CDC behavior, so the simplest load strategy (plain streaming append, no primary_keys) keeps the flow focused on the one thing under test.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• flowx_testing/010_ing_001_zip_filter.json -- single-ingestion-flow onboarding spec (no transformation_flows/reconciliation_flows).
  • sample_data/flowx_testing/crm_usecase/customer_data.csv (100 rows) / vendor_feed.csv (50 rows) -- generated by sample_data/flowx_testing/crm_usecase/generate_crm_zip_filter_fixtures.py.
  • notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/03_seed_ing_001_zip_filter_data.py -- a new, dedicated seed notebook (kept separate from 02_seed_flowx_testing_data.py, which belongs to scenarios 001/002/003) that provisions the crm/bronze_crm schemas and landing_zip/_schemas Volumes, then zips each CSV fixture directly on-cluster into /Volumes/{{catalog}}/crm/landing_zip/incoming/ -- the same "build the archive bytes in-process" convention 02_seed_flowx_testing_data.py already uses for scenario 001's own ZIPs, since workspace-bundle sync can mangle a pre-built .zip upload.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• {{catalog}}.bronze_crm.customer_raw -- exactly 100 rows, all sourced from customer_data_20260828.zip.
  • vendor_feed_20260828.zip remains untouched in /Volumes/{{catalog}}/crm/landing_zip/incoming/ (not extracted, not deleted).
  • No vendor_feed records anywhere in {{catalog}}.bronze_crm.customer_raw or in /Volumes/{{catalog}}/crm/landing_zip/extracted/customer/ -- that extract Volume should contain only the CSV unpacked from customer_data_20260828.zip.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
flowx_testing/010_ing_001_zip_filter.json's one ingestion_flows[] entry:

"source_config": {
  "path": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/crm/landing_zip/extracted/customer/",
  "format": "csv",
  "schema_location": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/crm/_schemas/customer/",
  "source_zip_handling": {
    "enabled": true,
    "source_zip_path": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/crm/landing_zip/incoming/",
    "zip_file_pattern": "customer_*.zip",
    "target_volume_path": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/crm/landing_zip/extracted/customer/",
    "delete_source_after_extract": false
  }
}

target_config: {"cdc_load_strategy": "APPEND", "storage_format": "delta"} -- plain streaming table, no primary keys.

docs.text:
• New fixtures, not a reuse. No existing seeded fixture matches this scenario's exact requirement (2 specific archives with specific, verification-critical row counts of 100 and 50 landing in the same incoming Volume), so 2 new CSV fixtures and 1 new dedicated seed notebook were added rather than extending 02_seed_flowx_testing_data.py -- kept separate so this test case's build/run never touches scenarios 001/002/003's own shared seed step.
  • No run_observability_task. TESTING_PLAN.md's own "Proposed Pipeline & Job Architecture" column for TC-ING-001 names a second run_observability_task step, but per TESTING_STATUS.md's framing, TESTING_PLAN.md is a planned/aspirational matrix, not a literal build spec -- no other real scenario's job wires observability in by default (it's opt-in, added via a spec's own observability[] array plus a separate job, as scenario 100's dlt_observability_job.yml does). This build follows the real setup_control_tables → seed → onboard → run_pipeline convention instead; observability can be layered on later the same way scenario 100's was, if desired.

docs.title: Test Pipeline: ZIP Source Purge Retention Policy (TC-ING-002)
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Prove source_zip_handling.delete_source_after_extract: true (§3 of 01_control_metadata_schema.md) actually purges a landed ZIP archive from its incoming Volume once its contents have been successfully extracted -- distinct from the false default demonstrated elsewhere in this repo (scenario 001's ea_*.zip archives, and scenario 100's customer_plain_raw flow, both set it false explicitly so their source archives persist for repeated local test runs). This is a single-flow, ingestion-only scenario -- no CDC dispatch, no transformation, no reconciliation.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Land a single ZIP archive, orders_batch_01.zip, in /Volumes/{catalog}/sales/landing_zip/incoming/.
  • Extract it via Auto Loader's source_zip_handling into /Volumes/{catalog}/sales/landing_zip/extracted/orders/.
  • Ingest the extracted CSV into {catalog}.bronze_sales.orders_raw (cdc_load_strategy: "APPEND" -- an immutable batch of order records, no upsert/history concept needed).
  • Verify the source ZIP is gone from incoming/ post-extraction, the extracted CSV is present in extracted/orders/, and orders_raw holds the expected row count.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• flowx_testing/011_ing_002_zip_retention.json -- ingestion-only onboarding spec (no transformation_flows/reconciliation_flows), one flow: df_ing_002_zip_retention_orders_ingest.
  • sample_data/sample_raw_orders.csv -- reused as-is (10 rows: order_id, order_ts, account_id), no new sample data needed for this scenario. Re-zipped on-cluster into orders_batch_01.zip by notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/03_seed_ing_002_zip_retention_data.py (same in-memory-buffer-then-single-sequential-write pattern 02_seed_flowx_testing_data.py already uses for the ea_*.zip archives -- see 12_zip_ingestion_pipeline.md's platform-gotchas section for why a pre-built .zip can't just be synced through the bundle instead).

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• {catalog}.bronze_sales.orders_raw (Delta, streaming table) -- 10 rows, one per source order.
  • /Volumes/{catalog}/sales/landing_zip/incoming/orders_batch_01.zip -- absent after a successful pipeline update (this is the behavior under test).
  • /Volumes/{catalog}/sales/landing_zip/extracted/orders/orders_batch_01.csv -- present, the extracted member file Auto Loader read from.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
flowx_testing/011_ing_002_zip_retention.json's one ingestion flow:

"source_config": {
  "path": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/sales/landing_zip/extracted/orders/",
  "format": "csv",
  "schema_location": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/sales/_schemas/orders/",
  "reader_options": {"header": "true", "cloudFiles.inferColumnTypes": "true"},
  "capture_technical_metadata": true,
  "source_zip_handling": {
    "enabled": true,
    "source_zip_path": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/sales/landing_zip/incoming/",
    "zip_file_pattern": "orders_batch_01.zip",
    "target_volume_path": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/sales/landing_zip/extracted/orders/",
    "delete_source_after_extract": true
  }
},
"target_config": {"cdc_load_strategy": "APPEND", "storage_format": "delta"}

docs.title: Test Pipeline: TC-ING-003 -- Zerobus Streaming Delta Feed Ingestion (Append-Count Assertion)
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md (Module 1, TC-ING-003), flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md, docs/30_test_pipeline_recon_features.md (the doc-writing template this follows).

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Prove that source_type: "zerobus" ingestion (streaming read of an existing Delta table -- see 01_control_metadata_schema.md §3) correctly picks up a genuinely large batch of newly-appended source rows across two separate pipeline updates -- not just the handful of illustrative records scenario 002's own onboarding already exercises. This test deliberately reuses the already-deployed flowx_test_002_zerobus_pipeline (dataflow_group_id: dfg_flowx_002_zerobus_bronze) rather than standing up a dedicated pipeline of its own -- TC-ING-003 needs no new DAG shape, only a bigger, two-phase data volume against the existing one.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Seed {catalog}.Excalibur_usecase.zerobus_source_bus with 1,000 baseline synthetic customer rows (TC003-000001..TC003-001000), generated on-cluster -- additive to, and non-colliding with, scenario 002/003's own small C001-C007 fixture rows already in that table.
  • Re-onboard dfg_flowx_002_zerobus_bronze from this test's own spec (012_ing_003_zerobus_append.json) so this job is self-contained (works from a clean environment, the same pattern flowx_test_004_recon_features_job already uses to re-onboard scenario 002/003) -- the spec's ingestion flow is a faithful copy of 002_zerobus_data_load.json's own, so onboarding it is an idempotent no-op against an already-onboarded control-table row.
  • Run flowx_test_002_zerobus_pipeline once against the 1,000-row baseline.
  • Append 200 more synthetic rows (TC003-001001..TC003-001200) to the same source table.
  • Run the same pipeline a second time and confirm zerobus_bronze's row count grew by exactly 200 between the two updates.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• flowx_testing/012_ing_003_zerobus_append.json -- re-onboards dfg_flowx_002_zerobus_bronze / df_excalibur_zerobus_ingest (the same dataflow group and flow id scenario 002 already onboards); no new fields beyond that spec's own shape.
  • notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/03_seed_ing_003_zerobus_baseline.py -- new seed notebook, parameterized by id_prefix/start_index/row_count, called twice by this job (baseline 1,000, then append 200).
  • Depends on scenario 002's own seed step (02_seed_flowx_testing_data.py) having provisioned the Excalibur_usecase schema and zerobus_source_bus's baseline shape -- this job runs that step itself first, so it works standalone rather than assuming flowx_test_002_003_job has already run.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• {catalog}.Excalibur_usecase.zerobus_source_bus -- gains 1,000, then 200 more TC003-* rows, on top of whatever scenario 002/003 fixtures already put there.
  • {catalog}.bronze_excalibur.zerobus_bronze -- the shared Bronze streaming table scenario 002 also writes to; after this job's two pipeline updates, its row count has grown by exactly baseline_count + 200 attributable to this run (see Expected results for the exact delta-based assertion).

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
012_ing_003_zerobus_append.json's single ingestion_flows[] entry: source_type: "zerobus" reading {{catalog}}.Excalibur_usecase.zerobus_source_bus, target_config.cdc_load_strategy: "APPEND", targeting {{catalog}}.bronze_excalibur.zerobus_bronze -- the same shape as scenario 002's own spec, since this test is only about data volume, not a new configuration surface.

03_seed_ing_003_zerobus_baseline.py widgets:

Widget Purpose Baseline call Append call catalog Target catalog flowx flowx id_prefix Synthetic customer_id prefix TC003 TC003 start_index First synthetic row's 1-based index 1 1001 row_count How many rows to generate this call 1000 200

Rows are generated directly from spark.range(start_index, start_index + row_count) (no CSV fixture -- 1,000+ literal rows in a checked-in file would be unwieldy for no real fixture value) with customer_id = '<prefix>-%06d', customer_name = 'TC-ING-003 Synthetic Customer <n>', status = 'ACTIVE', then MERGEd into zerobus_source_bus scoped to just those 3 columns (the same dynamic-column MERGE idiom 02_seed_flowx_testing_data.py::seed_zerobus_style_table_from_csv already uses, so it never collides with any extra column the table has picked up from scenario 003's own self-healing appends, e.g. updated_at). Each call is idempotent: it first counts existing rows already inside its own [start_index, start_index + row_count) id range and skips generation entirely if that range is already fully populated.

docs.title: Main execution flow
docs.text:
databricks bundle deploy --target dev
databricks bundle run flowx_test_ing_003_zerobus_append_job --target dev

Task chain: setup_control_tables -> seed_flowx_testing_data -> seed_ing_003_zerobus_baseline -> onboard_ing_003 -> run_pipeline_baseline -> seed_ing_003_zerobus_append -> run_pipeline_append.

docs.title: Expected results
docs.text:
SQL assertions (replace {catalog} with your actual target catalog; capture n1 right after run_pipeline_baseline completes, then n2 after run_pipeline_append):

-- capture the bronze row count right after the first pipeline update (n1)
SELECT count(*) AS n1 FROM {catalog}.bronze_excalibur.zerobus_bronze;

-- after appending 200 rows and re-running the pipeline, confirm the delta is exactly 200
SELECT count(*) AS n2 FROM {catalog}.bronze_excalibur.zerobus_bronze;
-- expect: n2 - n1 = 200

-- confirm the source bus itself carries all 1,200 synthetic rows this test added
SELECT count(*) FROM {catalog}.Excalibur_usecase.zerobus_source_bus WHERE customer_id LIKE 'TC003-%';
-- expect: 1200

-- Change Data Feed cross-check: exactly 200 append events on the second update
SELECT count(*) FROM table_changes('{catalog}.bronze_excalibur.zerobus_bronze', <version_before_run_pipeline_append>, <version_after_run_pipeline_append>)
WHERE _change_type = 'insert';
-- expect: 200

TESTING_PLAN.md's original TC-ING-003 template describes an absolute assertion (count(*) = 1,200 exactly, against a dedicated pipeline/schema of its own). This build deliberately reuses scenario 002's shared pipeline and shared zerobus_source_bus/ zerobus_bronze tables instead (per this build's own task instructions), so the row-count assertion above is delta-based (n2 - n1 = 200) rather than an absolute literal, since zerobus_bronze may already carry rows from scenario 002/003/004's own prior runs before this job ever executes. The WHERE customer_id LIKE 'TC003-%' filter isolates this test's own synthetic rows from that pre-existing data everywhere it matters.

Not yet executed against a live workspace -- see flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md for actual run status; a later phase runs and records it centrally, per this build pass's own scope.

docs.title: Real gap / judgment calls made building this
docs.text:
• Reused the existing flowx_test_002_zerobus_pipeline / dfg_flowx_002_zerobus_bronze exactly as instructed, rather than TESTING_PLAN.md's own aspirational dedicated flowx_test_ing_003_zerobus_stream_pipeline/excalibur_usecase schema -- so this test shares its target tables with scenario 002/003/004. Synthetic rows are namespaced under a TC003- customer_id prefix specifically so they never collide with scenario 002/003/004's own C001-C007 fixture rows or their reconciliation-match assertions (which key off those exact ids) -- but this job does add ~1,200 extra rows to a table other scenarios also read from, and both this job and scenario 002/003's own job drive the same Zerobus streaming checkpoint, which is a real, shared-state fragility already flagged for this exact pipeline in TESTING_STATUS.md's scenario 002/003 row (running the two jobs concurrently against the same workspace is not safe; run them sequentially).
  • Generated the 1,000+200 baseline/append rows programmatically (spark.range(...)) in a new seed notebook rather than a static CSV fixture, since a 1,000-row literal CSV would add size with no real fixture value over generated data -- consistent with this build's own "keep this minimal" guidance.
  • The row-count verification is expressed as a delta (n2 - n1 = 200) rather than TESTING_PLAN.md's own absolute 1,200, since the shared table may already carry other scenarios' rows by the time this job runs -- see "Expected results" above for the reasoning.

docs.title: Test Pipeline: TC-ING-004 -- ASN.1 Binary Telecom CDR Decoding
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md (Module 1), flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md, 13_asn1_dq_quarantine.md (the pre-existing ASN.1 + DQ/quarantine demonstration this scenario is a dedicated, TC-*-numbered sibling of, not a replacement for).

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Prove source_type: "asn1" binary telecom CDR decoding end to end, as its own dedicated, independently deployable test case (TC-ING-004 in TESTING_PLAN.md's Module 1), using a brand-new GSM call-detail-record schema (gsm_cdr.asn) distinct from the existing telecom_cdr(_v2).asn fixtures docs/13_asn1_dq_quarantine.md already exercises. This scenario's fixture batch is deliberately all-valid -- it proves the clean-decode path (imsi/callDurationSeconds populated, zero _asn1_decode_error rows), not the decode-failure/quarantine-routing path, which docs/13 already covers with a mixed-quality batch.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Decode 3 ASN.1 BER-encoded GSM CDR files against a configured schema (gsm_cdr.asn, a SEQUENCE of imsi, imei, callDurationSeconds, cellId, roamingFlag).
  • Land the decoded output as a streaming Bronze table ({catalog}.bronze_telecom.cdr_stream_raw, cdc_load_strategy: "APPEND").
  • Apply 3 quarantine-action DQ rules (decode success, non-empty imsi, non-negative callDurationSeconds) as a structural safety net -- with an all-valid fixture batch, the expected outcome is zero quarantined rows, proving both the decode and the DQ rules agree the batch is clean.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• sample_data/asn1_schema/gsm_cdr.asn -- the real ASN.1 module file (verified locally: a full asn1tools.compile_files(...) compile + encode/decode round-trip, and the framework's own asn1/decoder.py::derive_asn1_field_defs schema-derivation, both run clean against it before this scenario was wired into a spec -- see below).
  • 3 CDR fixtures, generated directly on-cluster at seed time by notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/03_seed_asn1_gsm_cdr_fixture.py (not synced as pre-built binary files -- Databricks Workspace Files sync can mangle a raw .ber upload; identical rationale to docs/13_asn1_dq_quarantine.md's and sample_data/generate_asn1_dq_fixtures.py's own note): gsm_cdr_001.ber / gsm_cdr_002.ber / gsm_cdr_003.ber, all valid.
  • flowx_testing/013_ing_004_asn1_decode.json.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• {catalog}.bronze_telecom.cdr_stream_raw -- 3 rows, one per fixture, with imsi, imei, callDurationSeconds, cellId, roamingFlag, and _asn1_decode_error (NULL on every row) all populated per the ASN.1 -> Spark type mapping (imsi/imei/cellId -> string, callDurationSeconds -> bigint, roamingFlag -> boolean).
  • {catalog}.bronze_telecom.cdr_stream_raw_quarantine -- created (per register_main_and_quarantine_tables's conditional-creation rule -- see 17_onboarding_template_reference.md §4.7) since this spec's dq_config.rules include a quarantine-action rule, but expected empty (0 rows) for this all-valid fixture batch.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
flowx_testing/013_ing_004_asn1_decode.json's one ingestion_flows[] entry:

"source_config": {
  "path": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/telecom/landing_cdr/incoming/",
  "schema_location": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/telecom/_schemas/cdr_stream_raw/",
  "file_pattern": "*.ber",
  "asn1_schema_path": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/telecom/schemas/gsm_cdr.asn",
  "asn1_codec": "ber",
  "asn1_pdu_name": "GsmCallDetailRecord",
  "capture_technical_metadata": true
}

Two distinct telecom-schema Volumes are provisioned by the seed notebook, deliberately named to avoid confusing one for the other:

  • {catalog}.telecom.schemas -- holds the real .asn module file itself (/Volumes/{catalog}/telecom/schemas/gsm_cdr.asn), per this test case's own spec.
  • {catalog}.telecom._schemas -- Auto Loader's cloudFiles.schemaLocation checkpoint state (schema_location), the same _schemas-named-Volume convention Excalibur_usecase._schemas already uses in scenario 002/003 -- not the same thing as the volume above, despite the similar name.

target_config is plain APPEND (a raw, append-only CDR event stream -- there is no natural update/merge key for an individual call record, unlike a dimension-style entity), so generate_hash_columns/primary_keys are omitted entirely (inert for APPEND regardless -- see 17_onboarding_template_reference.md §4.2).

dq_config.rules (all action: "quarantine", record_id_column: "imsi" since this schema has no dedicated recordId field the way telecom_cdr_v2.asn does):

rule_id expression dq_asn1_decode_ok _asn1_decode_error IS NULL dq_imsi_present imsi IS NOT NULL AND imsi <> '' dq_call_duration_non_negative callDurationSeconds IS NULL OR callDurationSeconds >= 0

(The IS NULL OR ... >= 0 form on the duration rule -- not just >= 0 -- is deliberate; see docs/13_asn1_dq_quarantine.md's identical callout on SQL three-valued logic for why a bare >= 0 would silently fail to flag a genuinely NULL value as a violation.)

docs.title: Main execution flow
docs.text:
databricks bundle deploy --target dev
databricks bundle run flowx_test_ing_004_asn1_decode_job --target dev

Task chain: setup_control_tables -> seed_asn1_gsm_cdr_fixture -> onboard_ing_004 -> run_ing_004_pipeline.

Runtime path (notebooks/03_engine/03_lakeflow_declarative_pipeline.py, read_asn1_source -> asn1/decoder.py::decode_asn1_binary_stream): Auto Loader's binaryFile-format cloudFiles reader lists the 3 .ber files from path -> derive_asn1_field_defs introspects gsm_cdr.asn once (via asn1tools.parse_files) to build the Spark output schema -> mapInPandas decodes each file's raw bytes against GsmCallDetailRecord, one partition at a time (the ASN.1 schema compiled once per partition, not once per row) -> the 3 quarantine rules are evaluated per row -> register_main_and_quarantine_tables splits clean rows into cdr_stream_raw, any DQ-rule failures into cdr_stream_raw_quarantine.

FROM {catalog}.bronze_telecom.cdr_stream_raw;
-- expect: 3 rows, imsi/callDurationSeconds NOT NULL on every row, _asn1_decode_error NULL on every row

SELECT count(*) AS decode_error_rows
FROM {catalog}.bronze_telecom.cdr_stream_raw

This pass's actual verification status: see flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md for whether this job was actually run against the live workspace and what the real result was -- per this project's scope discipline, deployment/execution across all 45 TC-* scenarios happens in a later, centralized pass, not from this build step.

docs.title: Design decisions
docs.text:
• A dedicated gsm_cdr.asn schema, not a reuse of telecom_cdr(_v2).asn. The two existing schemas already have their own dedicated demonstration (docs/13_asn1_dq_quarantine.md) exercising the decode-failure/DQ-violation path with a mixed-quality 5-file batch; reusing them here would blur which scenario is proving what. gsm_cdr.asn adds imei and roamingFlag (a BOOLEAN field, not otherwise exercised by the existing two schemas) and drops msisdn/regionCode/recordId, matching this test case's own field list exactly.
  • A literal double-hyphen inside a draft comment closed the ASN.1 comment early, live and reproducible. While drafting gsm_cdr.asn's own header comment (ironically, while writing the warning about this exact pitfall, already flagged once in telecom_cdr.asn's own comment), a ") -- a small GSM..." fragment's mid-line -- closed the comment right there, leaving a small GSM call-detail-record SEQUENCE as unparsed ASN.1 syntax -- pyparsing.exceptions.ParseSyntaxException: Expected Type, found 'small'. Caught by actually running asn1tools.compile_files(...) locally against the file before wiring it into a spec (see below), not by inspection.
  • All 3 fixtures are valid (unlike docs/13's deliberately mixed batch) because this scenario's own "Expected Output & Verification Logic" is specifically "decoded imsi/call_duration_sec populated, zero decode-error rows" -- a clean-decode assertion, not a quarantine-routing one. The decode-failure path is already real, tested code (docs/13_asn1_dq_quarantine.md's cdr_005.ber), so this scenario doesn't need to duplicate it.

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text: Asn1DecodeError if gsm_cdr.asn itself is malformed or asn1_pdu_name doesn't resolve to a SEQUENCE in it (validated once, onboarding-adjacent, via derive_asn1_field_defs); per-record decode failures are captured inline as _asn1_decode_error (never raised), so one malformed file wouldn't abort the batch -- not exercised by this scenario's own fixture set (see docs/13_asn1_dq_quarantine.md's cdr_005.ber for that path), but structurally covered by the dq_asn1_decode_ok rule regardless.

docs.title: Extension points
docs.text: Add a 4th CDR file (e.g. a deliberately malformed one, mirroring docs/13's cdr_005.ber) to notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/03_seed_asn1_gsm_cdr_fixture.py to additionally exercise the decode-failure/quarantine path against this same gsm_cdr.asn schema -- no spec change needed, the 3 quarantine rules already cover it.

docs.title: Real gaps / judgment calls made building this scenario
docs.text:
• No pre-existing ASN.1 fixture matched this test case's own field list (imsi/imei/callDurationSeconds/cellId/roamingFlag) -- the two schemas already in sample_data/asn1_schema/ (telecom_cdr.asn/telecom_cdr_v2.asn) are missing imei and roamingFlag and carry msisdn/regionCode instead, so a genuinely new .asn module and fixture set were built (verified via a real local asn1tools compile/encode/decode round-trip and the framework's own derive_asn1_field_defs, not just written by hand and assumed correct).
  • A brand-new seed notebook (notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/03_seed_asn1_gsm_cdr_fixture.py), rather than extending 02_seed_flowx_testing_data.py -- that notebook is explicitly scoped (per its own header) to specs 001/002/003, and this scenario's binary-fixture-generation-on-cluster requirement (see docs/13's identical rationale) is self-contained and unrelated to the EA/Excalibur fixtures it already provisions.
  • cdc_load_strategy: "APPEND", not a CDC-dispatched strategy -- a raw telecom CDR event stream has no natural per-call update/merge key, so SCD1/etc. would be a poor fit; this wasn't specified explicitly in the test case detail, a reasonable default for "streaming telecom CDR ingestion" was chosen instead.

docs.title: Test Pipeline: TC-ING-005 — Landing PGP Decryption via UC Secrets
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md (Module 1, TC-ING-005), flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md, 16_encryption_and_secrets.md (the full PGP/secrets design), 22_ingestion_pgp_zip_json_standardization.md (the source_zip_handling/pre_extraction_decryption mechanics this scenario exercises).

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Prove source_config.source_zip_handling.pre_extraction_decryption.type: "pgp" end to end, against a real PGP-encrypted-then-ZIPped archive, decrypted with a private key resolved from a genuine Unity Catalog secret at pipeline execution time — not merely a structural spec example (onboarding_templates/pipeline_onboarding_template.json's own pre_extraction_decryption example was never itself deployed; the closest prior live coverage, test_specs/spec_25_ingestion_pgp_zip_decrypt.json, ran against the poc catalog, not flowx). This scenario's realistic production framing: a finance partner drops a PGP-encrypted transactions extract into a landing volume; the framework must decrypt it with nothing more than a securely-stored private key, unzip the plaintext CSV, and land it in Bronze, with no decrypted intermediate ever persisted to permanent storage.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• One ingestion flow (df_finance_pgp_txns_ingest), source_type: "autoloader", cdc_load_strategy: "APPEND" — deliberately the simplest possible CDC strategy, since this scenario's whole point is the decrypt-then-unzip-then-ingest path, not CDC behavior.
  • source_zip_handling.pre_extraction_decryption dispatches the "pgp" handler (ingestion/readers.py::_apply_source_zip_handling → crypto/pgp.py::pgp_decrypt), keyed by private_key_secret — no passphrase_secret is configured, since this scenario's test-only keypair (like this project's other throwaway test keypairs) was deliberately generated without one.
  • delete_source_after_extract: false — deliberately, so the source financial_txns_202608.zip.pgp fixture survives a run and can be re-verified without re-seeding (the same choice spec_25's own PGP scenario made, for the same reason). This is orthogonal to the "no intermediate plaintext persisted" guarantee below: the decrypted .decrypted temp file is always removed in a finally block regardless of this flag —only the original encrypted source file's retention is configurable.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• flowx_testing/014_ing_005_pgp_decrypt.json — the onboarding spec (one ingestion flow, no transformation/reconciliation flows).
  • sample_data/flowx_testing/finance_usecase/txns_raw.csv — 5-row plaintext fixture (txn_id, account_id, amount, currency, txn_date, merchant), zipped and PGP-encrypted on-cluster by the seed step below.
  • sample_data/flowx_testing/finance_usecase/pgp_test_keypair_public.asc / pgp_test_keypair_private.asc — a dedicated, disposable, passphrase-less RSA-2048 PGP keypair generated specifically for this test scenario (via PGPy, the same library crypto/pgp.py wraps) and committed to the repo. Zero real security value — it protects nothing but this scenario's own synthetic fixture, and is never reused by any other test case in this repo.
  • notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/03_seed_pgp_decrypt_test_data.py — builds financial_txns_202608.zip.pgp in-memory (ZIP the CSV, then PGP-encrypt the ZIP's bytes via the framework's own crypto/pgp.py::pgp_encrypt) and lands it directly on-cluster, the same "build the archive in-process rather than sync a pre-built binary through the bundle" approach 02_seed_flowx_testing_data.py already established (workspace-bundle sync can mangle a pre-built .zip/binary upload).

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• {catalog}.bronze_finance.txns_raw — 5 rows, in plaintext, exactly matching txns_raw.csv's content, plus the usual __framework_* technical metadata columns.
  • /Volumes/{catalog}/finance/landing_pgp/extracted/txns/ — the decrypted, unzipped txns_raw.csv, landed there by extract_encrypted_zip before Auto Loader reads it.
  • /Volumes/{catalog}/finance/landing_pgp/incoming/financial_txns_202608.zip.pgp — still present after a run (delete_source_after_extract: false, see above).
  • No .decrypted intermediate file anywhere on the Volume — _apply_source_zip_handling always removes it in a finally block, success or failure, regardless of delete_source_after_extract (see 22_ingestion_pgp_zip_json_standardization.md §1.1).

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
flowx_testing/014_ing_005_pgp_decrypt.json's one ingestion flow:

"source_zip_handling": {
  "enabled": true,
  "source_zip_path": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/finance/landing_pgp/incoming/",
  "zip_file_pattern": "financial_txns_202608.zip.pgp",
  "target_volume_path": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/finance/landing_pgp/extracted/txns/",
  "pre_extraction_decryption": {
    "type": "pgp",
    "private_key_secret": {
      "secret_catalog": "{{catalog}}",
      "secret_schema": "security",
      "secret_key": "pgp_private_key_finance_test"
    }
  },
  "delete_source_after_extract": false
}

docs.title: Required prerequisite: provision the private key as a UC secret
docs.text:
Manual, admin-audited step — not automated by this framework, following the exact same security-scope pattern 05_deployment_guide.md's own prerequisites section already establishes for this project's other encryption keys (pii_encryption_key, cdr_zip_passphrase, egress_zip_password). This step must run before flowx_test_ing_005_pgp_decrypt_job's run_pipeline_task — the pipeline's pre_extraction_decryption step will fail with SecretResolutionError until it does:

# Test-only, disposable PGP private key -- protects nothing real (see sample_data/
# flowx_testing/finance_usecase/ header note). No passphrase, matching this project's
# other throwaway test keypairs.
databricks secrets put-secret security pgp_private_key_finance_test \
  --string-value "$(cat sample_data/flowx_testing/finance_usecase/pgp_test_keypair_private.asc)"

The matching public key (pgp_test_keypair_public.asc) needs no secret at all — it's used directly, in the clear, by the seed notebook to encrypt the fixture; only the private key half needs to live behind a UC secret.

docs.title: Main execution flow
docs.text:
databricks bundle deploy --target dev
databricks secrets put-secret security pgp_private_key_finance_test \
  --string-value "$(cat sample_data/flowx_testing/finance_usecase/pgp_test_keypair_private.asc)"
databricks bundle run flowx_test_ing_005_pgp_decrypt_job --target dev

Task chain: setup_control_tables → seed_pgp_decrypt_test_data → onboard_ing_005 → run_pipeline_task.

docs.title: Expected results — verification logic
docs.text:
-- Exactly 5 plaintext rows, matching txns_raw.csv's known content
SELECT txn_id, account_id, amount, currency, txn_date, merchant
FROM {catalog}.bronze_finance.txns_raw
ORDER BY txn_id;
-- expect: FTX-1001..FTX-1005, e.g. FTX-1003 -> ACC-4003, 300.00, EUR, 2026-08-22, Fabrikam Logistics

# Extracted plaintext CSV landed where source_zip_handling.target_volume_path points
databricks fs ls dbfs:/Volumes/{catalog}/finance/landing_pgp/extracted/txns/

# Source PGP+ZIP archive still present (delete_source_after_extract: false)
databricks fs ls dbfs:/Volumes/{catalog}/finance/landing_pgp/incoming/
# expect: financial_txns_202608.zip.pgp

# No lingering *.decrypted intermediate anywhere under landing_pgp/
databricks fs ls -r dbfs:/Volumes/{catalog}/finance/landing_pgp/ | grep decrypted
# expect: no output

If pre_extraction_decryption's secret hasn't been provisioned yet, or is wrong, the pipeline update fails fast with a CryptoError/SecretResolutionError naming the secret coordinates — this is the expected, correct failure mode, not a bug to route around; it proves the framework never silently falls through to treating an undecryptable file as a plain ZIP.

This pass's actual verification status: see flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md for whether this job was actually run against the live workspace and what the real result was — this document describes what should happen structurally; the status tracker records what did happen.

docs.title: Known gaps / judgment calls
docs.text:
• Scope-vs-catalog terminology: this doc's databricks secrets put-secret security pgp_private_key_finance_test command follows 05_deployment_guide.md's own prerequisites-section CLI pattern exactly (as this test case's own instructions required), which that guide itself labels a classic workspace-level secret scope command. The onboarding spec instead addresses this secret via the Unity Catalog three-level {secret_catalog, secret_schema, secret_key} shape ({{catalog}}, security, pgp_private_key_finance_test), resolved via dbutils.secrets.get(catalog=, schema=, key=) — a different, newer secret system per 16_encryption_and_secrets.md §1. This is a pre-existing terminology gap in this project's own docs (the identical pattern already exists for pii_encryption_key/cdr_zip_passphrase/egress_zip_password in 05_deployment_guide.md, and docs/20_crypto_abac_exhaustive_test_suite.md explicitly maps put-secret security pii_encryption_key to {secret_catalog, secret_schema, secret_key} = {catalog, security, pii_encryption_key}) — not something introduced or newly resolved by this test case. Follow whichever secrets CLI syntax your workspace/CLI version actually requires to create a Unity Catalog secret at {{catalog}}.security.pgp_private_key_finance_test; the important, framework-relevant part is the resulting secret coordinates, not the exact provisioning command's flag syntax.
  • Fixture generation approach: per this test case's own instructions, the PGP-encrypted ZIP fixture is generated by a new seed notebook step (notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/03_seed_pgp_decrypt_test_data.py), not a one-off local script whose binary output gets committed — consistent with this repo's established aversion to syncing pre-built binary/ZIP artifacts through the bundle (see 05_deployment_guide.md's ASN.1 section). A one-off local script (using crypto/pgp.py directly, matching this test case's own suggested approach) was used, once, to generate the disposable test keypair itself and to verify the full PGP-decrypt-then-unzip round trip locally before writing any of these artifacts. The keypair's own PGP User ID identifies it as disposable test-only material ("FlowX TC-ING-005 Test Key (finance, disposable, no passphrase)", visible via gpg --list-packets or any PGP key inspector) -- not a plaintext comment in the .asc file itself, which is otherwise a standard OpenPGP armored block with no room for free-text annotation.

docs.title: Test Pipeline: TC-ING-006 -- Nested JSON Struct Flattening (explode_columns)
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md (Module 1, TC-ING-006), flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Prove source_config.explode_columns (Auto Loader / source_type: "autoloader", format: "json") correctly flattens a nested JSON array-of-structs column into discrete top-level columns, one row per array element -- see 01_control_metadata_schema.md §3 and ingestion/json_flattening.py.

This session added a new auto_flatten_all flag that changes explode_columns's default behavior: an empty/absent explode_columns is now a schema-preserving pass-through (no implicit flattening) unless auto_flatten_all: true is also set. This scenario deliberately sets explode_columns explicitly to ["metrics"] rather than relying on any default, to prove the named-column-scoped explode path specifically -- not the auto_flatten_all "flatten everything" path (which is out of scope for this test case).

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Land 2 nested JSON device-telemetry records into a dedicated iot landing Volume -- each record carries a metrics array of 2 {sensor, val} elements, e.g.: 
    {"device_id": "D1", "device_type": "env_sensor", "event_ts": "2026-08-28T09:00:00Z", "metrics": [{"sensor": "temp", "val": 22.5}, {"sensor": "pressure", "val": 101.3}]}
  • Onboard one ingestion flow with source_config.explode_columns: ["metrics"] and target_config.cdc_load_strategy: "APPEND" (immutable telemetry facts -- no dedup/history needed), targeting {catalog}.bronze_iot.sensor_telemetry_flat.
  • apply_explode_columns (ingestion/json_flattening.py) explodes the metrics array<struct<sensor, val>> column (explode_outer, one row per element) and immediately flattens the resulting struct element in the same pass, producing metrics_sensor and metrics_val as discrete top-level columns -- exactly the behavior tests/unit/test_json_flattening.py::test_populated_explode_columns_on_array_of_struct_fully_denests_in_one_entry already unit-tests.
  • Needs no dedicated seed fixture reuse -- no existing seeded table/volume carries a nested JSON struct/array shape, so this scenario seeds its own small dedicated fixture rather than repurposing scenario 001/002/003/100's flat CSV/Zerobus fixtures.

docs.title: Test Pipeline: TC-ING-007 -- Inline Data Standardization SQL
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md (Module 1, TC-ING-007), flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Prove source_config.data_standardization_sql (Auto Loader / source_type: "autoloader", format: "csv") applies simple per-column normalization -- trimming whitespace and fixing casing -- to specific columns at ingest time, before the row ever reaches the Bronze table -- see 01_control_metadata_schema.md §3 and 22_ingestion_pgp_zip_json_standardization.md §5 for the full grammar and its rationale.

This scenario deliberately uses only the restricted column-expression grammar the framework enforces (ingestion/standardization_sql.py / onboarding/spec_validator.py::_validate_data_standardization_sql): each entry is exactly one column expression ending in an explicit AS <column_name> clause, applied via withColumn(alias, F.expr(expression)) -- not a full SELECT statement. A value containing a bare SELECT/FROM/JOIN/UNION/WHERE/any DDL/DML keyword, or a ;, is rejected outright at onboarding time.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Land 3 dirty company records into a dedicated master landing Volume -- each carries a region and email value with extra leading/trailing whitespace and/or inconsistent casing, e.g.: 
    company_id,company_name,region,email,updated_at
CO001,Acme Corp LLC,"  us-east  "," invalid-email@test.com  ",2026-08-28T09:00:00
  • Onboard one ingestion flow with two data_standardization_sql entries -- "TRIM(UPPER(region)) AS region" and "LOWER(TRIM(email)) AS email" -- and target_config.cdc_load_strategy: "APPEND" (plain append, no dedup/history needed for this reference feed), targeting {catalog}.bronze_master.companies_standardized.
  • apply_data_standardization_sql (ingestion/standardization_sql.py) applies each expression in order, one withColumn at a time, overwriting the existing region/email columns in place -- exactly the behavior tests/unit/test_standardization_sql.py::test_multiple_expressions_applied_in_order already unit-tests.
  • Needs no dedicated seed fixture reuse -- no existing seeded table/volume carries this dirty-string-normalization shape, so this scenario seeds its own small dedicated fixture rather than repurposing another scenario's CSV fixtures.

docs.text:
• flowx_testing/016_ing_007_standardize.json -- ingestion-only onboarding spec (no transformation_flows/reconciliation_flows), one flow: df_ing_007_standardize.
  • sample_data/flowx_testing/master_usecase/companies_batch1.csv -- 3 company records (CO001, CO002, CO003), each with a differently-dirty region/email value (padded whitespace, upper-case, or both) so the standardization expressions are proven across more than one input shape, not just the one literal example in the test-case brief.
  • notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/03_seed_ing_007_standardize_data.py -- provisions {catalog}.master / {catalog}.bronze_master schemas and {catalog}.master.landing_companies / {catalog}.master._schemas volumes, then lands the fixture file at /Volumes/{catalog}/master/landing_companies/companies_batch1.csv.

No quarantine table (dq_config.rules is an empty list).

-- The test-case brief's literal example row: whitespace trimmed, region upper-cased,

SELECT region, email FROM {catalog}.bronze_master.companies_standardized WHERE company_id = 'CO001';
-- expect: region = 'US-EAST', email = 'invalid-email@test.com'

-- Every row's region/email is standardized the same way, regardless of input casing/padding
SELECT company_id, region, email FROM {catalog}.bronze_master.companies_standardized ORDER BY company_id;
-- expect:
--   CO001 | US-EAST  | invalid-email@test.com
--   CO002 | EU-WEST  | contact@globex.com
--   CO003 | AP-SOUTH | support@northwind.example

-- The count from the test-case brief's own assertion form: every row satisfies the
-- standardized CO001 pattern's *shape* (no residual leading/trailing whitespace, region
-- fully upper-case, email fully lower-case) -- confirmed per-row above rather than via a
-- single aggregate, since only CO001 shares the brief's exact literal values.
SELECT count(*) FROM {catalog}.bronze_master.companies_standardized
WHERE region = trim(upper(region)) AND email = lower(trim(email));
-- expect: 3 (equals total row count -- no row was left un-standardized)

-- company_name (not a standardized column) still carries its original padding untouched
SELECT company_id, company_name FROM {catalog}.bronze_master.companies_standardized WHERE company_id = 'CO003';
-- expect: company_name = '  Northwind Traders  ' (unchanged)

docs.title: Test Pipeline: TC-ING-008 -- Technical Metadata Enrichment & Column Ordering
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md (Module 1, TC-ING-008), flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Prove that the framework's technical-metadata enrichment (source_config.capture_technical_metadata, defaulting true -- ingestion/technical_metadata.py) lands the correct, current set of __framework_* columns on a plain CSV Auto Loader ingestion, and that business columns always occupy the leading positions of the target table's schema -- never pushed behind the framework's own generated columns.

Doc-drift note (read this before trusting any other document's column list): this session confirmed flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md's own narrative for this test case names 7 columns (_rescued_data plus 6 __framework_* names) and its header claims "8". Neither number matches the real code. The two source-of-truth functions actually wired into the ingestion path (notebooks/03_engine/03_lakeflow_declarative_pipeline.py::_build_ingestion_dataframe and engine/flow_registration.py::register_staged_view) are:

  • ingestion/technical_metadata.py -- attach_technical_metadata (4 columns) + attach_framework_ingestion_timestamp (1 column).
  • dq/quarantine.py -- add_quarantine_columns, which runs unconditionally on every flow (not only when dq_config.rules is non-empty) and always attaches 5 more columns.

That's 10 real __framework_* columns, plus the native (not __framework_-prefixed) Auto Loader _rescued_data column -- see Configuration below for the exact list and order.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Land a plain (non-ZIP) CSV file into a dedicated ea/bronze_ea landing Volume.
  • One ingestion_flow (df_ing_008_dept_tech_metadata_ingest) with source_type: "autoloader", format: "csv", and capture_technical_metadata: true -- explicitly set, even though it only reasserts the function's own default, so the spec self-documents the behavior under test.
  • cdc_load_strategy: "APPEND", no primary_keys/liquid_clustering_columns -- this scenario is about column presence/ordering, not CDC or Delta-stats behavior, so storage/column_ordering.py::reorder_columns_for_delta_stats is a deliberate no-op here: with no primary_keys/liquid_clustering_columns and no surrogate/hash columns generated, its front-priority list matches nothing on this DataFrame, so it returns the DataFrame unchanged -- the append-order column sequence from the read is exactly what lands in the target table.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• flowx_testing/017_ing_008_tech_metadata.json -- single-ingestion-flow onboarding spec (no transformation_flows/reconciliation_flows).
  • sample_data/flowx_testing/ea_usecase/departments.csv (4 rows: dept_id, dept_name, region) -- reused as-is from scenario 001 rather than a new fixture (see Build notes).
  • notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/03_seed_ing_008_tech_metadata_data.py -- a new, dedicated seed notebook that provisions {{catalog}}.ea / {{catalog}}.bronze_ea schemas and the ea.landing_csv / ea._schemas Volumes (distinct from scenario 001's own EA_usecase/landing_zip Volume family), then copies the CSV fixture directly (no ZIP step) into /Volumes/{{catalog}}/ea/landing_csv/.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• {{catalog}}.bronze_ea.departments_tech_metadata_raw -- 4 rows, with columns in this exact order:
# Column Origin 1 dept_id source CSV 2 dept_name source CSV 3 region source CSV 4 _rescued_data native Auto Loader column (always added for a structured format) 5 __framework_source_file_name attach_technical_metadata 6 __framework_source_file_size attach_technical_metadata 7 __framework_source_file_modification_time attach_technical_metadata 8 __framework_source_file_metadata_headers attach_technical_metadata 9 __framework_ingestion_timestamp_utc attach_framework_ingestion_timestamp 10 __framework_dq_failed_rule_ids add_quarantine_columns (always runs) 11 __framework_dq_failure_reasons add_quarantine_columns 12 __framework_dq_quarantine_flag add_quarantine_columns (always false -- no quarantine rules configured) 13 __framework_pipeline_run_id add_quarantine_columns 14 __framework_record_id add_quarantine_columns (always NULL -- no dq_config.record_id_column configured)

All 3 business columns occupy indices 0–2; every _rescued_data/__framework_* column is trailing, at indices 3–13.

docs.title: Expected results -- simulation notes
docs.text:
Row count (after a run, replace {catalog} with your actual target catalog):

SELECT count(*) FROM {catalog}.bronze_ea.departments_tech_metadata_raw;
-- expect: 4

Schema-order assertion -- the core claim of this test case. ordinal_position in information_schema.columns reflects the table's actual physical column order:

SELECT column_name, ordinal_position
FROM {catalog}.information_schema.columns
WHERE table_catalog = '{catalog}'
  AND table_schema = 'bronze_ea'
  AND table_name = 'departments_tech_metadata_raw'
ORDER BY ordinal_position;
-- expect, in this exact order:
--  0 dept_id
--  1 dept_name
--  2 region
--  3 _rescued_data
--  4 __framework_source_file_name
--  5 __framework_source_file_size
--  6 __framework_source_file_modification_time
--  7 __framework_source_file_metadata_headers
--  8 __framework_ingestion_timestamp_utc
--  9 __framework_dq_failed_rule_ids
-- 10 __framework_dq_failure_reasons
-- 11 __framework_dq_quarantine_flag
-- 12 __framework_pipeline_run_id
-- 13 __framework_record_id

-- Equivalent single-boolean assertion: every business column's ordinal_position must be
-- strictly less than every _rescued_data/__framework_* column's ordinal_position.
SELECT
  max(CASE WHEN column_name IN ('dept_id', 'dept_name', 'region') THEN ordinal_position END)
    < min(CASE WHEN column_name = '_rescued_data' OR column_name LIKE '\_\_framework\_%' THEN ordinal_position END)
  AS business_columns_precede_technical_columns
FROM {catalog}.information_schema.columns
WHERE table_catalog = '{catalog}' AND table_schema = 'bronze_ea'
  AND table_name = 'departments_tech_metadata_raw';
-- expect: true

Column-population assertion -- technical metadata columns must actually be populated (non-null), not merely present:

SELECT
  count(*) AS total_rows,
  count(__framework_source_file_name) AS non_null_file_name,
  count(__framework_source_file_size) AS non_null_file_size,
  count(__framework_source_file_modification_time) AS non_null_file_mod_time,
  count(__framework_ingestion_timestamp_utc) AS non_null_ingestion_ts,
  count(_rescued_data) AS non_null_rescued_data
FROM {catalog}.bronze_ea.departments_tech_metadata_raw;
-- expect: total_rows = 4, all four __framework_* counts = 4;
-- non_null_rescued_data = 0 (all 4 rows have a clean 3-column match, nothing to rescue)
