docs.title: Build notes / judgment calls
docs.text:
• Target table renamed to avoid a real collision. Both this test case's own brief and TESTING_PLAN.md name the target table {{catalog}}.bronze_ea.departments_raw -- but that exact three-part name is already the real, live target of scenario 001's df_ea_departments_ingest flow (flowx_testing/001_zip_file_onboarding.json, resources/flowx_test_001_zip_join_export_pipeline.yml). Two independent Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines cannot both own/materialize a streaming table under the identical catalog.schema.table name -- whichever job ran second would fail against the other pipeline's already-existing table ownership. Rather than silently letting that collision surface later (in the centralized deploy/run phase, across 45 test cases at once), this build uses departments_tech_metadata_raw instead, keeping the same bronze_ea schema and the same underlying EA department reference data semantics. This is a genuine, deliberate deviation from the literal brief -- flagged here rather than silently building something that would break scenario 001 (or itself) when actually run.
  • Reused fixture, not a new one. sample_data/flowx_testing/ea_usecase/departments.csv already carries dept_id/dept_name (plus one extra region business column) across 4 rows -- it was reused as-is per this project's "reuse before inventing new sample data" convention, landed as a plain CSV rather than scenario 001's ZIP-wrapped copy of the same file. The extra region column doesn't weaken the schema-order assertion (if anything, it strengthens it: 3 business columns must precede the technical ones, not just 2). source_zip_handling is intentionally absent from this flow's source_config -- unlike scenario 001, this file lands unzipped.
  • No run_observability_task. TESTING_PLAN.md's own "Proposed Pipeline & Job Architecture" column names a second run_observability_task step, but per TESTING_STATUS.md's framing and the precedent already set by docs/31_tc_ing_001.md's own build notes, TESTING_PLAN.md is a planned/aspirational matrix, not a literal build spec -- observability is opt-in (a spec's own observability[] array plus a separate job, as scenario 100's does), not part of the default setup_control_tables -> seed -> onboard -> run_pipeline chain every other real scenario in this repo follows.

docs.title: Test Pipeline: Schema Evolution & Malformed Column Rescue (TC-ING-009)
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md (Module 1, TC-ING-009), flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Prove that source_config.schema_evolution_mode: "rescue" (Auto Loader's cloudFiles.schemaEvolutionMode, see ingestion/readers.py::read_autoloader_source) genuinely protects a streaming ingestion flow against two distinct drift shapes arriving in the same day-2 batch, without failing the stream and without silently dropping data:

  1. An unannounced new column (unannounced_flag) that was never part of the schema Auto Loader inferred from the day-1 batch.
  2. A malformed value in an already-typed column -- one day-2 row's id is the non-numeric string "ABC", where every day-1 row's id inferred as an integer.

In "rescue" mode, Auto Loader never widens the schema or fails the micro-batch for either case: instead, both the extra column's value and the unparseable typed value are captured as JSON into the framework's _rescued_data column for the affected row(s), leaving every other column's value on that row intact. This is a different tradeoff from "addNewColumns" (would evolve the schema and restart the stream) or "failOnNewColumns" (would hard-fail the micro-batch) -- see 01_control_metadata_schema.md §3 and 17_onboarding_template_reference.md §2.2 for the full schema_evolution_mode enum.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• One ingestion_flow (df_ing_009_rescue_schema_ingest), source_type: "autoloader", reading CSV from /Volumes/{{catalog}}/ops/landing_drift/ with schema_evolution_mode: "rescue" and reader_options: {"header": "true", "cloudFiles.inferColumnTypes": "true"} (so id infers as INT from the day-1 batch, making day-2's "ABC" a genuine type mismatch rather than a same-type string value).
  • cdc_load_strategy: "APPEND" -- this scenario is about schema/type drift capture, not CDC behavior, so the simplest load strategy keeps the flow focused on the one thing under test.
  • Land day-1 (feed_day1.csv, columns id, name, 3 clean rows) first and run the pipeline once, establishing the inferred schema at schema_location. Then land day-2 (feed_day2.csv, columns id, name, unannounced_flag, 3 rows -- one with a non-numeric id) and re-run the pipeline: every day-2 row should land with _rescued_data IS NOT NULL (from the unannounced column alone), and the one malformed-id row should additionally show id IS NULL for that row (its value went to _rescued_data instead, since "ABC" cannot cast to INT).

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• flowx_testing/018_ing_009_rescue_schema.json -- single-ingestion-flow onboarding spec (no transformation_flows/reconciliation_flows).
  • sample_data/flowx_testing/ops_usecase/feed_day1.csv -- day-1 batch, id, name, 3 rows (1,Alice / 2,Bob / 3,Carol).
  • sample_data/flowx_testing/ops_usecase/feed_day2.csv -- day-2 batch, id, name, unannounced_flag, 3 rows (4,Dave,Y / 5,Eve,N / ABC,Frank,Y) -- the third row's id is the non-numeric string "ABC".
  • notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/03_seed_ing_009_rescue_schema_data.py -- a new, dedicated seed notebook (kept separate from every other scenario's seed step) that provisions the ops/bronze_ops schemas and landing_drift/_schemas Volumes, then lands only feed_day1.csv. It deliberately does not land feed_day2.csv -- see "Triggering day-2 schema drift" below.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• {{catalog}}.bronze_ops.feed_rescued_raw -- after the day-1-only run: 3 rows (id 1/2/3), _rescued_data NULL for all of them (clean batch, nothing to rescue).
  • After day-2 lands and the pipeline re-runs: 3 more rows land (6 total). All 3 new rows have _rescued_data IS NOT NULL (each carries the unannounced_flag value Auto Loader couldn't place on the inferred schema). The Frank row additionally has id IS NULL (its literal "ABC" is inside _rescued_data instead, not silently coerced or dropped).
  • No pipeline failure, no quarantine table (no dq_config.rules configured) -- "rescue" mode's entire point is to keep the stream running through both drift shapes.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
flowx_testing/018_ing_009_rescue_schema.json's one ingestion_flows[] entry:

"source_config": {
  "path": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/ops/landing_drift/",
  "format": "csv",
  "schema_location": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/ops/_schemas/feed_rescued_raw/",
  "schema_evolution_mode": "rescue",
  "reader_options": {"header": "true", "cloudFiles.inferColumnTypes": "true"},
  "capture_technical_metadata": true
}

target_config: {"cdc_load_strategy": "APPEND", "storage_format": "delta"} -- plain streaming table, no primary keys.

Resources:

  • resources/flowx_test_ing_009_rescue_schema_pipeline.yml -- flowx_test_ing_009_rescue_schema_pipeline (catalog: flowx, schema: bronze_ops, serverless, dataflow.group.id: dfg_ing_009_rescue_schema).
  • resources/flowx_test_ing_009_rescue_schema_job.yml -- flowx_test_ing_009_rescue_schema_job.

docs.title: Main execution flow
docs.text:
databricks bundle deploy --target dev
databricks bundle run flowx_test_ing_009_rescue_schema_job --target dev

Task chain: setup_control_tables -> seed_ing_009_rescue_schema_data -> onboard_ing_009 -> run_ing_009_pipeline. This job run lands and ingests day-1 only (feed_day1.csv), which establishes Auto Loader's inferred schema (id: INT, name: STRING) at schema_location.

docs.title: Triggering day-2 schema drift
docs.text:
Day-2 is deliberately not part of the automated task chain -- it must be dropped in manually, after day-1 has already been onboarded and run once, so Auto Loader's schema is already committed to schema_location before the drifted batch arrives (the same day-1-then-day-2 convention 08_test_pipeline_1_volume_scd.md uses for its own SCD drift test):

# 1. Copy the day-2 fixture into the same landing Volume day-1 already landed in:
databricks fs cp sample_data/flowx_testing/ops_usecase/feed_day2.csv \
  dbfs:/Volumes/flowx/ops/landing_drift/feed_day2.csv --profile dev

# 2. Re-run just the pipeline (Auto Loader picks up the new file on the next update;
#    no need to re-run setup/seed/onboard):
databricks bundle run flowx_test_ing_009_rescue_schema_pipeline --target dev

(Equivalently, from a notebook attached to the same workspace: dbutils.fs.cp("file:...", "/Volumes/flowx/ops/landing_drift/feed_day2.csv").)

docs.title: Expected results -- simulation notes
docs.text:
SQL assertions (after the day-1-only run, replace {catalog} with your actual target catalog):

SELECT count(*) AS row_count, count(_rescued_data) AS rescued_count
FROM {catalog}.bronze_ops.feed_rescued_raw;
-- expect: row_count=3, rescued_count=0

After day-2 lands and the pipeline re-runs:

SELECT count(*) FROM {catalog}.bronze_ops.feed_rescued_raw;
-- expect: 6 (3 day-1 + 3 day-2)

-- Every day-2 row should have been rescued (unannounced_flag alone triggers this)
SELECT id, name, _rescued_data
FROM {catalog}.bronze_ops.feed_rescued_raw
WHERE name IN ('Dave', 'Eve', 'Frank')
ORDER BY name;
-- expect: _rescued_data IS NOT NULL for all 3 rows (contains "unannounced_flag" in the JSON)

-- The malformed-id row specifically: id itself must be NULL, not "ABC" or a cast error
SELECT id, name, _rescued_data
FROM {catalog}.bronze_ops.feed_rescued_raw
WHERE name = 'Frank';
-- expect: id IS NULL; _rescued_data contains both "id":"ABC" and "unannounced_flag":"Y"

-- Day-1 rows remain completely unaffected by the later drift
SELECT id, name, _rescued_data
FROM {catalog}.bronze_ops.feed_rescued_raw
WHERE name IN ('Alice', 'Bob', 'Carol');
-- expect: _rescued_data IS NULL for all 3, id populated (1, 2, 3)

(Per this project's build convention, that tracker is updated centrally in a later phase, not by this build itself.)

docs.title: Build notes / judgment calls
docs.text:
• New fixtures, not a reuse. No existing seeded fixture combines an unannounced new column with a malformed value in an already-typed column in the same drift batch, so 2 new small CSV fixtures and 1 new dedicated seed notebook were added, following the same "separate seed notebook per new test case" convention 03_seed_ing_006_json_explode_data.py and 03_seed_ing_001_zip_filter_data.py already established.
  • Day-2 landing is a manual, documented step, not a job task. This mirrors the existing 08_test_pipeline_1_volume_scd.md convention (its own day-2 CSV is "dropped in" manually between two bundle run invocations, not automated inside the job) rather than inventing a new pattern -- the point of this test case is the schema-evolution behavior on a second, independent Auto Loader trigger, which a single job run landing both files at once would not exercise cleanly (Auto Loader could plausibly infer the union schema from one combined initial batch instead of genuinely evolving mid-stream).
  • One row deliberately breaks the inferred type, not the column set. The task's own wording ("a non-numeric value in a typed column") is satisfied by id specifically, since cloudFiles.inferColumnTypes: "true" + a clean all-integer day-1 batch is what makes id a genuinely typed (INT) column in the first place -- a non-numeric value in an already-STRING column (e.g. name) would never be "malformed," just a normal string.

docs.title: Test Pipeline: Streaming Append-Only Fact Loading (TC-CDC-001)
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md (Module 2, TC-CDC-001), flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md, 02_cdc_load_strategies.md § APPEND.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Prove that target_config.cdc_load_strategy: "APPEND" genuinely appends every row from every landed micro-batch verbatim into the Bronze streaming table -- with no deduplication, no primary_keys/apply_changes dispatch, no __framework_hash_key/__framework_hash_value columns, and no history tracking of any kind. The one thing this scenario is specifically designed to catch: two (or more) rows that share an identical (user_id, event_timestamp) pair must both land in the target table, not be silently collapsed to one -- which is exactly what would happen if APPEND were ever mistakenly routed through CDC dispatch (e.g. an accidental primary_keys inference) instead of engine/flow_registration.py's plain streaming no-op path.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Land 2 clickstream CSV batches in the same incoming Volume so Auto Loader's one triggered (availableNow) pipeline update processes both as separate micro-batches in a single run:
  • page_clicks_batch1.csv -- 8 rows, including one intentional duplicate (user_id, event_timestamp) pair (CLK00005/CLK00006, both U1002 @ 2026-08-28T10:16:40Z).
  • page_clicks_batch2.csv -- 6 rows, including a second intentional duplicate pair within the batch (CLK00009/CLK00010, both U1005 @ 2026-08-28T10:20:00Z) and a third row (CLK00012) that repeats batch 1's (U1002, 2026-08-28T10:16:40Z) key again -- proving APPEND never deduplicates across files/micro-batches either, not just within one.
  • One ingestion_flow (df_cdc_001_page_clicks_ingest) with source_type: "autoloader", plain CSV format, no source_zip_handling (out of scope for this scenario -- TC-ING-001/002 already cover ZIP selection/retention).
  • cdc_load_strategy: "APPEND", no primary_keys, no columns_to_check/columns_to_exclude -- the simplest possible load strategy, keeping the flow focused on the one thing under test.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• flowx_testing/019_cdc_001_append.json -- single-ingestion-flow onboarding spec (no transformation_flows/reconciliation_flows).
  • sample_data/flowx_testing/web_usecase/page_clicks_batch1.csv (8 rows) / page_clicks_batch2.csv (6 rows) -- 14 rows total, hand-authored (no generator script needed for a fixture this small).
  • notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/03_seed_cdc_001_append_data.py -- a new, dedicated seed notebook (kept separate from 02_seed_flowx_testing_data.py, which belongs to scenarios 001/002/003) that provisions the web/bronze_web schemas and landing_clicks/_schemas Volumes, then copies both CSV fixtures straight into /Volumes/{{catalog}}/web/landing_clicks/incoming/ -- no ZIP handling needed here, since plain Auto Loader CSV ingestion is this scenario's own focus.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• {{catalog}}.bronze_web.page_clicks_stream -- exactly 14 rows, one per input CSV row across both batches, with every click_id present and no row collapsed or merged.
  • The 3 rows sharing key (U1002, 2026-08-28T10:16:40Z) (CLK00005, CLK00006, CLK00012) all present simultaneously; same for the 2 rows sharing (U1005, 2026-08-28T10:20:00Z) (CLK00009, CLK00010).
  • No __framework_hash_key/__framework_hash_value columns on the target (APPEND is not CDC-dispatched, so dq/quarantine.py::_apply_hash_and_surrogate_key_columns never adds them regardless of generate_hash_columns's default).

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
flowx_testing/019_cdc_001_append.json's one ingestion_flows[] entry:

"source_config": {
  "path": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/web/landing_clicks/incoming/",
  "format": "csv",
  "schema_location": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/web/_schemas/page_clicks_stream/",
  "reader_options": {"header": "true", "cloudFiles.inferColumnTypes": "true"},
  "capture_technical_metadata": true
},
"target_config": {"cdc_load_strategy": "APPEND", "storage_format": "delta"},
"dq_config": {"rules": []}

Target: {{catalog}}.bronze_web.page_clicks_stream, target_type: "streaming_table".

docs.title: Main execution flow
docs.text:
databricks bundle deploy --target dev
databricks bundle run flowx_test_cdc_001_append_job --target dev

Task chain: setup_control_tables -> seed_cdc_001_append_data -> onboard_cdc_001 -> run_pipeline.

docs.title: Expected results — simulation notes
docs.text:
SQL assertions (after a run, replace {catalog} with your actual target catalog):

-- Total row count: 14 (8 + 6), verbatim, no dedup
SELECT count(*) FROM {catalog}.bronze_web.page_clicks_stream;
-- expect: 14

-- The 3-way duplicate key: all 3 click_ids present
SELECT click_id FROM {catalog}.bronze_web.page_clicks_stream
WHERE user_id = 'U1002' AND event_timestamp = '2026-08-28T10:16:40Z'
ORDER BY click_id;
-- expect: CLK00005, CLK00006, CLK00012 (3 rows)

-- The within-batch duplicate key: both click_ids present
SELECT count(*) FROM {catalog}.bronze_web.page_clicks_stream
WHERE user_id = 'U1005' AND event_timestamp = '2026-08-28T10:20:00Z';
-- expect: 2

-- No CDC hash columns were added (APPEND is never CDC-dispatched)
DESCRIBE {catalog}.bronze_web.page_clicks_stream;
-- expect: no __framework_hash_key / __framework_hash_value columns present

docs.title: Test Pipeline: Full Materialized View Snapshot (TC-CDC-002)
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md (Module 2, TC-CDC-002), flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md, 02_cdc_load_strategies.md § TRUNCATE_AND_LOAD.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Prove that target_config.cdc_load_strategy: "TRUNCATE_AND_LOAD" on a target_type: "materialized_view" transformation flow genuinely fully recomputes its target from its source on every pipeline update -- rather than incrementally appending -- so a small reference dimension (daily FX currency rates) always reflects exactly the current source content, with no stale/superseded rows ever accumulating no matter how many times the pipeline is triggered. This is the direct structural contrast with APPEND (TC-CDC-001): a materialized view is a full recompute, so re-running the same pipeline update against unchanged source data must leave the target's row count completely unchanged, never growing.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Land one 50-row FX rate CSV extract (one row per distinct ISO currency code, all dated the same rate_date) in a landing Volume so Auto Loader's one triggered (availableNow) pipeline update ingests all 50 rows into Bronze in a single micro-batch.
  • One ingestion_flow (df_cdc_002_fx_rates_ingest) with source_type: "autoloader", plain CSV format, cdc_load_strategy: "APPEND" -- a plain Bronze landing table, no ZIP handling, no CDC dispatch (out of scope for this scenario; the strategy under test lives entirely in the downstream transformation flow).
  • One transformation_flow (ts_cdc_002_fx_rates_truncate_load) reading that Bronze table as a batch source_inputs view and writing target_type: "materialized_view" with cdc_load_strategy: "TRUNCATE_AND_LOAD" -- the flow under test.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• flowx_testing/020_cdc_002_truncate.json -- one ingestion flow + one transformation flow, no reconciliation_flows.
  • sample_data/flowx_testing/ref_usecase/fx_rates_batch1.csv -- 50 rows, hand-authored (no generator script needed for a fixture this small): 50 distinct real ISO 4217 currency codes (AED … ZAR), each with a plausible exchange_rate against USD, all sharing rate_date = 2026-08-28.
  • notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/03_seed_cdc_002_truncate_data.py -- a new, dedicated seed notebook (kept separate from every other scenario's own seed notebook) that provisions the ref/bronze_ref/silver_ref schemas and landing_fx/_schemas Volumes, then copies the CSV fixture straight into /Volumes/{{catalog}}/ref/landing_fx/incoming/.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• {{catalog}}.bronze_ref.fx_rates_raw -- exactly 50 rows after the CSV is ingested (a plain APPEND streaming table; no __framework_hash_key/__framework_hash_value columns, since APPEND is never CDC-dispatched).
  • {{catalog}}.silver_ref.dim_fx_rates_current -- exactly 50 rows, every time the pipeline is triggered, regardless of how many times it runs against the same unchanged Bronze content -- the property this scenario exists to prove. A materialized view under TRUNCATE_AND_LOAD is recomputed wholesale from transformation_sql on each update, so there is no incremental state to accumulate.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
flowx_testing/020_cdc_002_truncate.json's ingestion flow:

"source_config": {
  "path": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/ref/landing_fx/incoming/",
  "format": "csv",
  "schema_location": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/ref/_schemas/fx_rates_raw/",
  "reader_options": {"header": "true", "cloudFiles.inferColumnTypes": "true"},
  "capture_technical_metadata": true
},
"target_config": {"cdc_load_strategy": "APPEND", "storage_format": "delta"}

Target: {{catalog}}.bronze_ref.fx_rates_raw, target_type: "streaming_table".

Its transformation flow -- the flow under test:

"source_inputs": [
  {"input_name": "fx_rates_raw_src", "table": "{{catalog}}.bronze_ref.fx_rates_raw", "is_streaming": false}
],
"transformation_sql": "SELECT currency_code, rate_date, exchange_rate FROM fx_rates_raw_src",
"target_config": {"cdc_load_strategy": "TRUNCATE_AND_LOAD", "storage_format": "delta"}

Target: {{catalog}}.silver_ref.dim_fx_rates_current, target_type: "materialized_view".

docs.title: Main execution flow
docs.text:
databricks bundle deploy --target dev
databricks bundle run flowx_test_cdc_002_truncate_job --target dev

Task chain: setup_control_tables -> seed_cdc_002_truncate_data -> onboard_cdc_002 -> run_pipeline.

To exercise the "no accumulation across runs" property directly: after the first successful job run, simply run databricks bundle run flowx_test_cdc_002_truncate_job --target dev again (or trigger just the pipeline update on its own) without re-landing any new file -- Auto Loader's checkpoint means Bronze stays at 50 rows regardless, and the materialized view's own full recompute means Silver stays at 50 rows too, on every subsequent update.

docs.title: Expected results — simulation notes
docs.text:
SQL assertions (after a run, replace {catalog} with your actual target catalog):

-- Bronze: exactly 50 rows, one per landed CSV row
SELECT count(*) FROM {catalog}.bronze_ref.fx_rates_raw;
-- expect: 50

-- Silver materialized view: exactly 50 rows -- the core assertion
SELECT count(*) FROM {catalog}.silver_ref.dim_fx_rates_current;
-- expect: 50

-- Re-run the pipeline update again (no new source file landed) and re-query:
SELECT count(*) FROM {catalog}.silver_ref.dim_fx_rates_current;
-- expect: still 50 -- no accumulation, no duplication, across repeated triggered updates

-- Every distinct currency code from the fixture is present exactly once
SELECT currency_code, count(*) FROM {catalog}.silver_ref.dim_fx_rates_current
GROUP BY currency_code HAVING count(*) <> 1;
-- expect: 0 rows returned

docs.title: Build notes / judgment calls
docs.text:
• New fixture, not a reuse. sample_data/sample_fx_rates.csv already exists in this repo, but it belongs to the original test_specs/*.json sample suite (seeded directly as raw_fx_rates by notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/00_seed_sample_data.py, not landed via a Volume/Auto Loader), has only 10 rows, and deliberately includes one invalid negative rate (BRL,-0.10) for a different, DQ-focused purpose. Neither its shape (already a table, not a landable CSV) nor its row count (10, not the 50 this TC specifically calls for) fit this scenario, so a new 50-row sample_data/flowx_testing/ref_usecase/fx_rates_batch1.csv fixture and its own dedicated seed notebook were added instead, following the same sample_data/flowx_testing/<domain>_usecase/ convention every other flowx_testing/* scenario's fixtures already use.
  • One CSV extract, not two. TESTING_PLAN.md frames the scenario as "daily FX rates arrive as a full replacement extract," but proving "no accumulation across runs" only requires landing the fixture once and triggering the pipeline more than once against the same unchanged Bronze content -- a materialized view's full-recompute semantics make that the correct, minimal way to exercise the property under test (see "Main execution flow" above). A second, differently-valued daily extract was considered but is not needed to prove this TC's own assertion and would only add fixture volume without adding coverage.
  • Bronze ingestion is plain APPEND, not TRUNCATE_AND_LOAD. The TC names TRUNCATE_AND_LOAD/materialized_view for the flow under test only; the raw landing step is ordinary Bronze ingestion (matching every other scenario's Bronze layer), keeping the strategy under test isolated to the one transformation flow it's meant to exercise.
  • No run_observability_task. Same judgment call as docs/40_tc_cdc_001.md: no other real scenario's job wires observability in by default (it's opt-in, via a spec's own observability[] array plus a separate job); this build follows the real setup_control_tables -> seed -> onboard -> run_pipeline convention instead.
  • No DQ rules, no governance tags, no reconciliation. This scenario is scoped to TRUNCATE_AND_LOAD's own full-recompute behavior; DQ (TC-DQ-*), governance (TC-GOV-*), and reconciliation are separate, already-tracked test modules with their own dedicated rows in TESTING_PLAN.md.

docs.title: Test Pipeline: SCD Type 1 Overwrite with Delete Mapping (TC-CDC-003)
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md (Module 2, TC-CDC-003), flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md, 02_cdc_load_strategies.md § SCD1.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Prove two things about target_config.cdc_load_strategy: "SCD1" in one scenario:

  1. Overwrite-in-place, no history. When the same primary key (customer_id) reappears in a later batch with a newer sequence_by_column value, dlt.apply_changes(..., stored_as_scd_type="1") overwrites that key's existing row wholesale -- the target never accumulates a second row for the same key, and the old attribute value is gone entirely (unlike SCD2, which would open a new history version instead).
  2. Delete mapping physically removes a row. cdc_operation_column/ cdc_operation_mapping.delete_values marks matching source rows as deletes; apply_changes(..., apply_as_deletes=...) removes the key from the target instead of upserting it -- whether or not that key ever previously existed in the target at all.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Land a customer tier feed in 2 separate batches (Day-1, then Day-2) in the same incoming Volume, so the pipeline's two triggered updates each see exactly one batch:
  • Day-1: C001 @ tier=SILVER, cdc_op=UPSERT.
  • Day-2: C001 @ tier=PLATINUM, cdc_op=UPSERT (a genuine attribute change on an already-existing key) -- and C002 @ cdc_op=DELETED (a delete marker for a key that was never landed on Day-1 at all, proving a delete op need not reference a pre-existing row to correctly result in "absent from the target").
  • One ingestion_flow (df_cdc_003_customer_scd1_ingest) with source_type: "autoloader", plain CSV format, cdc_load_strategy: "SCD1", primary_keys: ["customer_id"], sequence_by_column: "updated_at", cdc_operation_column: "cdc_op", cdc_operation_mapping.delete_values: ["DELETED"].

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• flowx_testing/021_cdc_003_scd1.json -- single-ingestion-flow onboarding spec (no transformation_flows/reconciliation_flows).
  • sample_data/flowx_testing/crm_usecase/customer_scd1_day1.csv (1 row) / customer_scd1_day2.csv (2 rows) -- hand-authored (no generator script needed for a fixture this small).
  • notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/03_seed_cdc_003_scd1_data.py -- a new, dedicated seed notebook (kept separate from every other scenario's own seed notebook) that provisions the crm schema and landing_customer/_schemas Volumes, then lands only the Day-1 fixture in /Volumes/{{catalog}}/crm/landing_customer/incoming/. The Day-2 fixture is deliberately not landed by this notebook -- see "Main execution flow" below for the manual second step this scenario requires.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• {{catalog}}.silver_crm.dim_customer_scd1 -- after the Day-1 run: exactly 1 row, C001 @ tier=SILVER. After the Day-2 run: still exactly 1 row for C001, now tier=PLATINUM (the Day-1 value is gone, overwritten in place, no second row) -- and 0 rows for C002 (its delete marker means it is never upserted at all).
  • __framework_hash_key/__framework_hash_value columns present (SCD1 is CDC-dispatched; generate_hash_columns defaults true).

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
flowx_testing/021_cdc_003_scd1.json's one ingestion_flows[] entry:

"source_config": {
  "path": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/crm/landing_customer/incoming/",
  "format": "csv",
  "schema_location": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/crm/_schemas/dim_customer_scd1/",
  "reader_options": {"header": "true", "cloudFiles.inferColumnTypes": "true"},
  "capture_technical_metadata": true
},
"target_config": {
  "cdc_load_strategy": "SCD1",
  "primary_keys": ["customer_id"],
  "sequence_by_column": "updated_at",
  "cdc_operation_column": "cdc_op",
  "cdc_operation_mapping": {"delete_values": ["DELETED"]},
  "storage_format": "delta"
},
"dq_config": {"rules": []}

Target: {{catalog}}.silver_crm.dim_customer_scd1, target_type: "streaming_table" (SCD1 always ends up backed by a genuine Streaming Table for its real storage, regardless of the flow's declared target_type -- see 02_cdc_load_strategies.md).

docs.title: Main execution flow
docs.text:
databricks bundle deploy --target dev
databricks bundle run flowx_test_cdc_003_scd1_job --target dev

Task chain: setup_control_tables -> seed_cdc_003_scd1_data -> onboard_cdc_003 -> run_pipeline. This first job run lands and processes only the Day-1 fixture -- confirm dim_customer_scd1 holds exactly 1 row (C001 @ tier=SILVER) before moving on.

Day-2 step (manual, by design -- this is the behavior the scenario exists to prove):

  1. Copy the Day-2 fixture into the same incoming Volume, e.g. from a notebook attached to the same catalog: 
    dbutils.fs.cp(
    "file:/path/to/sample_data/flowx_testing/crm_usecase/customer_scd1_day2.csv",
    "/Volumes/flowx/crm/landing_customer/incoming/customer_scd1_day2.csv",
)
    (or databricks fs cp from the CLI against the same destination path).
  2. Re-run just the pipeline (no need to re-run the whole job -- setup_control_tables/ seed_cdc_003_scd1_data/onboard_cdc_003 are all a one-time/idempotent prerequisite, not part of the behavior under test here): 
    databricks bundle run flowx_test_cdc_003_scd1_pipeline --target dev
  3. Auto Loader picks up customer_scd1_day2.csv as a new file in its next triggered (availableNow) update, and apply_changes processes both of its rows: C001's existing row is overwritten with tier=PLATINUM (sequenced by updated_at, which is newer than Day-1's); C002's row is recognized as a delete (cdc_op=DELETED matches cdc_operation_mapping.delete_values) and is never inserted.

docs.title: Expected results — simulation notes
docs.text:
SQL assertions (after the Day-2 run, replace {catalog} with your actual target catalog):

-- C001 overwritten in place -- exactly 1 row, latest tier value
SELECT tier FROM {catalog}.silver_crm.dim_customer_scd1 WHERE customer_id = 'C001';
-- expect: PLATINUM (1 row)

-- C002's delete marker means it is never present in the target
SELECT count(*) FROM {catalog}.silver_crm.dim_customer_scd1 WHERE customer_id = 'C002';
-- expect: 0

-- No history kept -- SCD1 never accumulates a second row per key
SELECT count(*) FROM {catalog}.silver_crm.dim_customer_scd1 WHERE customer_id = 'C001';
-- expect: 1 (not 2 -- contrast with TC-CDC-004's SCD2, which would show 2)

This pass's actual verification status: see flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md for whether this job was actually run against the live workspace and what the real result was -- this document describes what should happen structurally; the status tracker records what did happen, if anything, each time this scenario is executed. (Per this project's build convention, that tracker is updated centrally in a later phase, not by this build itself.)

docs.title: Build notes / judgment calls
docs.text:
• New fixtures, not a reuse. No existing seeded fixture carries a customer_id/tier shape with a dedicated delete-operation column, so 2 small new CSV fixtures (3 rows total) and 1 new dedicated seed notebook were added, kept separate from every other scenario's own seed notebook and fixtures.
  • Two-step execution is intentional, not a workaround. SCD1's overwrite/delete behavior is only observable across two separate pipeline updates against the same target -- a single job run landing both fixtures at once would still produce the correct final state, but would never demonstrate the "Day-1 row visibly changes in place on Day-2" property the test case asks for. The job's own automated run therefore covers only Day-1 (a clean, idempotent, fully self-contained job execution); the Day-2 re-land-and-rerun step is documented here as a manual follow-up, the same convention already established by 18_test_pipeline_scd1_wide_table_column_exclusion.md's own Day-1/Day-2 narrative.
  • C002 has no Day-1 row. TESTING_PLAN.md's own scenario description sends C002 only on Day-2, already carrying the delete marker -- this is deliberate (per the row's own wording: "verify ... physically drops records matching delete operation codes"), and correctly exercises apply_changes's handling of a delete for a key with no prior state: the row is simply never inserted, rather than inserted-then-immediately-deleted.
  • No run_observability_task. TESTING_PLAN.md's own "Proposed Pipeline & Job Architecture" column names a second run_observability_task step, but per TESTING_STATUS.md's framing, TESTING_PLAN.md is a planned/aspirational matrix, not a literal build spec -- no other real scenario's job wires observability in by default (it's opt-in, added via a spec's own observability[] array plus a separate job). This build follows the real setup_control_tables -> seed -> onboard -> run_pipeline convention instead; observability can be layered on later the same way scenario 100's was, if desired.
  • No DQ rules, no governance tags. This scenario is scoped to SCD1's own overwrite-in-place/delete-mapping behavior; DQ (TC-DQ-*) and governance (TC-GOV-*) are separate, already-tracked test modules with their own dedicated rows in TESTING_PLAN.md.

docs.title: Test Pipeline: SCD Type 2 Full History & Active Companion View (TC-CDC-004)
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md (Module 2, TC-CDC-004), flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md, 02_cdc_load_strategies.md § SCD2.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Prove that target_config.cdc_load_strategy: "SCD2" genuinely opens a new history row (native __START_AT/__END_AT tracking columns) the moment a tracked column changes for an existing key -- rather than overwriting the row in place the way SCD1 would -- and that the framework's auto-generated <target_table>_current companion table (cdc/scd.py::register_scd2_reporting_view) reports only the single currently-active version per key. A second, narrower thing this scenario also proves: target_config.columns_to_check genuinely scopes what counts as a change -- advancing sequence_by_column alone, with the tracked column unchanged, must not open a spurious new version.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• One ingestion_flow (df_cdc_004_employee_scd2_ingest), source_type: "autoloader", target_config.cdc_load_strategy: "SCD2" -- SCD2 is valid directly on an ingestion flow (only SCD3 is transformation-only, see 02_cdc_load_strategies.md), so this scenario needs no separate transformation step to exercise it.
  • primary_keys: ["employee_id"], sequence_by_column: "updated_at", columns_to_check: ["dept_id"] -- history tracking is scoped to department transfers only.
  • Two CSV "day" extracts landed in the same incoming Volume before the pipeline's one triggered run: E101 moves from dept D1 to D2 (must open a new version); E102/E103 are re-sent with an advanced updated_at but an unchanged dept_id (must not open a new version); E104 is a new hire appearing only in the day-2 extract (plain insert). dlt.apply_changes orders strictly by sequence_by_column, not file arrival order, so landing both extracts before a single run is equivalent to two separate daily runs for this scenario's purposes.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• flowx_testing/022_cdc_004_scd2.json -- single-ingestion-flow onboarding spec (no transformation_flows/reconciliation_flows).
  • sample_data/flowx_testing/hr_usecase/dim_employee_day1.csv (3 rows) / dim_employee_day2.csv (4 rows) -- new fixtures, hand-authored (see Build notes).
  • notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/03_seed_cdc_004_scd2_data.py -- a new, dedicated seed notebook (kept separate from every other test case's own seed step) that provisions the hr/silver_hr schemas and landing_emp/_schemas Volumes, then lands both CSV fixtures directly in /Volumes/{{catalog}}/hr/landing_emp/incoming/.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• {{catalog}}.silver_hr.dim_employee_scd2 -- the real SCD2 target, a genuine Lakeflow Streaming Table regardless of its declared target_type (dlt.apply_changes requires one -- see 02_cdc_load_strategies.md). Exactly 2 rows for employee_id = 'E101': one closed (__END_AT populated, dept_id = 'D1'), one open (__END_AT IS NULL, dept_id = 'D2'). Exactly 1 row each for E102/E103/E104 (no spurious version for the two untracked-column bumps).
  • {{catalog}}.silver_hr.dim_employee_scd2_current -- the auto-generated companion table (a real @dlt.table, not a @dlt.view -- see the two live-deployment bugs this design specifically fixes, documented in 02_cdc_load_strategies.md § SCD2). Exactly 1 row for E101, with dept_id = 'D2'.
  • __framework_hash_key/__framework_hash_value and delta.enableChangeDataFeed = "true" on the main target (every SCD2-dispatched target gets both, per 02_cdc_load_strategies.md § the hash-key/hash-value framework).

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
flowx_testing/022_cdc_004_scd2.json's one ingestion_flows[] entry:

"target_config": {
  "cdc_load_strategy": "SCD2",
  "storage_format": "delta",
  "primary_keys": ["employee_id"],
  "sequence_by_column": "updated_at",
  "columns_to_check": ["dept_id"]
}

source_config.path: /Volumes/{{catalog}}/hr/landing_emp/incoming/ (Auto Loader CSV, schema_location auto-derived under /Volumes/{{catalog}}/hr/_schemas/dim_employee_scd2/).

docs.title: Main execution flow
docs.text:
databricks bundle deploy --target dev
databricks bundle run flowx_test_cdc_004_scd2_job --target dev

Task chain: setup_control_tables → seed_cdc_004_scd2_data → onboard_cdc_004 → run_pipeline.

docs.title: Expected results — simulation notes
docs.text:
SQL assertions (after a run, replace {catalog} with your actual target catalog):

-- Full history: 2 rows for E101 (one closed, one open)
SELECT dept_id, __START_AT, __END_AT
FROM {catalog}.silver_hr.dim_employee_scd2
WHERE employee_id = 'E101'
ORDER BY __START_AT;
-- expect: (D1, <day1 ts>, <day2 ts>), (D2, <day2 ts>, NULL)

SELECT count(*) FROM {catalog}.silver_hr.dim_employee_scd2 WHERE employee_id = 'E101';
-- expect: 2

-- Untracked-column bump does not open a spurious version
SELECT employee_id, count(*) FROM {catalog}.silver_hr.dim_employee_scd2
WHERE employee_id IN ('E102', 'E103') GROUP BY employee_id;
-- expect: 1 row each

-- Companion "current" table reports only the active D2 row
SELECT dept_id FROM {catalog}.silver_hr.dim_employee_scd2_current WHERE employee_id = 'E101';
-- expect: D2

(Per this project's build convention, that tracker is updated centrally in a later phase, not by this build itself.)

docs.title: Build notes / judgment calls
docs.text:
• New fixtures, not a reuse. No existing seeded fixture matches this scenario's exact requirement (a specific employee/department transfer plus an untracked-column-only bump on two other keys, all verification-critical), so 2 new CSV fixtures and 1 new dedicated seed notebook were added, following the exact pattern flowx_test_cdc_001_append_job already established (03_seed_cdc_001_append_data.py) rather than extending 02_seed_flowx_testing_data.py or the pre-existing ea_usecase employee fixtures (those use a different, static single-snapshot shape with no day-1/day-2 department transfer and no E101/D1/D2 naming the test case specifically calls for).
  • columns_to_check scoping folded into the same fixture. Rather than building a second, separate scenario for columns_to_check, E102/E103 re-sending an advanced updated_at with an unchanged dept_id in the day-2 extract cheaply proves that lever within this same test case, at no extra fixture cost.
  • No run_observability_task. TESTING_PLAN.md's own "Proposed Pipeline & Job Architecture" column for TC-CDC-004 names a second run_observability_task step, but per TESTING_STATUS.md's framing and every other real scenario built so far (including sibling flowx_test_cdc_001_append_job), TESTING_PLAN.md is a planned/aspirational matrix, not a literal build spec -- observability is opt-in, wired via a spec's own observability[] array plus a separate job, as scenario 100's dlt_observability_job.yml does. This build follows the real setup_control_tables → seed → onboard → run_pipeline convention instead.
  • Companion object is a table, not a view. The TC detail line says "companion view"; per 02_cdc_load_strategies.md the framework deliberately registers dim_employee_scd2_current as a genuine @dlt.table (not a @dlt.view) -- this doc and its SQL assertions use the real, live object name/kind rather than the TC's colloquial "view" wording.

docs.title: Test Pipeline: SCD Type 3 Current & Previous State (TC-CDC-005)
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md (Module 2, TC-CDC-005), flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md, 02_cdc_load_strategies.md § SCD3.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Prove that target_config.cdc_load_strategy: "SCD3" tracks only the current and immediately-previous value of a monitored column — current_status/previous_status — as a subscription's status changes over time, with no full history kept (unlike SCD2) and no overwrite-with-no-trace-of-the-past (unlike SCD1). cdc/scd.py::register_scd3 has no native Lakeflow apply_changes equivalent for this: it materializes full history into a hidden _dim_subscription_scd3_scd2_history table (via stored_as_scd_type="2"), then pivots the two most recent versions of each key into current_<col>/previous_<col> columns on the public target — this scenario is the one place in this test suite that actually exercises that pivot end to end, across 3 genuinely separate pipeline updates (not 3 rows landed at once).

SCD3 is transformation-flow only — spec_validator.py::_validate_target_config rejects it explicitly on an ingestion_flow ("SCD3 pivots current/previous state via an internal history table, which only makes sense downstream of a raw ingestion flow"). So this scenario's spec necessarily pairs a plain APPEND ingestion flow (landing raw status-change events into Bronze) with a downstream SCD3 transformation flow reading that Bronze table incrementally — it cannot be built as ingestion-only.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• One ingestion_flow (df_cdc_005_subscription_events_ingest), source_type: "autoloader", plain CSV, cdc_load_strategy: "APPEND" — every landed status-change event is appended verbatim into {{catalog}}.bronze_sub.subscription_status_events_raw, no dedup, no CDC dispatch (APPEND never needs primary_keys).
  • One transformation_flow (ts_cdc_005_scd3_subscription), reading that Bronze table streaming, with cdc_load_strategy: "SCD3", primary_keys: ["sub_id"], columns_to_check: ["status"], sequence_by_column: "event_ts" — publishing {{catalog}}.silver_sub.dim_subscription_scd3.
  • Land subscription S100's status through 3 separate batches, each followed by its own pipeline update — not 3 rows landed together in one run — so the current/previous pivot is proven to advance correctly across separate incremental updates to the hidden SCD2 history table, the way a real subscription lifecycle actually arrives over time:
  • subscription_batch1.csv — status: TRIAL (event_ts: 2026-08-01T09:00:00Z).
  • subscription_batch2.csv — status: ACTIVE (event_ts: 2026-08-10T09:00:00Z).
  • subscription_batch3.csv — status: CHURNED (event_ts: 2026-08-20T09:00:00Z).

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• flowx_testing/023_cdc_005_scd3.json — one ingestion_flows entry (APPEND, Bronze) + one transformation_flows entry (SCD3, Silver); no reconciliation_flows.
  • sample_data/flowx_testing/sub_usecase/subscription_batch{1,2,3}.csv — 3 fixtures, one row each, same sub_id/customer_id/plan_name, differing only in status/event_ts.
  • notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/03_seed_cdc_005_scd3_data.py — a new, dedicated seed notebook, parameterized by a batch_number widget ("1"/"2"/"3") so it can be invoked 3 separate times across the job, landing exactly one new file into /Volumes/{{catalog}}/sub/landing_sub/incoming/ each time. Provisions the sub/bronze_sub/silver_sub schemas and landing_sub/_schemas Volumes (idempotent, re-run before every batch).

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• {{catalog}}.bronze_sub.subscription_status_events_raw — 3 rows after all 3 updates, one per landed event, verbatim (APPEND, no dedup).
  • {{catalog}}.silver_sub.dim_subscription_scd3 — exactly 1 row for sub_id = 'S100':
  • After pipeline update 1: current_status = 'TRIAL', previous_status = NULL (only one version exists yet — register_scd3's rank-2 max_by window finds nothing to pull).
  • After pipeline update 2: current_status = 'ACTIVE', previous_status = 'TRIAL'.
  • After pipeline update 3 (final, asserted state): current_status = 'CHURNED', previous_status = 'ACTIVE'.
  • A hidden {{catalog}}.silver_sub._dim_subscription_scd3_scd2_history streaming table (2 versions after update 2, 3 versions after update 3) — the real SCD2 history register_scd3 pivots over; not meant to be queried directly by consumers, but confirms the mechanism.
  • customer_id/plan_name (passthrough, non-tracked columns) present unprefixed on every row — only status is named in columns_to_check, so only it gets pivoted into current_<col>/previous_<col>.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
flowx_testing/023_cdc_005_scd3.json's transformation flow — the part of this spec that is actually new/interesting (the ingestion flow is a plain APPEND landing, identical in shape to TC-CDC-001's):

"source_inputs": [
  {"input_name": "subscription_events_src", "table": "{{catalog}}.bronze_sub.subscription_status_events_raw", "is_streaming": true}
],
"transformation_sql": "SELECT sub_id, customer_id, plan_name, status, event_ts FROM subscription_events_src",
"target_config": {
  "cdc_load_strategy": "SCD3",
  "primary_keys": ["sub_id"],
  "sequence_by_column": "event_ts",
  "columns_to_check": ["status"]
}

sequence_by_column: "event_ts" is set explicitly (rather than relying on the __framework_ingestion_timestamp_utc fallback) so version ordering inside the hidden SCD2 history table is driven by the subscription event's own business timestamp, not by whichever wall-clock moment each batch happened to be processed at — the more realistic choice for a lifecycle event feed, and independent of exactly when each batch's pipeline update actually runs.

docs.title: Main execution flow
docs.text:
databricks bundle deploy --target dev
databricks bundle run flowx_test_cdc_005_scd3_job --target dev

Task chain (one job, 3 interleaved land/run cycles):

setup_control_tables
  -> seed_cdc_005_batch1 (lands TRIAL)
    -> onboard_cdc_005
      -> run_pipeline_batch1   (update 1: current=TRIAL, previous=NULL)
        -> seed_cdc_005_batch2 (lands ACTIVE)
          -> run_pipeline_batch2   (update 2: current=ACTIVE, previous=TRIAL)
            -> seed_cdc_005_batch3 (lands CHURNED)
              -> run_pipeline_batch3   (update 3: current=CHURNED, previous=ACTIVE)

Onboarding (onboard_cdc_005) runs exactly once, immediately before the first pipeline update — the spec itself never changes across batches, only the landed data does, so re-onboarding between batches would be redundant (a harmless no-op upsert, but not needed). Each run_pipeline_batchN task targets the same flowx_test_cdc_005_scd3_pipeline — Auto Loader's own checkpoint ensures each triggered (availableNow) update only picks up the one newly-landed file, and the transformation flow's streaming source input reads that single new row incrementally into the hidden SCD2 history table, which is exactly what makes 3 separate updates necessary to observe 3 separate current/previous pivots (landing all 3 files before any pipeline update would instead collapse all 3 status changes into one Auto Loader micro-batch, and the SCD2 history table would likely see all 3 versions open in the same update — still technically producing current=CHURNED, previous=ACTIVE at the end, but proving nothing about whether the pivot behaves correctly across separate updates, which is this scenario's actual point).

docs.title: Expected results — simulation notes
docs.text:
SQL assertions (after all 3 updates have run, replace {catalog} with your actual target catalog):

-- The asserted final state (TESTING_PLAN.md's own TC-CDC-005 row)
SELECT current_status, previous_status
FROM {catalog}.silver_sub.dim_subscription_scd3
WHERE sub_id = 'S100';
-- expect: current_status = 'CHURNED', previous_status = 'ACTIVE'

-- Exactly one row for this key (SCD3 keeps no separate history rows on the public target)
SELECT count(*) FROM {catalog}.silver_sub.dim_subscription_scd3 WHERE sub_id = 'S100';
-- expect: 1

-- Passthrough columns are untouched (not pivoted, since only 'status' is in columns_to_check)
SELECT customer_id, plan_name FROM {catalog}.silver_sub.dim_subscription_scd3 WHERE sub_id = 'S100';
-- expect: CUST5001, PRO_MONTHLY

-- The raw Bronze landing has all 3 events, verbatim
SELECT count(*) FROM {catalog}.bronze_sub.subscription_status_events_raw;
-- expect: 3

-- The hidden SCD2 history table backing the pivot has all 3 versions
SELECT status FROM {catalog}.silver_sub._dim_subscription_scd3_scd2_history ORDER BY __START_AT;
-- expect: TRIAL, ACTIVE, CHURNED (3 rows)

Mid-sequence assertions, if you want to verify the pivot advances correctly at each step rather than only checking the final state (run these between run_pipeline_batch1 and run_pipeline_batch2, and again between run_pipeline_batch2 and run_pipeline_batch3):

-- After update 1 only
SELECT current_status, previous_status FROM {catalog}.silver_sub.dim_subscription_scd3 WHERE sub_id = 'S100';
-- expect: current_status = 'TRIAL', previous_status = NULL

-- After update 2 only
SELECT current_status, previous_status FROM {catalog}.silver_sub.dim_subscription_scd3 WHERE sub_id = 'S100';
-- expect: current_status = 'ACTIVE', previous_status = 'TRIAL'

This pass's actual verification status: see flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md for whether this job was actually run against the live workspace and what the real result was — this document describes what should happen structurally; the status tracker records what did happen, if anything, each time this scenario is executed. (Per this project's build convention, that tracker is updated centrally in a later phase, not by this build itself.)

docs.title: Build notes / judgment calls
docs.text:
• Real, verified column names. current_<col>/previous_<col> are read directly out of cdc/scd.py::register_scd3's own implementation (current_columns/previous_columns list comprehensions over tracked_columns, i.e. columns_to_check) rather than assumed — for this spec's columns_to_check: ["status"], that resolves to exactly current_status/ previous_status, matching TESTING_PLAN.md's own TC-CDC-005 assertion verbatim.
  • New fixtures and a new, parameterized seed notebook. No existing seeded fixture carries a subscription-status-lifecycle shape, so 3 small new one-row CSV fixtures and 1 new seed notebook (03_seed_cdc_005_scd3_data.py, kept separate from every other scenario's own seed notebook) were added. The seed notebook is parameterized by batch_number rather than split into 3 separate notebooks, since all 3 batches share identical schema/Volume-provisioning logic and differ only in which single fixture file gets copied.
  • 3 separate pipeline_task job steps against the same pipeline, interleaved with 3 separate seed steps — a deliberate departure from every other scenario's single run_pipeline step, required by SCD3's nature: the current/previous pivot can only be meaningfully proven to advance if each status change is processed by its own pipeline update, not batched together. onboard_cdc_005 still runs only once, since the spec content itself is unchanged across batches.
  • ingestion_flow needed even though this TC is "about" SCD3. SCD3 is validator-rejected on ingestion flows, so a bronze landing step is structurally required regardless of how minimal this scenario intends to keep things — this mirrors the onboarding template's own ts_template_scd3_example, which likewise reads from an already-ingested bronze table rather than defining SCD3 as an ingestion-side flow.
  • No DQ rules, no governance tags, no encryption. This scenario is scoped to SCD3's own current/previous pivot behavior; DQ (TC-DQ-*) and governance (TC-GOV-*) are separate, already-tracked test modules with their own dedicated rows in TESTING_PLAN.md.
  • No run_observability_task. TESTING_PLAN.md's "Proposed Pipeline & Job Architecture" column names one, but per TESTING_STATUS.md's framing and every other real scenario's own job (e.g. TC-CDC-001's), observability is opt-in via a spec's own observability[] array plus a separate job — not wired in by default here.

docs.title: Test Pipeline: Full Snapshot Diffing With Natural PK (TC-CDC-006)
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md (Module 2, TC-CDC-006), flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md, 02_cdc_load_strategies.md § FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Prove that target_config.cdc_load_strategy: "FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC" correctly diffs successive full extracts from a source that does carry a natural business key -- a daily inventory dump. With primary_keys: ["item_id"] configured, cdc/snapshot.py::register_full_snapshot_cdc hands each newly-landed full extract to dlt.apply_changes_from_snapshot(keys=["item_id"], stored_as_scd_type="1"), which diffs it against the previous extract by that key: a key absent from the latest dump is removed from the target, a key present in both but with changed attribute values is updated in place (unlike FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC_NO_PK's "delete-old-hash-row/insert-new-hash-row" behavior -- see TC-CDC-007 -- a real key lets Lakeflow perform a genuine upsert), and a key never seen before is inserted.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Land a warehouse inventory extract in 2 successive full snapshots (Day-1, then Day-2) in the same landing Volume, so the pipeline's two triggered updates each diff one extract against the previous state:
  • Day-1 (inventory_snapshot_day1.csv, 3 rows): baseline snapshot, keys [1, 2, 3].
  • Day-2 (inventory_snapshot_day2.csv, 3 rows): key 1 (Steel Bolts) is absent entirely (a delete); key 2 (Copper Wire) is unchanged; key 3 (Rubber Gaskets) keeps its identity but its quantity and warehouse attributes change (an update, 300 -> 850, WH-EAST -> WH-CENTRAL); key 4 (Aluminum Sheets) is a brand-new row (an insert).
  • One ingestion_flow (df_cdc_006_inventory_snapshot_ingest) with source_type: "autoloader", plain CSV format, cdc_load_strategy: "FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC", primary_keys: ["item_id"], no cdc_operation_column/cdc_operation_mapping -- this scenario relies purely on "absent from the latest dump" to express a delete, not an explicit delete-marker column.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• flowx_testing/024_cdc_006_snapshot_pk.json -- single-ingestion-flow onboarding spec (no transformation_flows/reconciliation_flows).
  • sample_data/flowx_testing/inventory_usecase/inventory_snapshot_day1.csv (3 rows) / inventory_snapshot_day2.csv (3 rows) -- new, hand-authored fixtures: no existing seeded fixture pairs a natural business key with a 2-day insert/update/delete full-snapshot shape -- the closest existing pair, sample_data/sample_mainframe_customer_master_day1/2.csv, is deliberately key-less (it is reused by TC-CDC-007's FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC_NO_PK scenario instead) -- so 2 small new CSVs (6 rows total) were added under their own inventory_usecase/ subdirectory, following this project's per-scenario fixture convention.
  • notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/03_seed_cdc_006_snapshot_pk_data.py -- a new, dedicated seed notebook (kept separate from every other scenario's own seed notebook) that provisions the inventory schema and landing_dumps/_schemas Volumes, then lands only the Day-1 extract in /Volumes/{{catalog}}/inventory/landing_dumps/. The Day-2 extract is deliberately not landed by this notebook -- see "Main execution flow" below for the manual second step this scenario requires.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• {{catalog}}.silver_inventory.inventory_snapshot_cdc -- after the Day-1 run: exactly 3 rows, keys {1, 2, 3}. After the Day-2 run: exactly 3 rows, keys {2, 3, 4} -- key 1 is gone, key 3 carries its new quantity/warehouse values (same row, updated in place, not a second row), key 4 is present as a new row.
  • __framework_hash_key/__framework_hash_value present on every row (generate_hash_columns defaults to true for every CDC-dispatched strategy) -- hashed from item_id and from every non-key business column respectively.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
flowx_testing/024_cdc_006_snapshot_pk.json's one ingestion_flows[] entry:

"source_config": {
  "path": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/inventory/landing_dumps/",
  "format": "csv",
  "schema_location": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/inventory/_schemas/inventory_snapshot_cdc/",
  "reader_options": {"header": "true", "cloudFiles.inferColumnTypes": "true"},
  "capture_technical_metadata": true
},
"target_config": {
  "cdc_load_strategy": "FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC",
  "primary_keys": ["item_id"],
  "storage_format": "delta"
},
"dq_config": {"rules": []}

Target: {{catalog}}.silver_inventory.inventory_snapshot_cdc, target_type: "streaming_table" (every CDC-dispatched strategy -- including FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC -- ends up backed by a genuine Lakeflow Streaming Table for its real storage regardless of the flow's declared target_type; see 02_cdc_load_strategies.md). primary_keys: ["item_id"] is required here -- cdc/snapshot.py::register_full_snapshot_cdc raises CdcStrategyError if it were empty for this strategy.

docs.title: Main execution flow
docs.text:
databricks bundle deploy --target dev
databricks bundle run flowx_test_cdc_006_snapshot_pk_job --target dev

Task chain: setup_control_tables -> seed_cdc_006_snapshot_pk_data -> onboard_cdc_006 -> run_pipeline. This first job run lands and processes only the Day-1 extract -- confirm inventory_snapshot_cdc holds exactly 3 rows, keys {1, 2, 3}, before moving on.

Day-2 step (manual, by design -- this is the behavior the scenario exists to prove):

  1. Copy the Day-2 fixture into the same landing Volume, e.g. from a notebook attached to the same catalog: 
    dbutils.fs.cp(
    "file:/path/to/sample_data/flowx_testing/inventory_usecase/inventory_snapshot_day2.csv",
    "/Volumes/flowx/inventory/landing_dumps/inventory_snapshot_day2.csv",
)
    (or databricks fs cp from the CLI against the same destination path).
  2. Re-run just the pipeline (no need to re-run the whole job -- setup_control_tables/seed_cdc_006_snapshot_pk_data/onboard_cdc_006 are all a one-time/idempotent prerequisite, not part of the behavior under test here): 
    databricks bundle run flowx_test_cdc_006_snapshot_pk_pipeline --target dev
  3. Auto Loader picks up inventory_snapshot_day2.csv as a new file in its next triggered (availableNow) update; cdc/snapshot.py's _latest_snapshot callback hands the full Day-2 extract to apply_changes_from_snapshot as the new latest-snapshot version, which diffs it against the Day-1 version by item_id: key 1 is removed (absent from Day-2), key 3 is updated in place (same key, new attribute values), and key 4 is inserted (a key never seen before). Key 2 is untouched either way.

docs.title: Expected results — simulation notes
docs.text:
SQL assertions (after the Day-2 run, replace {catalog} with your actual target catalog):

-- Final key set is exactly {2, 3, 4} -- key 1 is gone
SELECT item_id FROM {catalog}.silver_inventory.inventory_snapshot_cdc ORDER BY item_id;
-- expect: 2, 3, 4 (3 rows -- no row for item_id = 1)

-- Row count reflects the net Day-2 delta (3 in, 3 out: -1 delete, +1 insert, 1 in-place update)
SELECT count(*) FROM {catalog}.silver_inventory.inventory_snapshot_cdc;
-- expect: 3

-- item_id 1 was removed (present on Day-1, absent from Day-2)
SELECT count(*) FROM {catalog}.silver_inventory.inventory_snapshot_cdc WHERE item_id = 1;
-- expect: 0

-- item_id 3 was updated in place -- same key, new attribute values, still exactly 1 row
SELECT quantity, warehouse FROM {catalog}.silver_inventory.inventory_snapshot_cdc
WHERE item_id = 3;
-- expect: 850, WH-CENTRAL (1 row, not 2)

-- item_id 4 was inserted (new on Day-2)
SELECT item_name, quantity, warehouse FROM {catalog}.silver_inventory.inventory_snapshot_cdc
WHERE item_id = 4;
-- expect: Aluminum Sheets, 150, WH-WEST (1 row)

-- item_id 2 was untouched across both runs
SELECT item_name, quantity, warehouse FROM {catalog}.silver_inventory.inventory_snapshot_cdc
WHERE item_id = 2;
-- expect: Copper Wire, 1200, WH-WEST (1 row)

This pass's actual verification status: see flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md for whether this job was actually run against the live workspace and what the real result was -- this document describes what should happen structurally; the status tracker records what did happen, if anything, each time this scenario is executed. (Per this project's build convention, that tracker is updated centrally in a later phase, not by this build itself.)

docs.title: Build notes / judgment calls
docs.text:
• New fixtures, not a reuse. No existing seeded fixture carries a natural-business-key full-snapshot pair shaped for FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC (the framework's other snapshot fixture pair, sample_mainframe_customer_master_day1/2.csv, is deliberately key-less, purpose-built for TC-CDC-007's FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC_NO_PK scenario instead) -- so 2 small new CSV fixtures (6 rows total) and 1 new dedicated seed notebook were added, kept separate from every other scenario's own fixtures/seed notebook.
  • Two-step execution is intentional, not a workaround -- the same convention already established by docs/42_tc_cdc_003.md's SCD1 Day-1/Day-2 scenario and docs/46_tc_cdc_007.md's FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC_NO_PK scenario. Full-snapshot insert/update/delete diffing is only observable across two separate pipeline updates against the same target: a single job run landing both extracts at once would let Auto Loader's one triggered update see both files' rows together, which would not demonstrate a genuine "next full snapshot supersedes the previous one" diff. The job's own automated run therefore covers only Day-1 (a clean, idempotent, fully self-contained job execution); the Day-2 re-land-and- rerun step is documented above as a manual follow-up.
  • No explicit delete marker. cdc_operation_column/cdc_operation_mapping are omitted entirely -- this scenario proves the simpler, unmarked case: a key's mere absence from the latest full extract is itself sufficient for apply_changes_from_snapshot to treat it as a delete, no source-side delete flag required. (An explicit delete-marker column is exercised elsewhere -- see SCD1's cdc_operation_column example in 02_cdc_load_strategies.md.)
  • target_type: "streaming_table", matching every other ingestion flow in this repo. This field only controls whether the framework's internal quarantine-filtered "clean" view is read as a stream or a batch upstream of CDC dispatch (engine/flow_registration.py: is_streaming = flow_row.target_type == "streaming_table" for ingestion flows) -- the strategy's real published target table is always a genuine Streaming Table regardless (cdc/snapshot.py::register_full_snapshot_cdc always calls dlt.create_streaming_table), so this setting does not change the scenario's observable behavior; it is kept purely for consistency with every other ingestion flow already onboarded in this project.
  • No run_observability_task. TESTING_PLAN.md's own "Proposed Pipeline & Job Architecture" column names a second run_observability_task step, but per TESTING_STATUS.md's framing, TESTING_PLAN.md is a planned/aspirational matrix, not a literal build spec -- no other real scenario's job wires observability in by default (it's opt-in, added via a spec's own observability[] array plus a separate job). This build follows the real setup_control_tables -> seed -> onboard -> run_pipeline convention instead.
  • No DQ rules, no governance tags. This scenario is scoped to FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC's own natural-key diffing behavior; DQ (TC-DQ-*) and governance (TC-GOV-*) are separate, already-tracked test modules with their own dedicated rows in TESTING_PLAN.md.

docs.title: Test Pipeline: Full Snapshot Diffing Without PK (TC-CDC-007)
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md (Module 2, TC-CDC-007), flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md, 02_cdc_load_strategies.md § FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC_NO_PK.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Prove that target_config.cdc_load_strategy: "FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC_NO_PK" correctly diffs successive full extracts from a source with no natural business key at all -- a classic legacy mainframe file dump. With no primary_keys configured, dq/quarantine.py:: _apply_hash_and_surrogate_key_columns generates __framework_surrogate_key (crypto/hashing.py::generate_surrogate_key_hash, a deterministic SHA-256 hash of every payload column) and cdc/snapshot.py::register_full_snapshot_cdc uses that hash -- not a user-supplied column -- as the apply_changes_from_snapshot diff key. A row that changes any field is therefore correctly tracked as a delete-of-the-old-row plus insert-of-a-new-row (the only possible interpretation when there is no stable identity to hang an "update" off of), a genuinely new row is inserted, and a row absent from the latest extract is removed.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Land a legacy mainframe customer/account extract in 2 successive full snapshots (Day-1, then Day-2) in the same landing Volume, so the pipeline's two triggered updates each diff one extract against the previous state:
  • Day-1 (sample_mainframe_customer_master_day1.csv, 10 rows): baseline snapshot, no natural key column present (customer_name, customer_city, customer_status only).
  • Day-2 (sample_mainframe_customer_master_day2.csv, 10 rows): John Smith's customer_status changes ACTIVE -> INACTIVE; Fatima Ali's customer_city changes Dallas -> Fort Worth; Wei Zhang is entirely absent (a delete); Noah Kim is a brand-new row (an insert). The other 7 rows are unchanged.
  • One ingestion_flow (df_cdc_007_mainframe_accounts_ingest) with source_type: "autoloader", plain CSV format, cdc_load_strategy: "FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC_NO_PK", generate_surrogate_key: true (the strategy's own default -- set explicitly here for clarity), no primary_keys at all.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• flowx_testing/025_cdc_007_snapshot_nopk.json -- single-ingestion-flow onboarding spec (no transformation_flows/reconciliation_flows).
  • sample_data/sample_mainframe_customer_master_day1.csv (10 rows) / sample_mainframe_customer_master_day2.csv (10 rows) -- reused, not newly authored: these already exist, generated by sample_data/generate_sample_datasets.py:: generate_mainframe_snapshot_datasets specifically for a FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC_NO_PK "two-day snapshot pair: 1 update, 1 delete, 1 insert" scenario -- an exact shape match for this test case, so no new fixture was written.
  • notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/03_seed_cdc_007_snapshot_nopk_data.py -- a new, dedicated seed notebook (kept separate from every other scenario's own seed notebook) that provisions the legacy schema and landing_mainframe/_schemas Volumes, then lands only the Day-1 extract in /Volumes/{{catalog}}/legacy/landing_mainframe/. The Day-2 extract is deliberately not landed by this notebook -- see "Main execution flow" below for the manual second step this scenario requires.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• {{catalog}}.silver_legacy.mainframe_accounts_cdc -- after the Day-1 run: exactly 10 rows, one per Day-1 source row, each carrying a non-null __framework_surrogate_key. After the Day-2 run: still exactly 10 rows (the net Day-2 delta: -1 for Wei Zhang's removal, +1 for Noah Kim's insertion; John Smith's and Fatima Ali's changed rows each still count as exactly one present row, just under a new surrogate-key value).
  • __framework_surrogate_key present and non-null on every row (this strategy's defining column). __framework_hash_key is also present -- with no primary_keys configured, the generated surrogate key itself becomes the key hashed into __framework_hash_key (dq/quarantine.py::_apply_hash_and_surrogate_key_columns).

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
flowx_testing/025_cdc_007_snapshot_nopk.json's one ingestion_flows[] entry:

"source_config": {
  "path": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/legacy/landing_mainframe/",
  "format": "csv",
  "schema_location": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/legacy/_schemas/mainframe_accounts_cdc/",
  "reader_options": {"header": "true", "cloudFiles.inferColumnTypes": "true"},
  "capture_technical_metadata": true
},
"target_config": {
  "cdc_load_strategy": "FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC_NO_PK",
  "generate_surrogate_key": true,
  "storage_format": "delta"
},
"dq_config": {"rules": []}

Target: {{catalog}}.silver_legacy.mainframe_accounts_cdc, target_type: "streaming_table" (every CDC-dispatched strategy -- including FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC_NO_PK -- ends up backed by a genuine Lakeflow Streaming Table for its real storage regardless of the flow's declared target_type; see 02_cdc_load_strategies.md). No primary_keys field is set at all -- cdc/snapshot.py::register_full_snapshot_cdc unconditionally uses keys = ["__framework_surrogate_key"] whenever cdc_load_strategy == "FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC_NO_PK", so one is never needed.

docs.title: Main execution flow
docs.text:
databricks bundle deploy --target dev
databricks bundle run flowx_test_cdc_007_snapshot_nopk_job --target dev

Task chain: setup_control_tables -> seed_cdc_007_snapshot_nopk_data -> onboard_cdc_007 -> run_pipeline. This first job run lands and processes only the Day-1 extract -- confirm mainframe_accounts_cdc holds exactly 10 rows, each with a non-null __framework_surrogate_key, before moving on.

Day-2 step (manual, by design -- this is the behavior the scenario exists to prove):

  1. Copy the Day-2 fixture into the same landing Volume, e.g. from a notebook attached to the same catalog: 
    dbutils.fs.cp(
    "file:/path/to/sample_data/sample_mainframe_customer_master_day2.csv",
    "/Volumes/flowx/legacy/landing_mainframe/sample_mainframe_customer_master_day2.csv",
)
    (or databricks fs cp from the CLI against the same destination path).
  2. Re-run just the pipeline (no need to re-run the whole job -- setup_control_tables/seed_cdc_007_snapshot_nopk_data/onboard_cdc_007 are all a one-time/idempotent prerequisite, not part of the behavior under test here): 
    databricks bundle run flowx_test_cdc_007_snapshot_nopk_pipeline --target dev
  3. Auto Loader picks up sample_mainframe_customer_master_day2.csv as a new file in its next triggered (availableNow) update; cdc/snapshot.py's _latest_snapshot callback hands the full Day-2 extract (with fresh __framework_surrogate_key values recomputed over every row) to apply_changes_from_snapshot as the new latest-snapshot version, which diffs it against the Day-1 version by surrogate key: John Smith's and Fatima Ali's old-hash rows are removed and their new-hash rows inserted (their real-world identity is the same row, but the framework has no way to know that without a natural key -- it only sees "an old hash disappeared, a new one appeared", which is the documented, correct behavior for this strategy), Wei Zhang's row is removed entirely (absent from Day-2), and Noah Kim's row is inserted (a hash never seen before).

docs.title: Expected results — simulation notes
docs.text:
SQL assertions (after the Day-2 run, replace {catalog} with your actual target catalog):

-- Every row has a surrogate key
SELECT count(*) AS rows_missing_surrogate_key
FROM {catalog}.silver_legacy.mainframe_accounts_cdc
WHERE __framework_surrogate_key IS NULL;
-- expect: 0

-- Row count reflects the net Day-2 delta (10 in, 10 out: -1 delete, +1 insert)
SELECT count(*) FROM {catalog}.silver_legacy.mainframe_accounts_cdc;
-- expect: 10

-- Wei Zhang was removed (present on Day-1, absent from Day-2)
SELECT count(*) FROM {catalog}.silver_legacy.mainframe_accounts_cdc
WHERE customer_name = 'Wei Zhang';
-- expect: 0

-- Noah Kim was inserted (new on Day-2)
SELECT customer_city, customer_status FROM {catalog}.silver_legacy.mainframe_accounts_cdc
WHERE customer_name = 'Noah Kim';
-- expect: San Jose, ACTIVE (1 row)

-- John Smith's status change landed under a new surrogate key, old value gone
SELECT customer_status FROM {catalog}.silver_legacy.mainframe_accounts_cdc
WHERE customer_name = 'John Smith';
-- expect: INACTIVE (1 row, not 2 -- the Day-1 ACTIVE-hash row is gone)

-- Fatima Ali's city change landed the same way
SELECT customer_city FROM {catalog}.silver_legacy.mainframe_accounts_cdc
WHERE customer_name = 'Fatima Ali';
-- expect: Fort Worth (1 row)
