(Per this project's build convention, that tracker is updated centrally in a later phase, not by this build itself.)

docs.title: Build notes / judgment calls
docs.text:
• Reused existing fixtures, not new ones. sample_data/sample_mainframe_customer_master_ day1.csv/_day2.csv already existed, purpose-built by generate_sample_datasets.py:: generate_mainframe_snapshot_datasets for exactly this "no natural key, 1 update, 1 delete, 1 insert" shape -- per this project's own build convention (reuse a close-enough existing fixture over inventing a new one), these are read directly from their existing top-level sample_data/ location rather than copied into a new sample_data/flowx_testing/<usecase>/ subdirectory.
  • Two-step execution is intentional, not a workaround -- the same convention already established by docs/42_tc_cdc_003.md's SCD1 Day-1/Day-2 scenario and 18_test_pipeline_scd1_wide_table_column_exclusion.md. Surrogate-key-based insert/update/delete diffing is only observable across two separate pipeline updates against the same target: a single job run landing both extracts at once would let Auto Loader's one triggered update see both files' rows together, which would not demonstrate a genuine "next full snapshot supersedes the previous one" diff. The job's own automated run therefore covers only Day-1 (a clean, idempotent, fully self-contained job execution); the Day-2 re-land-and-rerun step is documented above as a manual follow-up.
  • generate_surrogate_key: true is set explicitly even though it is this strategy's own documented default (dq/quarantine.py::_apply_hash_and_surrogate_key_columns: target_config.get("generate_surrogate_key", cdc_load_strategy == "FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC_NO_PK")) -- for readability, matching the worked examples in onboarding_templates/onboarding_spec_full_reference.json and pipeline_onboarding_template.json, both of which set it explicitly too.
  • target_type: "streaming_table", matching every other ingestion flow in this repo. This field only controls whether the framework's internal quarantine-filtered "clean" view is read as a stream or a batch upstream of CDC dispatch (engine/flow_registration.py: is_streaming = flow_row.target_type == "streaming_table" for ingestion flows) -- the strategy's real published target table is always a genuine Streaming Table regardless (cdc/snapshot.py::register_full_snapshot_cdc always calls dlt.create_streaming_table), so this setting does not change the scenario's observable behavior; it is kept purely for consistency with every other ingestion flow already onboarded in this project.
  • No run_observability_task. TESTING_PLAN.md's own "Proposed Pipeline & Job Architecture" column names a second run_observability_task step, but per TESTING_STATUS.md's framing, TESTING_PLAN.md is a planned/aspirational matrix, not a literal build spec -- no other real scenario's job wires observability in by default (it's opt-in, added via a spec's own observability[] array plus a separate job). This build follows the real setup_control_tables -> seed -> onboard -> run_pipeline convention instead.
  • No DQ rules, no governance tags. This scenario is scoped to FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC_NO_PK's own surrogate-key diffing behavior; DQ (TC-DQ-*) and governance (TC-GOV-*) are separate, already-tracked test modules with their own dedicated rows in TESTING_PLAN.md.

docs.title: Test Pipeline: Multi-Source Streaming-to-Batch 4-Way Inner Join (TC-TRF-001)
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md (Module 3, TC-TRF-001), flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Prove that a transformation_flows entry can join one streaming Auto Loader source (is_streaming: true) against three batch-read dimension tables (is_streaming: false) in a single transformation_sql inner join, and that the join genuinely excludes an entity present on one side but absent on the other -- not just that a 4-way join parses and runs in general (scenario 001 already proves that, but every row on every side of its join always matches, so it never exercises the exclusion behavior itself).

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• 4 ingestion_flows, all source_type: "autoloader", all target_type: "streaming_table", landing plain (unzipped) CSVs into this test case's own dedicated bronze tables:
  • df_trf001_assignments_ingest -> bronze_ea.trf001_assignments_raw -- the fact table, read is_streaming: true at the join.
  • df_trf001_employees_ingest -> bronze_ea.trf001_employees_raw -- dimension, read is_streaming: false.
  • df_trf001_departments_ingest -> bronze_ea.trf001_departments_raw -- dimension, read is_streaming: false.
  • df_trf001_projects_ingest -> bronze_ea.trf001_projects_raw -- dimension, read is_streaming: false.
  • One transformation_flows entry (ts_trf001_ea_joined_assignments) with 4 source_inputs, doing a plain JOIN (SQL JOIN = inner join) across all 4, reusing scenario 001's own join-SQL pattern verbatim (see resources/flowx_test_001_zip_join_export_pipeline.yml's header comment and flowx_testing/001_zip_file_onboarding.json's transformation_sql) -- only the source_inputs[].table values differ (this test case's own trf001_* bronze tables, not scenario 001's ZIP-ingested ones):
SELECT a.employee_id, a.project_id, a.hours_allocated, e.employee_name, e.role, e.dept_id,
       d.dept_name, d.region, p.project_name, p.budget
FROM assignments_raw a
JOIN employees_raw e ON a.employee_id = e.employee_id
JOIN departments_raw d ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id
JOIN projects_raw p ON a.project_id = p.project_id
  • employee_id = 'E005' (Olivia Brown, dept_id = 'D004') exists in trf001_employees_raw but has no row in trf001_assignments_raw -- the inner join must silently drop it, not error and not appear in the output with NULL join columns (that would be a LEFT JOIN, not what this SQL does).
  • cdc_load_strategy: "APPEND" on every flow -- this scenario is about join semantics, not CDC behavior, so the simplest load strategy keeps the flow focused on the one thing under test (same choice scenario 001 and TC-ING-001 both already made for the same reason).

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• flowx_testing/026_trf_001_4way_join.json -- 4 ingestion_flows + 1 transformation_flows entry (no reconciliation_flows).
  • sample_data/flowx_testing/ea_usecase/{employees,departments,projects,assignments}.csv -- reused as-is, no new fixture needed (see Build notes below for why these files already have exactly the shape this test case requires).
  • notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/03_seed_trf_001_4way_join_data.py -- a new, dedicated seed notebook (kept separate from 02_seed_flowx_testing_data.py, which belongs to scenario 001) that provisions the ea/bronze_ea/silver_ea schemas and landing_assignments/landing_employees/landing_departments/landing_projects/ _schemas Volumes, then lands each CSV fixture plain, unzipped (no source_zip_handling -- ZIP extraction isn't what this test case exercises).

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• {{catalog}}.silver_ea.trf001_ea_joined_assignments -- exactly 5 rows (one per assignments.csv row: E001/P001, E002/P001, E002/P002, E003/P003, E004/P004), every join column populated (no NULLs from the reference sides, since every dept_id/project_id referenced by assignments.csv/employees.csv resolves in both departments.csv/projects.csv).
  • Zero rows with employee_id = 'E005' anywhere in that table.
  • {{catalog}}.bronze_ea.trf001_employees_raw still has all 5 employees (E001-E005) -- E005's absence is a property of the join output only, not of the ingested employee dimension itself.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
flowx_testing/026_trf_001_4way_join.json's one transformation_flows[] entry's source_inputs:

"source_inputs": [
  {"input_name": "assignments_raw", "table": "{{catalog}}.bronze_ea.trf001_assignments_raw", "is_streaming": true},
  {"input_name": "employees_raw", "table": "{{catalog}}.bronze_ea.trf001_employees_raw", "is_streaming": false},
  {"input_name": "departments_raw", "table": "{{catalog}}.bronze_ea.trf001_departments_raw", "is_streaming": false},
  {"input_name": "projects_raw", "table": "{{catalog}}.bronze_ea.trf001_projects_raw", "is_streaming": false}
]

target_config: {"cdc_load_strategy": "APPEND", "storage_format": "delta"} on every flow -- plain streaming tables, no primary keys, no hash columns.

databricks bundle run flowx_test_trf_001_4way_join_job --target dev

Task chain: setup_control_tables → seed_trf_001_4way_join_data → onboard_trf_001 → run_pipeline.

docs.title: Build notes / judgment calls
docs.text:
• Reused fixture, not new sample data. sample_data/flowx_testing/ea_usecase/{employees,departments,projects,assignments}.csv (already seeded by scenario 001's own 02_seed_flowx_testing_data.py, as plain ZIP payloads) already have exactly this test case's required shape with zero changes needed: employees.csv has 5 rows (E001-E005), assignments.csv has exactly 5 rows covering only E001-E004, and every dept_id/project_id referenced anywhere resolves cleanly in departments.csv/projects.csv. Per this project's build convention (reuse over inventing new sample data), this test case's own seed notebook reads the same 4 CSV files directly rather than generating new ones -- only the landing mechanism differs (plain copy here vs. on-cluster ZIP-then-land in scenario 001's seed step).
  • Genuine naming collision with scenario 001 -- resolved by renaming this test case's own targets, not scenario 001's. TESTING_PLAN.md's own Databricks-object-names column for TC-TRF-001 names bronze targets employees_raw/departments_raw/projects_raw/ assignments_raw and a silver target ea_joined_assignments -- but scenario 001 (flowx_test_001_zip_join_export_pipeline, already deployed) already owns real, already-materialized Lakeflow objects with those exact same {catalog}.bronze_ea.*/{catalog}.silver_ea.ea_joined_assignments three-part names. Two different Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines cannot both declare a streaming table/materialized-view/sink against the identical Unity Catalog table -- Lakeflow ties a managed table to the one pipeline that created it, so this test case's own pipeline attempting to CREATE STREAMING TABLE over scenario 001's already-owned tables would fail at deployment/runtime with a table-ownership conflict, not produce two independent test results. Per this build's scope discipline (never edit another test case's files), the fix had to be on this test case's side: every one of this spec's own bronze targets is named trf001_<name>_raw and its silver target is named trf001_ea_joined_assignments, all still under the same bronze_ea/silver_ea schemas TESTING_PLAN.md names, just with a disambiguating table-name prefix. The join-SQL pattern, the DQ/CDC semantics, and the expected row-count assertions are otherwise byte-for-byte what TESTING_PLAN.md and the task both describe -- only the literal target table names changed, and only to avoid breaking an already-deployed, real object this build is barred from touching.
  • No run_observability_task. Same judgment call TC-ING-001's doc already made: TESTING_PLAN.md's "Proposed Pipeline & Job Architecture" column names a second run_observability_task step, but per TESTING_STATUS.md's own framing, that column is planned/aspirational, not a literal build spec -- no other real scenario's job wires observability in by default (it's opt-in, layered on separately, as scenario 100's dlt_observability_job.yml does). This build follows the real setup_control_tables → seed → onboard → run_pipeline convention instead.

docs.title: Test Pipeline: Multi-Regional Ingestion UNION ALL Consolidation (TC-TRF-002)
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md (Module 3, TC-TRF-002), flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Prove that transformation_sql genuinely combines two independently-ingested regional Bronze tables via UNION ALL into one consolidated enterprise Silver dataset -- no rows lost, none duplicated, none deduplicated away -- and that both regions' rows survive intact (their region value included) rather than one region's data silently overwriting or shadowing the other.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Two ingestion_flows, each a plain streaming Auto Loader CSV ingest with cdc_load_strategy: "APPEND" (no primary keys, no CDC comparison -- this scenario is about UNION ALL consolidation, not CDC behavior, so the simplest load strategy keeps the flow focused on the one thing under test):
  • df_trf_002_orders_na_ingest -> {{catalog}}.bronze_sales.orders_na_raw (5 rows).
  • df_trf_002_orders_eu_ingest -> {{catalog}}.bronze_sales.orders_eu_raw (4 rows).
  • One transformation_flow (ts_trf_002_union_all_global_orders) with two source_inputs (both is_streaming: true, referencing the two Bronze tables above) and transformation_sql: "SELECT * FROM orders_na_raw UNION ALL SELECT * FROM orders_eu_raw" -> {{catalog}}.silver_sales.all_global_orders.
  • Row counts (5 NA / 4 EU) are deliberately scaled down from TESTING_PLAN.md's own 500/400 -- the ratio (unequal sizes, both non-trivial) is what this scenario proves, not the absolute count, and small fixtures keep onboarding/pipeline runs fast. Deliberately unequal sizes so a passing row-count assertion can't be explained by one side accidentally being read twice.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• flowx_testing/027_trf_002_union_all.json -- 2 ingestion flows + 1 transformation flow (no reconciliation_flows).
  • sample_data/flowx_testing/sales_usecase/orders_na_raw.csv (5 rows, region = 'NA') / orders_eu_raw.csv (4 rows, region = 'EU').
  • notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/03_seed_trf_002_union_all_data.py -- a new, dedicated seed notebook (kept separate from every other test case's own seed step) that provisions the sales/bronze_sales/silver_sales schemas and two independent per-region landing Volumes (landing_orders_na, landing_orders_eu -- deliberately separate, not one shared incoming folder, so each Auto Loader flow only ever discovers its own region's file), then lands one CSV batch per region.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• {{catalog}}.bronze_sales.orders_na_raw -- exactly 5 rows.
  • {{catalog}}.bronze_sales.orders_eu_raw -- exactly 4 rows.
  • {{catalog}}.silver_sales.all_global_orders -- exactly 9 rows (5 + 4), with both NA and EU values present in its region column.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
flowx_testing/027_trf_002_union_all.json's transformation_flows[0]:

"source_inputs": [
  {"input_name": "orders_na_raw", "table": "{{catalog}}.bronze_sales.orders_na_raw", "is_streaming": true},
  {"input_name": "orders_eu_raw", "table": "{{catalog}}.bronze_sales.orders_eu_raw", "is_streaming": true}
],
"transformation_sql": "SELECT * FROM orders_na_raw UNION ALL SELECT * FROM orders_eu_raw",
"target_config": {"cdc_load_strategy": "APPEND", "storage_format": "delta"}

No watermark is needed on either source_inputs[] entry -- watermarks are only required when two streaming inputs are joined; a plain UNION ALL across streams has no such requirement (see 17_onboarding_template_reference.md §3.2/§3.4). The engine rewrites the bare FROM orders_na_raw/FROM orders_eu_raw references to FROM STREAM ... automatically at runtime since both inputs are marked is_streaming: true -- the spec itself never writes STREAM.

docs.title: Main execution flow
docs.text:
databricks bundle deploy --target dev
databricks bundle run flowx_test_trf_002_union_all_job --target dev

Task chain: setup_control_tables → seed_trf_002_union_all_data → onboard_trf_002 → run_pipeline.

docs.title: Expected results — simulation notes
docs.text:
SQL assertions (after a run, replace {catalog} with your actual target catalog):

SELECT count(*) FROM {catalog}.bronze_sales.orders_na_raw;   -- expect: 5
SELECT count(*) FROM {catalog}.bronze_sales.orders_eu_raw;   -- expect: 4
SELECT count(*) FROM {catalog}.silver_sales.all_global_orders;  -- expect: 9

-- both regional codes represented, in the right proportion
SELECT region, count(*) FROM {catalog}.silver_sales.all_global_orders
GROUP BY region ORDER BY region;
-- expect: EU -> 4, NA -> 5

(Per this project's build convention, that tracker is updated centrally in a later phase, not by this build itself.)

docs.title: Build notes / judgment calls
docs.text:
• New, dedicated fixtures, not a reuse of sample_data/sample_orders_region_a.csv / sample_orders_region_b.csv. Those two existing CSVs already back an unrelated, pre-existing legacy scenario (tests/integration/test_transformation_union_all.py, a poc-catalog bronze_union_test/silver_union_test suite outside this flowx_testing/ TC series) whose assertions depend on their exact row counts (5 and 6) and order IDs -- reusing or trimming them here would either not match this TC's required 5/4 split or risk destabilizing that other suite's fixtures. New fixtures (sample_data/flowx_testing/sales_usecase/orders_na_raw.csv / orders_eu_raw.csv, 5 and 4 rows) were generated instead, following the exact same CSV shape (order_id, order_ts, customer_id, product_id, quantity, unit_price, region) so the two scenarios stay structurally analogous without sharing state.
  • No run_observability_task. TESTING_PLAN.md's own "Proposed Pipeline & Job Architecture" column names a second run_observability_task step for every test case in the matrix, but per the established convention already followed by every other individually-built TC in this repo (e.g. docs/31_tc_ing_001.md's own build notes), TESTING_PLAN.md is a planned/aspirational matrix, not a literal build spec -- observability is opt-in, wired via a spec's own observability[] array plus a separate job, not a default task on every pipeline job. This build follows the real setup_control_tables → seed → onboard → run_pipeline convention instead.
  • Region values 'NA'/'EU' (matching the ingestion flow/table naming) rather than the region_a/region_b values used by the unrelated legacy fixture noted above -- chosen to read naturally against this TC's own orders_na_raw/orders_eu_raw table names and the "both regional codes represented" verification wording in TESTING_PLAN.md.

docs.title: Test Pipeline: TC-TRF-003 — In-DAG Column Decryption for Business Computations
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md (Module 8, TC-TRF-003), flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md, 16_encryption_and_secrets.md (the full AES column encryption/decryption design), 01_control_metadata_schema.md §4/§7 and 17_onboarding_template_reference.md §3.3/§4.3 (the exact encrypted_columns/decrypted_columns field reference).

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Prove that a column encrypted at rest in Bronze can be decrypted in-memory, inside the same Lakeflow Declarative Pipeline DAG, immediately ahead of a real business computation over its plaintext value — never as a separate post-processing job, and never landing a decrypted copy back to storage. target_config.encrypted_columns (ingestion) and source_inputs[].decrypted_columns (transformation) are both individually exercised elsewhere in this project's docs/templates, but this scenario is the first to chain them end to end against a genuinely computed aggregate (sum(billing_amount)) and assert the exact resulting number, proving the round trip is lossless, not merely "no longer plaintext" (see 16_encryption_and_secrets.md §2's own account of a real, live-confirmed corruption bug this exact kind of round-trip assertion was needed to catch).

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• One ingestion flow (df_health_patient_visits_ingest), source_type: "autoloader", cdc_load_strategy: "APPEND" — deliberately the simplest possible CDC strategy, since an AES-GCM-encrypted column must never be compared for change detection (random IV per call — see 16_encryption_and_secrets.md §3), and APPEND has no comparison concept at all to worry about.
  • target_config.encrypted_columns AES-GCM-encrypts billing_amount in place (output_column same as column_name) before it lands in {{catalog}}.bronze_health.patient_visits_raw — keyed off {{catalog}}.security.pii_encryption_key, the existing UC secret this project already documents provisioning for in 05_deployment_guide.md's prerequisites section (reused verbatim, not a new key).
  • One transformation flow (ts_trf_003_patient_billing_summary), reading patient_visits_raw as a batch input (is_streaming: false — a full-recompute aggregate has no meaningful incremental/streaming form), whose source_inputs[].decrypted_columns decrypts billing_amount back to plaintext (cast_to_type: "double", matching the column's pre-encryption inferred CSV type) before transformation_sql ever runs.
  • transformation_sql: "SELECT sum(billing_amount) AS billing_amount FROM patient_visits_input" computes the aggregate over the now-plaintext column, published as a materialized_view (cdc_load_strategy: "TRUNCATE_AND_LOAD" — a full recompute on every pipeline update, the same pairing 17_onboarding_template_reference.md §4.1 documents for ts_template_truncate_and_load_example) into {{catalog}}.silver_health.patient_billing_summary.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• flowx_testing/028_trf_003_decrypt_transform.json — the onboarding spec (one ingestion flow, one transformation flow, no reconciliation flows).
  • sample_data/flowx_testing/health_usecase/patient_visits_batch1.csv — 5-row plaintext fixture (visit_id, patient_id, patient_name, visit_date, department, billing_amount), landed as-is (no ZIP/PGP handling — the encryption in this scenario is the framework's own encrypted_columns, not a landing-file-level concern).
  • notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/03_seed_trf_003_decrypt_transform_data.py — a new, dedicated seed notebook (per this test case's own instructions: a genuinely new fixture, not a reuse of an existing one) that provisions the health/bronze_health/silver_health schemas and the landing_visits/_schemas Volumes, then lands the CSV fixture directly — the same "plain Auto Loader CSV, no ZIP handling needed" pattern 03_seed_cdc_002_truncate_data.py already established for a materialized-view target scenario.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• {catalog}.bronze_health.patient_visits_raw — 5 rows; billing_amount stores AES-GCM ciphertext (base64-encoded binary), not plaintext, plus the usual __framework_* technical metadata columns.
  • {catalog}.silver_health.patient_billing_summary — exactly 1 row, one column (billing_amount), holding the decrypted-then-summed value.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
flowx_testing/028_trf_003_decrypt_transform.json's ingestion-side encryption:

"target_config": {
  "cdc_load_strategy": "APPEND",
  "storage_format": "delta",
  "encrypted_columns": [
    {
      "column_name": "billing_amount",
      "output_column": "billing_amount",
      "mode": "GCM",
      "secret": {"secret_catalog": "{{catalog}}", "secret_schema": "security", "secret_key": "pii_encryption_key"}
    }
  ]
}

...and the transformation-side decryption immediately ahead of the aggregate:

"source_inputs": [
  {
    "input_name": "patient_visits_input",
    "table": "{{catalog}}.bronze_health.patient_visits_raw",
    "is_streaming": false,
    "decrypted_columns": [
      {
        "column_name": "billing_amount",
        "output_column": "billing_amount",
        "mode": "GCM",
        "cast_to_type": "double",
        "secret": {"secret_catalog": "{{catalog}}", "secret_schema": "security", "secret_key": "pii_encryption_key"}
      }
    ]
  }
],
"transformation_sql": "SELECT sum(billing_amount) AS billing_amount FROM patient_visits_input"

mode: "GCM" matches on both sides deliberately — aes_decrypt is not mode-agnostic, it must match whatever mode the column was originally encrypted with (see 16_encryption_and_secrets.md §3).

docs.title: Required prerequisite: the pii_encryption_key UC secret must already exist
docs.text:
Manual, admin-audited step — not automated by this framework, and not (re-)provisioned by this test case. This scenario deliberately reuses the exact key 05_deployment_guide.md's own prerequisites section already documents provisioning for this project's other encryption scenarios — no new key is created:

databricks secrets create-scope security   # no-op if it already exists from an earlier scenario
databricks secrets put-secret security pii_encryption_key --string-value "$(openssl rand -hex 16)"

This must run before flowx_test_trf_003_decrypt_transform_job's run_pipeline_task — both the ingestion flow's encryption step and the transformation flow's decryption step fail with CryptoError/SecretResolutionError until it does. If this secret was already provisioned for an earlier scenario in this same workspace (e.g. TC-SEC-001, or the crypto exhaustive suite), this scenario reuses it as-is and needs no separate provisioning step at all.

docs.title: Main execution flow
docs.text:
databricks bundle deploy --target dev
databricks secrets put-secret security pii_encryption_key --string-value "$(openssl rand -hex 16)"   # skip if already provisioned
databricks bundle run flowx_test_trf_003_decrypt_transform_job --target dev

Task chain: setup_control_tables → seed_trf_003_decrypt_transform_data → onboard_trf_003 → run_pipeline_task.

docs.title: Expected results — verification logic
docs.text:
-- Bronze: billing_amount is ciphertext, never plaintext
SELECT billing_amount FROM {catalog}.bronze_health.patient_visits_raw LIMIT 1;
-- expect: base64-looking binary, never a value resembling "250.00"/"175.50"/etc.

-- Silver: the decrypted-then-summed value matches the fixture's known plaintext sum exactly
SELECT sum(billing_amount) FROM {catalog}.silver_health.patient_billing_summary;
-- expect: 1256.00  (== 250.00 + 175.50 + 320.25 + 99.75 + 410.50, the fixture's own known total)

If encrypted_columns/decrypted_columns' secret hasn't been provisioned yet, or is wrong, the pipeline update fails fast with a CryptoError/SecretResolutionError naming the secret coordinates — this is the expected, correct failure mode, not a bug to route around. If decrypted_columns[].mode/cast_to_type were ever set inconsistently with how the column was actually encrypted, aes_decrypt would either raise or return garbage bytes rather than the correct plaintext — this scenario's exact-sum assertion is specifically designed to catch that class of silent corruption, not just "is it no longer plaintext."

This pass's actual verification status: see flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md for whether this job was actually run against the live workspace and what the real result was — this document describes what should happen structurally; the status tracker records what did happen.

docs.title: Known gaps / judgment calls
docs.text:
• target_type choice for the Silver aggregate: this test case's own instructions describe the transformation as computing "running revenue totals" but leave the exact target_type unspecified. A plain SELECT sum(...) with no GROUP BY/window has no natural streaming or incremental form (Lakeflow streaming tables need an append-friendly, row-preserving query, not a single collapsing aggregate), so this scenario reads Bronze as a batch input (is_streaming: false) and publishes a materialized_view with cdc_load_strategy: "TRUNCATE_AND_LOAD" — a full recompute of the one-row summary on every pipeline update, the same pairing already established by ts_template_truncate_and_load_example (see 17_onboarding_template_reference.md §4.1). A per-row "running total" (e.g. a window function) was considered and rejected as unnecessary complexity beyond what the SQL assertion in this test case's own spec (SELECT sum(billing_amount) FROM ...) actually requires — a single summary row.
  • Scope-vs-catalog terminology, pii_encryption_key: identical to the pre-existing gap 35_tc_ing_005.md already flags for pgp_private_key_finance_test — the databricks secrets put-secret security pii_encryption_key ... command above follows 05_deployment_guide.md's own prerequisites-section CLI pattern exactly (as this test case's own instructions required, "reusing the EXISTING key"), which that guide's prose labels a classic workspace-level secret scope command, while the onboarding spec addresses this same key via the Unity Catalog three-level {secret_catalog, secret_schema, secret_key} shape, resolved via dbutils.secrets.get(catalog=, schema=, key=) — a different, newer secret system per 16_encryption_and_secrets.md §1. Not introduced or resolved by this test case; follow whichever secrets CLI syntax your workspace/CLI version actually requires to create a Unity Catalog secret at {{catalog}}.security.pii_encryption_key — the important, framework-relevant part is the resulting secret coordinates, not the exact provisioning command's flag syntax.
  • No dedicated DQ/quarantine rules were added to either flow — out of scope for what this test case's own detail asks for (decrypt-then-compute correctness), and adding one would have meant inventing an unrelated business rule with no bearing on the encryption/decryption path under test.

docs.title: Test Pipeline: DQ Action warn Non-Blocking Validation (TC-DQ-001)
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md (Module 4, TC-DQ-001), flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Prove that a dq_config rule with action: "warn" is genuinely non-blocking -- a row that fails a "warn" rule still lands in the target table exactly like a passing row. "warn" maps onto a native Lakeflow expectation (expect, not expect_or_drop/expect_or_fail), so the only observable effect of a violation is that it is counted/surfaced in the pipeline's own expectation metrics/event log -- unlike "drop" (TC-DQ-002, filters the row), "fail" (TC-DQ-003, aborts the update), or "quarantine" (TC-DQ-004, this framework's own extension that reroutes the row to a companion table). This scenario also proves the negative case: no <table>_quarantine table is ever created, since quarantine table registration is conditional on at least one rules[] entry having action == "quarantine" (see docs/01_control_metadata_schema.md §5 / docs/17_onboarding_template_reference.md §4.7) -- this spec has none.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Land 10 customer rows (scaled down from TESTING_PLAN.md's 100/15 template to a minimal 10/2, per this pass's "minimal, real, onboardable" convention) as a single plain CSV in /Volumes/{{catalog}}/crm/landing_dq_warn/ -- 2 of the 10 (C003 age 16, C006 age 15) violate the rule under test.
  • One ingestion_flow (df_dq_001_customer_warn_ingest) with source_type: "autoloader" and exactly one dq_config.rules[] entry: {"rule_id": "dq_customer_age_adult_warn", "expression": "age >= 18", "action": "warn"}.
  • cdc_load_strategy: "APPEND" -- this scenario is about DQ action semantics, not CDC behavior, so the simplest load strategy (plain streaming append, no primary_keys) keeps the flow focused on the one thing under test (same convention as TC-ING-001).

docs.title: Inputs

  • sample_data/flowx_testing/crm_usecase/customer_dq_warn.csv (10 rows, columns customer_id, customer_name, age, email) -- new fixture, added alongside this test case's build (see Build notes).
  • notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/03_seed_dq_001_warn_data.py -- a new, dedicated seed notebook (kept separate from 02_seed_flowx_testing_data.py and 03_seed_ing_001_zip_filter_data.py) that provisions the crm/bronze_crm schemas and landing_dq_warn/_schemas Volumes, then copies the fixture CSV directly into the landing Volume (no ZIP handling needed for this scenario).

  • No {{catalog}}.bronze_crm.customer_warn_raw_quarantine table -- dq_config here carries no action: "quarantine" rule, so register_main_and_quarantine_tables never registers one.
  • The pipeline's own expectation metrics (Lakeflow's native per-expectation pass/fail counts, visible in the pipeline's event log / DLT UI) show 2 failing records against dq_customer_age_adult_warn out of 10 evaluated.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Prove that a dq_config rule with action: "drop" silently filters a violating row out of the stream -- the row never lands in the target table, no companion _quarantine table is ever created, and the pipeline update itself does not fail. "drop" maps onto a native Lakeflow expectation (expect_or_drop, not expect/expect_or_fail), so unlike "warn" (TC-DQ-001, docs/50_tc_dq_001.md, row still lands) or "fail" (TC-DQ-003, aborts the update) or "quarantine" (TC-DQ-004, this framework's own extension that reroutes the row to a companion table), a "drop" violation leaves no trace in the target table or in any additional control-table-registered object at all. This scenario also proves the negative case: no <table>_quarantine table is ever created, since quarantine table registration is conditional on at least one rules[] entry having action == "quarantine" (see docs/01_control_metadata_schema.md §5 / docs/17_onboarding_template_reference.md §4.7) -- this spec has none.

docs.title: Test Pipeline: DQ Action fail Pipeline Execution Abort (TC-DQ-003)
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md (Module 4, TC-DQ-003), flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Prove that a dq_config rule with action: "fail" genuinely aborts the Lakeflow pipeline update the moment a violating row is encountered -- the strictest of the four DQ actions. "fail" maps onto a native Lakeflow expect_or_fail expectation, unlike "warn" (TC-DQ-001, non-blocking), "drop" (TC-DQ-002, silently filters the row), or "quarantine" (TC-DQ-004, this framework's own extension that reroutes the row to a companion table). This is the one DQ action where the pipeline update itself is expected to end in a FAILED state -- that is this test case's correct, intended outcome, not a defect to fix.

This test case is deliberately designed to fail its own pipeline run. Anyone re-running flowx_test_dq_003_fail_job and seeing the run_pipeline task end in FAILED (with a Lakeflow expectation-violation / ExpectationViolationException-style error referencing dq_accounts_account_id_not_null_fail) is seeing this scenario work exactly as designed.

  • cdc_load_strategy: "APPEND" -- this scenario is about DQ action semantics, not CDC behavior, so the simplest load strategy (plain streaming append, no primary_keys) keeps the flow focused on the one thing under test (same convention as TC-DQ-001/TC-ING-001).

  • {{catalog}}.bronze_banking.accounts_strict_raw is never successfully materialized with data by a run of this fixture -- a failed expect_or_fail update does not commit the streaming table's contents for that run.   • No {{catalog}}.bronze_banking.accounts_strict_raw_quarantine table -- dq_config here carries no action: "quarantine" rule, so register_main_and_quarantine_tables never registers one.

docs.title: Test Pipeline: DQ Action quarantine Routing & Diagnostics (TC-DQ-004)
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md (Module 4, TC-DQ-004), flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Prove that a dq_config rule with action: "quarantine" -- this framework's own extension, with no native Lakeflow equivalent -- genuinely reroutes a failing row to a companion <table>_quarantine table enriched with diagnostic columns, while a passing row proceeds downstream into the main target table untouched. This scenario deliberately exercises two independent quarantine-action rules on the same flow (Country IS NOT NULL, an Email format check), unlike TC-DQ-001/002/003's single-rule builds, to prove __framework_dq_failed_rule_ids correctly enumerates which rule(s) a given row failed, not merely that it failed some rule. Companion to docs/50_tc_dq_001.md ("warn") -- "drop" (TC-DQ-002) and "fail" (TC-DQ-003) remain Not Started as of this build (see TESTING_STATUS.md).

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Land 10 customer rows (scaled down from TESTING_PLAN.md's 85/10/5 template to a minimal 8/1/1, per this pass's "minimal, real, onboardable" convention) as a single plain CSV in /Volumes/{{catalog}}/test/landing_dq_quarantine/ -- 1 of the 10 (CUST006) has a null Country, 1 (CUST007) has a malformed Email, the other 8 are fully valid.
  • One ingestion_flow (df_dq_004_customer_quarantine_ingest) with source_type: "autoloader" and exactly two dq_config.rules[] entries, both action: "quarantine": dq_customer_country_not_null (Country IS NOT NULL) and dq_customer_email_format_valid (Email IS NOT NULL AND Email RLIKE '^[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}$').
  • record_id_column: "CustomerID" -- surfaced as __framework_record_id on quarantined rows, so a failing row's original business key survives into the quarantine table for diagnostics.
  • cdc_load_strategy: "APPEND" -- this scenario is about DQ quarantine-routing semantics, not CDC behavior, so the simplest load strategy (plain streaming append, no primary_keys) keeps the flow focused on the one thing under test (same convention as TC-DQ-001).
  • Reuses scenario 100's exact dq_config shape (rules[] + quarantine_table + record_id_column, following its Country_not_null rule pattern almost verbatim) rather than inventing a new one -- per this build's own instruction to treat scenario 100 as the reference quarantine implementation.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• flowx_testing/032_dq_004_quarantine.json -- single-ingestion-flow onboarding spec (no transformation_flows/reconciliation_flows).
  • sample_data/flowx_testing/crm_usecase/customer_dq_quarantine.csv (10 rows, columns CustomerID, CustomerName, Country, Email) -- new fixture, added alongside this test case's build (see Build notes).
  • notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/03_seed_dq_004_quarantine_data.py -- a new, dedicated seed notebook (kept separate from every other 03_seed_* notebook) that provisions the test/bronze_test schemas and landing_dq_quarantine/_schemas Volumes, then copies the fixture CSV directly into the landing Volume (no ZIP handling needed for this scenario).

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• {{catalog}}.bronze_test.customer_raw -- exactly 8 rows (the 8 fully-valid customers).
  • {{catalog}}.bronze_test.customer_raw_quarantine -- exactly 2 rows (CUST006, CUST007), auto-generated because at least one rules[] entry has action == "quarantine" (see docs/01_control_metadata_schema.md §5). Each row carries a populated __framework_dq_failed_rule_ids (naming exactly the one rule it failed -- these two fixture rows each fail only one of the two rules, not both) and a populated __framework_record_id (the row's own CustomerID).

docs.text:
flowx_testing/032_dq_004_quarantine.json's one ingestion_flows[] entry:

"source_config": {
  "path": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/test/landing_dq_quarantine/",
  "format": "csv",
  "schema_location": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/test/_schemas/customer_quarantine/",
  "reader_options": {"header": "true", "cloudFiles.inferColumnTypes": "true"},
  "capture_technical_metadata": true
},
"target_config": {"cdc_load_strategy": "APPEND", "storage_format": "delta"},
"dq_config": {
  "rules": [
    {"rule_id": "dq_customer_country_not_null", "expression": "Country IS NOT NULL", "action": "quarantine"},
    {"rule_id": "dq_customer_email_format_valid", "expression": "Email IS NOT NULL AND Email RLIKE '^[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\\.[A-Za-z]{2,}$'", "action": "quarantine"}
  ],
  "quarantine_table": "customer_raw_quarantine",
  "record_id_column": "CustomerID"
}

-- expect: 8

-- quarantine table: exactly the 2 failing rows, with diagnostics populated

FROM {catalog}.bronze_test.customer_raw_quarantine
ORDER BY __framework_record_id;
-- expect: CUST006 -> ["dq_customer_country_not_null"]
--         CUST007 -> ["dq_customer_email_format_valid"]

SELECT count(*) FROM {catalog}.bronze_test.customer_raw_quarantine;
-- expect: 2

docs.title: Build notes / judgment calls
docs.text:
• New fixture, not a reuse. No existing seeded fixture carries both Country and Email columns together (checked sample_data/flowx_testing/crm_usecase/customer_data.csv, customer_dq_warn.csv, the various sample_customer_*.csv files, and the wide-customer SCD1 fixtures), so one new 10-row CSV (customer_dq_quarantine.csv) and one new dedicated seed notebook were added, reusing the existing crm_usecase/ fixture directory rather than creating a new one.
  • Scaled down from the plan's 85/10/5 to 8/1/1. Per this build pass's explicit convention (a working, onboardable test case matters more than exhaustive row volume), 10 rows with 1 null-Country violation and 1 malformed-Email violation exercise the same two-rule quarantine-routing assertion as 85/10/5 would, just with a trivially-checkable row count.
  • A real, unresolved naming collision, flagged rather than silently avoided. TESTING_PLAN.md's own "Databricks Object Names" column for TC-DQ-004 names the target as {{catalog}}.bronze_test.customer_raw (+ customer_raw_quarantine) -- the exact same catalog.schema.table coordinates the pre-existing, already-deployed flowx_test_100_zipcsv_pipeline scenario already uses for its own customer_raw (a different dataflow_group_id, different pipeline, and a different source schema: CustomerID/Country/SignupDate there vs. CustomerID/CustomerName/Country/Email here). Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines tie a streaming table's ownership to the specific pipeline that created it -- two independent pipelines targeting the same three-part table name in the same catalog will conflict the moment both have actually run once (whichever runs second will fail claiming the table). This build follows the TC's own literal spec (and reuses scenario 100's exact quarantine-config pattern, per this task's own instruction) rather than unilaterally renaming the target table to something collision-free, since resolving cross-scenario physical conflicts across the full 45-test-case matrix is explicitly this project's later, centralized deployment phase's job, not an individual test-case build's. In practice: only one of flowx_test_100_zipcsv_pipeline / flowx_test_dq_004_quarantine_pipeline can be run against a given catalog's bronze_test.customer_raw at a time until that centralized phase either renames one target or resolves the conflict some other way.
  • quarantine_table/record_id_column both set explicitly. Unlike TC-DQ-001 (no quarantine-action rule, so both fields were correctly omitted there), this spec has two quarantine-action rules, so both fields are populated here per docs/17_onboarding_template_reference.md §4.7.

docs.title: Test Pipeline: Column-Level AES-GCM Encryption with Random IV (TC-SEC-001)
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md (Module 5, TC-SEC-001), flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md, 16_encryption_and_secrets.md, 01_control_metadata_schema.md §4.3.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Prove that target_config.encrypted_columns genuinely encrypts sensitive PII columns with AES-GCM before a target table is ever materialized -- not just that the framework claims to encrypt them, but that:

  1. The physical bytes stored on disk for ssn/credit_card are real AES-GCM ciphertext (BINARY), never the plaintext values that were landed.
  2. That ciphertext genuinely decrypts back to the exact original plaintext when the correct key is supplied -- a real round trip, not merely a "doesn't look like plaintext" check (see 16_encryption_and_secrets.md's own history: the project's original encryption test only ever checked "not plaintext" and missed a real ciphertext corruption bug for months as a result).
  3. This all works using the project's existing {{catalog}}.security.pii_encryption_key Unity Catalog secret -- the same one spec_08/spec_20/spec_22/spec_24 and the onboarding template already rely on -- with no new secret scope or key provisioned.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• One ingestion_flow (df_sec_001_customer_pii_ingest), source_type: "autoloader", plain CSV, landing a 3-row raw customer PII fixture with target_config.cdc_load_strategy: "APPEND" -- the simplest possible strategy, so this scenario stays scoped purely to encrypted_columns's own behavior and never entangles with CDC/hash-column concerns (APPEND never gets __framework_hash_key/__framework_hash_value at all, so there is no risk of accidentally violating 16_encryption_and_secrets.md's explicit warning to never put an encrypted column in columns_to_check/an SCD comparison set).
  • target_config.encrypted_columns encrypts both ssn and credit_card, each with mode: "GCM" (AES-GCM's random-IV mode -- the default and recommended mode), keyed off {secret_catalog: "{{catalog}}", secret_schema: "security", secret_key: "pii_encryption_key"}.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• flowx_testing/033_sec_001_aes_encrypt.json -- single-ingestion-flow onboarding spec (no transformation_flows/reconciliation_flows).
  • sample_data/flowx_testing/sec_usecase/customer_pii_day1.csv (3 rows) -- hand-authored; customer_id, customer_name, ssn, credit_card (well-known dummy card numbers -- the standard Visa/Mastercard/Amex test-number patterns, not real card data).
  • notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/03_seed_sec_001_aes_encrypt_data.py -- a new, dedicated seed notebook (kept separate from every other scenario's own seed notebook) that provisions the customers schema and landing_pii/_schemas Volumes, then lands the fixture in /Volumes/{{catalog}}/customers/landing_pii/incoming/.
  • Requires the {{catalog}}.security.pii_encryption_key Unity Catalog secret to already exist (see 05_deployment_guide.md §0 prerequisites) -- this scenario deliberately reuses it rather than provisioning anything new; the seed notebook does not provision it, exactly like every other encryption scenario in this project.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: • {{catalog}}.bronze_customers.customer_pii_encrypted -- 3 rows. ssn/credit_card are BINARY AES-GCM ciphertext; customer_id/customer_name/__framework_ingestion_timestamp_utc (and the other capture_technical_metadata columns) remain plain, untouched values -- only the two configured columns are ever encrypted. No __framework_hash_key/__framework_hash_value (not CDC-dispatched -- APPEND never gets them).

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
flowx_testing/033_sec_001_aes_encrypt.json's one ingestion_flows[] entry:

"source_config": {
  "path": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/customers/landing_pii/incoming/",
  "format": "csv",
  "schema_location": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/customers/_schemas/customer_pii_encrypted/",
  "reader_options": {"header": "true", "cloudFiles.inferColumnTypes": "true"},
  "capture_technical_metadata": true
},
"target_config": {
  "cdc_load_strategy": "APPEND",
  "storage_format": "delta",
  "encrypted_columns": [
    {
      "column_name": "ssn",
      "output_column": "ssn",
      "mode": "GCM",
      "secret": {"secret_catalog": "{{catalog}}", "secret_schema": "security", "secret_key": "pii_encryption_key"}
    },
    {
      "column_name": "credit_card",
      "output_column": "credit_card",
      "mode": "GCM",
      "secret": {"secret_catalog": "{{catalog}}", "secret_schema": "security", "secret_key": "pii_encryption_key"}
    }
  ]
},
"dq_config": {"rules": []}

Target: {{catalog}}.bronze_customers.customer_pii_encrypted, target_type: "streaming_table".

docs.title: Main execution flow
docs.text:
databricks bundle deploy --target dev
databricks bundle run flowx_test_sec_001_aes_encrypt_job --target dev

Task chain: setup_control_tables -> seed_sec_001_aes_encrypt_data -> onboard_sec_001 -> run_pipeline.

docs.title: Expected results — simulation notes
docs.text:
SQL assertion 1 -- stored values are non-plaintext ciphertext (replace {catalog} with your actual target catalog):

SELECT
  customer_id,
  typeof(ssn)          AS ssn_type,
  base64(ssn)          AS ssn_ciphertext_base64,
  typeof(credit_card)  AS credit_card_type,
  base64(credit_card)  AS credit_card_ciphertext_base64
FROM {catalog}.bronze_customers.customer_pii_encrypted
ORDER BY customer_id;
-- expect: ssn_type = 'binary', credit_card_type = 'binary' for every row; the base64 ciphertext
-- values bear no resemblance to the landed plaintext ("123-45-6789", "4111111111111111", ...)
-- and differ in length/content from each other despite the source values being short/similar.

Round-trip decrypt verification -- a PySpark snippet, not a raw SQL query, and deliberately so. A plain SQL aes_decrypt(ssn, secret('security', 'pii_encryption_key'), 'GCM') query would be wrong on two independent counts documented in 16_encryption_and_secrets.md §2: the SQL secret() function only resolves a classic workspace-level scope and cannot address this project's genuine three-level Unity Catalog secret at all, and — independently — a live-confirmed Databricks redaction bug corrupts any ciphertext produced by a query whose text contains a literal secret(...) call. crypto/column_crypto.py itself sidesteps both by resolving the key via dbutils.secrets.get(catalog=, schema=, key=) and passing it to aes_decrypt/aes_encrypt as a literal Column, never as SQL text -- the verification below mirrors that exact, already-proven-correct pattern instead of reintroducing a broken one:

from pyspark.sql import functions as F

pii_key = dbutils.secrets.get(catalog="flowx", schema="security", key="pii_encryption_key")

verify_df = (
    spark.table("flowx.bronze_customers.customer_pii_encrypted")
    .withColumn("ssn_plaintext", F.aes_decrypt(F.col("ssn"), F.lit(pii_key), F.lit("GCM")).cast("string"))
    .withColumn("credit_card_plaintext", F.aes_decrypt(F.col("credit_card"), F.lit(pii_key), F.lit("GCM")).cast("string"))
    .select("customer_id", "ssn_plaintext", "credit_card_plaintext")
    .orderBy("customer_id")
)
verify_df.show(truncate=False)
# expect:
# CUST001 | 123-45-6789 | 4111111111111111
# CUST002 | 234-56-7890 | 5500000000000004
# CUST003 | 345-67-8901 | 340000000000009

docs.title: Build notes / judgment calls
docs.text:
• Secret name follows the task's own instruction and this repo's real, already-provisioned secret, not TESTING_PLAN.md's placeholder names. TESTING_PLAN.md's own TC-SEC-001 row names a flowx_sec_scope/aes_gcm_256_key secret scope/key that doesn't exist anywhere else in this project -- every real encryption spec already built (spec_08, spec_20, spec_22, spec_24, the onboarding template) uses the one shared {secret_catalog, secret_schema, secret_key} = {"{{catalog}}", "security", "pii_encryption_key"} reference, provisioned once per 05_deployment_guide.md §0. This build reuses that existing secret, per the task's own explicit instruction, rather than inventing a second, redundant one.
  • New fixture, not a reuse. sample_data/sample_customer_pii_encryption.csv already exists, but it's shaped for the crypto_abac_exhaustive suite's own GCM/CBC/ECB-mode comparison (account_id/region_code/ssn_for_gcm/ssn_for_cbc/ssn_for_ecb/ssn_for_override) -- not the customer_id/ssn/credit_card shape this test case asks for. A small, new 3-row CSV fixture and one dedicated seed notebook were added instead, following this project's established one-scenario-one-seed-notebook convention (e.g. docs/42_tc_cdc_003.md).
  • cdc_load_strategy: "APPEND", not an SCD strategy. TESTING_PLAN.md's own row only asks to prove encryption-at-rest, not a CDC strategy; APPEND keeps this scenario scoped purely to encrypted_columns's own behavior and sidesteps 16_encryption_and_secrets.md's explicit warning never to put an encrypted column in an SCD comparison set.
  • No run_observability_task. TESTING_PLAN.md's "Proposed Pipeline & Job Architecture" column names a second run_observability_task step, but -- per this project's own real, established convention across every TC-* build so far (e.g. docs/42_tc_cdc_003.md) -- observability is opt-in via a spec's own observability[] array plus a separate job, never wired into every scenario's job by default. This build follows the real setup_control_tables -> seed -> onboard -> run_pipeline convention instead.
  • Round-trip verification is a PySpark snippet, not a plain SQL query. See "Expected results" above for the full reasoning -- a raw SQL aes_decrypt(..., secret(...), ...) query would be wrong twice over (wrong resolution function for a UC secret, and a live redaction bug), so this doc documents the same dbutils.secrets.get() + F.aes_decrypt pattern crypto/column_crypto.py itself uses, rather than a query shape known not to work correctly in this project.
  • original_data_type tag cross-check not exercised. This scenario has no transformation_flows/decrypted_columns, so 16_encryption_and_secrets.md §4's not-yet-wired original_data_type cross-check never comes into play here -- noted for completeness, not a gap specific to this build.

docs.title: Test Pipeline: SHA-256 Hash Key & Value Determinism (TC-SEC-002)
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md (Module 5, TC-SEC-002), flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md, 02_cdc_load_strategies.md § The hash-key/hash-value framework, 01_control_metadata_schema.md §4a.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Prove that __framework_hash_key/__framework_hash_value generation is genuinely deterministic and reproducible for a composite primary key, end to end against a real, persisted target table:

  1. __framework_hash_key is exactly sha2(concat_ws('||', region, account_id), 256) for every row -- not an approximation, not order-dependent, not something that only holds for a single-column key.
  2. A composite key actually matters. The same account_id (ACC001) recurs under 3 different region values in the fixture; a hash keyed on account_id alone would incorrectly collide these into "the same logical row," while the real composite-key hash gives each (region, account_id) pair its own distinct __framework_hash_key.
  3. __framework_hash_value is populated (non-NULL) whenever the resolved comparison-column set is non-empty, and is stable for rows whose comparison columns don't change.

docs.title: Where this is actually implemented (read before building or debugging this scenario)
docs.text:
__framework_hash_key/__framework_hash_value are not a reconciliation-only feature. Confirmed by reading both modules in full this pass:

  • cdc/hashing.py::compute_hash_columns is the sole place either column is computed -- __framework_hash_key = sha2(concat_ws('||', <coalesced-to-string, ordered primary_keys>), 256), __framework_hash_value = the same construction over the resolved comparison-column set (or a constant NULL when that set is empty).
  • dq/quarantine.py::_apply_hash_and_surrogate_key_columns is the only call site for an ingestion/transformation flow, invoked unconditionally for any CDC-dispatched strategy (SCD1/SCD2/SCD3/FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC/FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC_NO_PK) whenever target_config.generate_hash_columns resolves truthy (default true) -- gated only by needs_cdc_dispatch, not by anything reconciliation-specific. This runs on the clean (quarantine-filtered) upstream, before dlt.apply_changes/apply_changes_from_snapshot ever sees the data, so every row that lands in the real target table already carries both columns.
  • reconciliation/matcher.py consumes these columns (via hash_precomputed: true) or recomputes them inline for its own join -- it is a second, independent caller of the exact same cdc/hashing.py::compute_hash_columns function, not the place hash generation "lives." A reconciliation flow's own prepare_dataset_for_matching only ever materializes hash columns into an append_target_table for rows it actually appends (missing/drifted records) -- never for every row of a real target table the way a CDC-dispatched ingestion flow does.

Build decision: this scenario is a plain ingestion_flow (SCD1), not a reconciliation_flow. A genuine CDC-dispatched ingestion flow is the more direct, minimal, and verifiable exercise of the real hash-generation code path (dq/quarantine.py -> cdc/hashing.py) -- every row of the persisted {{catalog}}.silver_accounts.accounts_hashed table gets __framework_hash_key/__framework_hash_value, which is exactly what "verify __framework_hash_key equals sha2(...) for every row via direct SQL comparison" needs. A reconciliation-flow-only version would not materialize hash columns on every row of a real table (only on the subset it appends), making a "for every row" SQL assertion structurally impossible to satisfy that way.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Land a small accounts feed (single batch) with a genuine composite business key: region + account_id. ACC001 recurs under US/EU/APAC; ACC002 recurs under US/EU.
  • One ingestion_flow (df_sec_002_accounts_hashed_ingest) with source_type: "autoloader", plain CSV format, cdc_load_strategy: "SCD1", primary_keys: ["region", "account_id"], generate_hash_columns: true (explicit, though it's already the default for any CDC-dispatched strategy -- set here for clarity in a scenario dedicated to this exact feature).

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• flowx_testing/034_sec_002_hashing.json -- single-ingestion-flow onboarding spec (no transformation_flows/reconciliation_flows).
  • sample_data/flowx_testing/sec_usecase/accounts_hashed_batch1.csv (6 rows) -- hand-authored (no generator script needed for a fixture this small).
  • notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/03_seed_sec_002_hashing_data.py -- a new, dedicated seed notebook (kept separate from every other scenario's own seed notebook) that provisions the sec_accounts schema and landing_accounts/_schemas Volumes, then lands the fixture in /Volumes/{{catalog}}/sec_accounts/landing_accounts/incoming/.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• {{catalog}}.silver_accounts.accounts_hashed -- 6 rows (SCD1 with 6 distinct (region, account_id) composite keys, so every row is a distinct upsert, not an overwrite).
  • __framework_hash_key/__framework_hash_value columns present on every row (SCD1 is CDC-dispatched; generate_hash_columns is set explicitly true, matching the default).
  • delta.enableChangeDataFeed = true on the target (every CDC-dispatched target gets this -- incidental to this scenario, not itself under test here).

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
flowx_testing/034_sec_002_hashing.json's one ingestion_flows[] entry:

"source_config": {
  "path": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/sec_accounts/landing_accounts/incoming/",
  "format": "csv",
  "schema_location": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/sec_accounts/_schemas/accounts_hashed/",
  "reader_options": {"header": "true", "cloudFiles.inferColumnTypes": "true"},
  "capture_technical_metadata": true
},
"target_config": {
  "cdc_load_strategy": "SCD1",
  "primary_keys": ["region", "account_id"],
  "sequence_by_column": "updated_at",
  "generate_hash_columns": true,
  "storage_format": "delta"
},
"dq_config": {"rules": []}

Target: {{catalog}}.silver_accounts.accounts_hashed, target_type: "streaming_table" (SCD1 always ends up backed by a genuine Streaming Table for its real storage -- see 02_cdc_load_strategies.md).

columns_to_check/columns_to_exclude are both left unset, so __framework_hash_value is computed over every applicable non-key, non-technical column resolved at execution time (account_name, balance, status, updated_at) -- see 02_cdc_load_strategies.md § Comparison vs. storage.

docs.title: Main execution flow
docs.text:
databricks bundle deploy --target dev
databricks bundle run flowx_test_sec_002_hashing_job --target dev

Task chain: setup_control_tables -> seed_sec_002_hashing_data -> onboard_sec_002 -> run_pipeline.

docs.title: Expected results — simulation notes
docs.text:
SQL assertions (after a run, replace {catalog} with your actual target catalog):

-- Row count: 6 distinct (region, account_id) composite keys, all upserted
SELECT count(*) FROM {catalog}.silver_accounts.accounts_hashed;
-- expect: 6

-- Determinism: __framework_hash_key equals sha2(concat_ws('||', region, account_id), 256)
-- for EVERY row, via direct SQL recomputation -- this is the scenario's core assertion.
SELECT count(*) AS mismatched_rows
FROM {catalog}.silver_accounts.accounts_hashed
WHERE __framework_hash_key <> sha2(concat_ws('||', region, account_id), 256);
-- expect: 0

-- Composite key genuinely matters: the same account_id under different regions gets a
-- distinct hash_key each time (not collapsed to one row/one hash).
SELECT region, account_id, __framework_hash_key
FROM {catalog}.silver_accounts.accounts_hashed
WHERE account_id = 'ACC001'
ORDER BY region;
-- expect: 3 rows (APAC/EU/US), 3 distinct __framework_hash_key values

-- __framework_hash_value is populated (comparison-column set is non-empty here)
SELECT count(*) AS null_hash_value_rows
FROM {catalog}.silver_accounts.accounts_hashed
WHERE __framework_hash_value IS NULL;
-- expect: 0
