docs.title: Build notes / judgment calls
docs.text:
• Built as an ingestion_flow, not a reconciliation_flow -- see "Where this is actually implemented" above for the precise code-reading that led to this choice: hash-column generation is a CDC-dispatch-time feature (dq/quarantine.py/cdc/hashing.py), independent of and prior to reconciliation; reconciliation only ever consumes or re-derives the same columns, and only for a subset of rows (its own append set), which cannot satisfy a "for every row" assertion against a real, fully-materialized target table.
  • New fixture, not a reuse. No existing seeded fixture carries a (region, account_id) composite-key shape with a deliberately recurring account_id across regions, so 1 small new CSV fixture (6 rows) and 1 new dedicated seed notebook were added, kept separate from every other scenario's own seed notebook and fixtures (including TC-SEC-001's own sec_usecase fixture, customer_pii_day1.csv, which this scenario's fixture sits alongside without overlapping).
  • SCD1 chosen over SCD2/FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC. Any of the five CDC-dispatched strategies would exercise the identical hash-generation code path (_apply_hash_and_surrogate_key_columns doesn't branch on which strategy triggered it); SCD1 is the simplest to reason about for a single-batch, no-history determinism check, and needs no delete-marker/history-column noise.
  • No DQ rules, no governance tags, no encryption. This scenario is scoped to hash-key/value determinism; DQ (TC-DQ-*), governance (TC-GOV-*), and encryption (TC-SEC-001/TC-SEC-003) are separate, already-tracked test modules with their own dedicated rows in TESTING_PLAN.md.

docs.title: Test Pipeline: Secret Masking & Redaction in Telemetry (TC-SEC-003)
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md (Module 5, TC-SEC-003), flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md, 16_encryption_and_secrets.md (the full AES/PGP secret-resolution design, including §2's own account of the redaction mechanics this test exercises), 23_lakeflow_sinks.md (sink_config/pgp_zip mechanics), 54_tc_sec_001.md (the AES encrypted_columns config this scenario reuses verbatim), 63_tc_snk_003.md (the PGP sink_config config this scenario reuses verbatim, and the job-architecture convention this scenario follows).

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Verify that an encryption key resolved via dbutils.secrets.get() is genuinely never exposed in plaintext anywhere this framework's own telemetry surfaces reach — this project's own structured JSON logs, and the Spark driver/query-plan diagnostics a pipeline update produces. Read this whole document before treating a clean job run as a pass: per this session's own explicit instructions, this build is deliberately NOT written to paper over a real, already-investigated, NOT-yet-fixed gap in crypto/column_crypto.py — see "Expected results" below for exactly what is and isn't actually redacted today, and why.

One ingestion flow does double duty, exercising both secret-handling code paths this project has in one pipeline update:

  1. target_config.encrypted_columns AES-GCM-encrypts secret_value before {{catalog}}.bronze_sec.secrets_audit_raw is ever materialized, keyed off the SAME {{catalog}}.security.pii_encryption_key UC secret TC-SEC-001/ TC-TRF-003 already reuse. Resolution happens in crypto/column_crypto.py::apply_aes_column_encryption, on the pipeline driver, at graph-definition time.
  2. target_config.sink_config (target_type: "external_sink", format pgp_zip) additionally PGP-exports that same, already-ciphertext row set as a .zip.pgp archive, keyed off the SAME {{catalog}}.security.pgp_public_key_finance_egress_test UC secret TC-SNK-003 already provisions. Resolution happens in engine/sink_registration.py::_resolve_secret_into_options, also on the driver, also at graph-definition time — see 16_encryption_and_secrets.md §6.

Both are genuine, already-built, real configs from sibling test cases — this scenario does not invent a new encryption/PGP mechanism, only combines the two on one flow specifically to give the redaction assertion below two independent secret-handling code paths to inspect side by side.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• One ingestion flow (df_sec_003_secrets_audit_ingest), source_type: "autoloader", cdc_load_strategy: "APPEND" — deliberately the simplest possible CDC strategy (same reasoning as TC-SEC-001/TC-SNK-003): APPEND never touches columns_to_check/hash comparison at all, so there is no risk of violating 16_encryption_and_secrets.md's explicit warning never to put an encrypted (random-IV) column in a change-comparison set, and APPEND + autoloader still publishes a genuine Lakeflow Streaming Table, which target_type: "external_sink" requires of its main table (see 23_lakeflow_sinks.md).
  • target_type: "external_sink" — {{catalog}}.bronze_sec.secrets_audit_raw is materialized as a real, governed, DQ-quarantined table exactly like any other target type, plus a second @dlt.append_flow reads that same table (dlt.read_stream) into dlt.create_sink(format="pgp_zip", ...) — the single target this test case's own instructions name (flowx.bronze_sec.secrets_audit_raw), with the PGP export as an additional side effect of the SAME flow rather than a second, separate transformation flow.
  • target_config.encrypted_columns encrypts secret_value (mode: "GCM"), the one column in this fixture standing in for genuine credential/API-key material.
  • target_config.sink_config.post_export_archive.pgp_encryption is recipient_public_key_secret only (no sign_with_private_key_secret, no AES post_export_archive.secret ZIP password) — the exact same shape TC-SNK-003 already exercises, reused as-is rather than extended, so this scenario's PGP leg is not itself a new thing under test.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• flowx_testing/035_sec_003_redaction.json — the onboarding spec (one ingestion flow, no transformation/reconciliation flows).
  • sample_data/flowx_testing/sec_usecase/secrets_audit_batch1.csv — 5-row plaintext fixture (audit_id, secret_name, secret_value, accessed_by, accessed_at, access_reason) — a small, synthetic credential-vault access-audit log; every secret_name/secret_value is a clearly fake, example-shaped placeholder (AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE, sk_live_51Hc...EXAMPLE..., etc. — the same "well-known dummy value" convention TC-SEC-001 already established for ssn/credit_card), never real credential material.
  • notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/03_seed_sec_003_redaction_data.py — a new, dedicated seed notebook that provisions the sec landing schema/Volumes, the egress_sec schema + PGP-sink staging/output Volumes (a sink's destination Volume is never auto-created by the pipeline itself — see TC-SNK-003), and lands the fixture CSV.
  • Requires TWO Unity Catalog secrets to already exist, both reused verbatim, neither provisioned by this test case:
  • {{catalog}}.security.pii_encryption_key — see 05_deployment_guide.md §0 prerequisites.
  • {{catalog}}.security.pgp_public_key_finance_egress_test — provisioned by flowx_test_snk_003_pgp_zip_sink_job (see TC-SNK-003) from the disposable test keypair at sample_data/flowx_testing/finance_egress_usecase/ pgp_egress_keypair_public.asc. If TC-SNK-003 hasn't been run against a given workspace yet, provision it directly (same command TC-SNK-003's own doc gives): 
    databricks secrets put-secret security pgp_public_key_finance_egress_test \
  --string-value "$(cat sample_data/flowx_testing/finance_egress_usecase/pgp_egress_keypair_public.asc)"

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• {{catalog}}.bronze_sec.secrets_audit_raw — 5 rows; secret_value is BINARY AES-GCM ciphertext, never the plaintext values landed; audit_id/secret_name/accessed_by/ accessed_at/access_reason (and the usual __framework_* technical metadata columns) remain plain, untouched values.
  • /Volumes/{catalog}/egress_sec/audit_zips_export/secrets_audit_<batch_id>.zip.pgp — one PGP-encrypted archive per micro-batch, containing the already-ciphertext row set (the export @dlt.append_flow reads from the already-materialized main table, so secret_value is ciphertext in the exported archive too — a double-encrypted column, by construction, never a plaintext leak on the egress side).
  • Driver-side structured JSON log lines (observability/structured_logger.py::log_flow_event, emitted from logged_operation wrapping flow_registration/sink_registration) for this flow's flow_registration/sink_registration operations — metadata only (flow_id, status, record counts, duration_ms, sink_format, target_type, etc.); see "Expected results" for why this specific surface is not where this test case's real exposure lives.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
flowx_testing/035_sec_003_redaction.json's one ingestion_flows[] entry's target_config:

"target_config": {
  "cdc_load_strategy": "APPEND",
  "storage_format": "delta",
  "encrypted_columns": [
    {
      "column_name": "secret_value",
      "output_column": "secret_value",
      "mode": "GCM",
      "secret": {"secret_catalog": "{{catalog}}", "secret_schema": "security", "secret_key": "pii_encryption_key"}
    }
  ],
  "sink_config": {
    "path": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/egress_sec/audit_zips/_staging/",
    "format": "pgp_zip",
    "post_export_archive": {
      "enabled": true,
      "output_zip_path": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/egress_sec/audit_zips_export/",
      "export_file_name_format": "secrets_audit_{batch_id}",
      "pgp_encryption": {
        "enabled": true,
        "recipient_public_key_secret": {"secret_catalog": "{{catalog}}", "secret_schema": "security", "secret_key": "pgp_public_key_finance_egress_test"}
      }
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Main execution flow
docs.text:
databricks bundle deploy --target dev
# only if not already provisioned by an earlier TC-SNK-003 run in this workspace:
databricks secrets put-secret security pgp_public_key_finance_egress_test \
  --string-value "$(cat sample_data/flowx_testing/finance_egress_usecase/pgp_egress_keypair_public.asc)"
databricks bundle run flowx_test_sec_003_redaction_job --target dev

Task chain: setup_control_tables → seed_sec_003_redaction_data → onboard_sec_003 → run_pipeline. No separate observability job task — see "Known gaps / judgment calls".

docs.title: Expected results — this test is expected to FAIL its own core assertion, not pass cleanly
docs.text:
Read this section before running anything. This is not a normal "run the job, check the counts" scenario. TESTING_PLAN.md's own row for TC-SEC-003 asserts: "Grep driver and task logs for secret key string → 0 matches. All secret references display as [REDACTED]." Two genuinely different things happen when that assertion is actually checked against this framework as it exists today, and conflating them is exactly the mistake this doc exists to prevent:

1. This project's own structured JSON logs (log_flow_event/logged_operation) — expected to pass cleanly. By design (observability/structured_logger.py's own docstring), the payload this module ever emits is a fixed set of business-level fields — operation, flow_id, status, record counts, duration_ms, error, plus caller-supplied metadata like sink_format/ target_type/cdc_load_strategy. It never carries column data or a resolved secret value at all — there is no code path by which pii_encryption_key's or pgp_public_key_finance_egress_test's plaintext value could reach one of these JSON lines. A grep of this framework's own driver-log JSON output for either secret's literal value is expected to find zero matches, and resolve_secret_value's own error-path logging (crypto/secrets.py) only ever names the catalog.schema.key label, never the value, even on a resolution failure.

2. Spark's own query-plan/execution-plan surface — expected to FAIL. TESTING_PLAN.md's own wording explicitly includes "execution plans" alongside driver logs, and this is exactly where this framework's current implementation falls short, per a real gap this session investigated and explicitly left open (see crypto/column_crypto.py's own module docstring, and 16_encryption_and_secrets.md §2's "Trade-off this accepts" paragraph — memory: architecture-review-remediation-2026-08, if available):

"This does mean the resolved key value now exists as a Python string on the driver for the duration of one flow's graph-definition call ... an intentional trade against the alternative of encryption being silently non-functional."

apply_aes_column_encryption resolves pii_encryption_key's plaintext value once via resolve_secret_ref, then passes it into F.aes_encrypt(F.col(...), F.lit(resolved_key), F.lit(mode)) — as a literal Column value, not interpolated SQL text. That change was made specifically (and correctly) to fix a different, earlier bug: Databricks' spark.redaction.regex credential-redaction machinery keys off the literal substring secret( appearing in a query's text, and previously corrupted the resulting ciphertext when that substring was present. Avoiding that substring genuinely fixes the corruption bug. It does not, however, make the resolved key value itself invisible. F.lit(resolved_key) embeds that plaintext value directly into the DataFrame's expression tree as a Catalyst Literal node — a basic, verifiable property of how F.lit() works, independent of any redaction mechanism. Nothing in this framework's code path additionally masks a Literal node's displayed value, and spark.redaction.regex's own substring-matching approach has nothing to key off here (there is no secret-named key or config string anywhere near this literal — contrast with sink_registration.py's own _resolve_secret_into_options, which deliberately keeps secret in the option key name precisely so that redaction mechanism still fires for the sink's own diagnostics — see 16_encryption_and_secrets.md §6). Concretely, expect the resolved pii_encryption_key value to appear in plaintext wherever this flow's staged-view DataFrame's plan is ever displayed or captured — a .explain(True)/.explain("formatted") call against the staged view, the Spark UI's SQL/DataFrame execution tab for this flow's update, or a full DEBUG-level Catalyst/driver log capture of the optimized plan.

What this means for the two verification steps below: do not treat a completed job run, or a clean grep of this project's own JSON structured logs, as proof this test case passed. This scenario's honest, complete result is: (a) encryption and PGP export both work correctly (the ciphertext round-trips, the archive decrypts) — functionally this is a passing pipeline; but (b) the "secrets never appear anywhere in telemetry" assertion, taken as broadly as TESTING_PLAN.md states it (driver logs and execution plans), currently fails on the AES leg, specifically because of the gap quoted above. This is the accurate, complete status to record — not a silent pass.

-- Bronze: secret_value is ciphertext, never plaintext (this part is expected to hold)
SELECT secret_name, typeof(secret_value), base64(secret_value)
FROM {catalog}.bronze_sec.secrets_audit_raw ORDER BY audit_id;
-- expect: typeof = 'binary' for every row; base64 output bears no resemblance to the landed
-- plaintext secret_value ("AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE", "sk_live_51Hc...", etc.)

# Egress archive lands with a .zip.pgp extension, containing the already-ciphertext row set
databricks fs ls dbfs:/Volumes/{catalog}/egress_sec/audit_zips_export/
# expect: secrets_audit_<batch_id>.zip.pgp (no bare .zip files)

# This is the check that is expected to demonstrate the gap, not disprove it -- run against the
# pipeline update's own captured plan/DEBUG log, or interactively against the staged view:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F
pii_key = dbutils.secrets.get(catalog="flowx", schema="security", key="pii_encryption_key")
staged_df = spark.table("flowx.bronze_sec.secrets_audit_raw").select(
    F.aes_encrypt(F.lit("probe"), F.lit(pii_key), F.lit("GCM")).alias("probe_col")
)
staged_df.explain(True)
# expect: the printed logical/optimized/physical plan contains the literal pii_key string value
# verbatim inside the aes_encrypt/Literal expression -- reproducing, in miniature, exactly what
# apply_aes_column_encryption's own real call site does inside this flow's graph-definition call.

This pass's actual verification status: see flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md for whether this job was actually run against the live workspace and what the real result was — this document describes what should happen structurally; the status tracker records what did happen.

docs.title: Known gaps / judgment calls
docs.text:
• This test case is built to genuinely surface a known, open gap, not to fake a clean pass. Per this session's own explicit instructions: the spec/resources/fixtures above are built faithfully and are fully deployable, but the "Expected results" section above is written to describe the real, current outcome (encryption/PGP export succeed; the broader no-secret-in-telemetry assertion does not hold for the AES leg's query-plan surface) rather than writing verification steps that would misleadingly suggest full masking already works. Treat any future fix to crypto/column_crypto.py's key-resolution approach (e.g., a genuine per-executor key-derivation scheme that never places the raw key value in a Catalyst Literal) as the trigger to revisit and rewrite this section, not this test case's build itself.
  • Single combined flow, not two. target_config.encrypted_columns and target_config.sink_config coexisting on one target_type: "external_sink" ingestion flow is not explicitly demonstrated elsewhere in this project's existing docs/specs, but nothing in 01_control_metadata_schema.md §4/ 23_lakeflow_sinks.md restricts either field to a particular target_type or to mutual exclusion with the other, and this shape lets one flow satisfy this test case's own single named target (flowx.bronze_sec.secrets_audit_raw) while still genuinely exercising both secret-handling code paths side by side, matching TESTING_PLAN.md's own framing ("Pipeline executes AES encryption and PGP sink packaging") more directly than splitting them across an ingestion flow and a second transformation flow would have.
  • PGP secret reused verbatim from TC-SNK-003, not TESTING_PLAN.md's own placeholder naming. Same pre-existing terminology/naming gap TC-SNK-003 and TC-ING-005 already document — TESTING_PLAN.md's own row doesn't name a secret for TC-SEC-003 at all beyond the ambient "Databricks Secrets" mention, so this build reuses TC-SNK-003's real, already-provisioned {{catalog}}.security.pgp_public_key_finance_egress_test rather than inventing a third PGP keypair/secret for this project to track.
  • No separate run_observability_task. TESTING_PLAN.md's own "Proposed Pipeline & Job Architecture" column names a second task for every TC-* scenario including this one, but — per this project's now-consistent, real, established convention across every already-built scenario (TC-SEC-001, TC-DQ-001, TC-DQ-003, and especially TC-SNK-003, the methodologically closest sibling — see 63_tc_snk_003.md's own "Known gaps" section) — structured JSON logging fires automatically as a side effect of run_pipeline itself, with no separate task needed to "activate" it. This is, in fact, the exact log surface this doc's own "Expected results" section inspects (and finds clean) above.
  • New fixture, not a reuse. sample_data/flowx_testing/sec_usecase/ already holds customer_pii_day1.csv (TC-SEC-001) and accounts_hashed_batch1.csv (TC-SEC-002), but neither is shaped for a credential-vault audit log — a small, new 5-row CSV (secrets_audit_batch1.csv) and one dedicated seed notebook were added instead, under the same sec_usecase/ fixture directory (a genuine, minimal addition, not a new top-level use case directory).
  • egress_sec schema/Volumes are a genuinely new provisioning step, not a reuse of TC-SNK-003's own finance_egress/secure_drops Volumes — kept separate so this scenario's own PGP archives never mix with TC-SNK-003's, even though both flows resolve the exact same recipient public key secret.

docs.title: Test Pipeline: Post-Deployment UC Table & Column Tag Application (TC-GOV-001)
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, 01_control_metadata_schema.md §6, 06_governance_integration.md, flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Prove that governance_tags (table tags + column tags) declared on an onboarding spec are genuinely applied, post-deployment, as real Unity Catalog ALTER TABLE ... SET TAGS/ ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN ... SET TAGS DDL against an already-materialized table -- independent of whether a new Lakeflow pipeline update just wrote that table. This is the "tags-only governance model" documented in 06_governance_integration.md: the framework applies key-value tags; it does not create or bind the Unity Catalog masking/row-filter policy that gives a tag its enforcement behavior.

This scenario deliberately builds no new ingestion pipeline. It re-onboards a new ingestion_flow (its own new dataflow_group_id) that targets scenario 100's already-deployed {{catalog}}.bronze_test.customer_raw table, carrying only governance_tags -- then runs notebooks/04_governance/04_apply_governance_and_egress.py directly, exactly like scenario 100's own job would as its own post-run_pipeline task, just without a pipeline update in front of it this time (the table is already there).

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Reuse {{catalog}}.bronze_test.customer_raw (created by flowx_test_100_zipcsv_pipeline / flowx_test_100_job, per TESTING_STATUS.md's own "Executed -- Pass" entry for scenario 100, most recently re-verified 2026-08-29) as the tag target -- no new table, no new fixture data, no new pipeline.
  • One ingestion_flow (df_gov_001_tagging_customer_raw, under a brand-new dataflow_group_id: "dfg_flowx_gov_001_tagging") whose target_catalog/target_schema/ target_table point at that same bronze_test.customer_raw coordinates, carrying:
  • governance_tags.table_tags: {"domain": "finance", "compliance": "sox"}.
  • governance_tags.column_tags: [{"column": "CustomerID", "tags": {"classification": "restricted", "mask": "PII"}}].
  • A job that onboards this spec (a pure control-table upsert -- dataflow_group_spec/ ingestion_flow_spec rows only, no DLT graph involved) and then calls 04_apply_governance_and_egress.py directly against dataflow_group_id: "dfg_flowx_gov_001_tagging", which loops that group's one active ingestion_flow_spec row and issues the tag DDL against bronze_test.customer_raw.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• flowx_testing/036_gov_001_tagging.json -- single-ingestion-flow onboarding spec (no transformation_flows/reconciliation_flows), reusing scenario 100's own source_config/ target_config shape (autoloader, SCD1, primary_keys: ["CustomerID"]) purely so the spec onboards cleanly -- this flow's source_config/target_config are never actually executed by any pipeline (see Build notes).
  • Depends on {{catalog}}.bronze_test.customer_raw already existing in the target workspace -- i.e. flowx_test_100_job having run at least once already. No seed step of its own.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• system.information_schema.table_tags -- one row each for domain = 'finance' and compliance = 'sox' against {{catalog}}.bronze_test.customer_raw.
  • system.information_schema.column_tags -- one row each for classification = 'restricted' and mask = 'PII' against the CustomerID column of the same table.
  • {{catalog}}.config.dataflow_group_spec / ingestion_flow_spec -- one new row each, under dataflow_group_id = 'dfg_flowx_gov_001_tagging', with governance_tags_json populated. No DLT pipeline is deployed or run against this group -- these rows exist purely so apply_all_governance_tags has a governance_tags_json/target-table triple to read.
  • {{catalog}}.bronze_test.customer_raw itself is untouched data-wise -- same row count, same content as scenario 100 last left it. Only its UC tag metadata changes.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
flowx_testing/036_gov_001_tagging.json's one ingestion_flows[] entry:

"target_catalog": "{{catalog}}",
"target_schema": "bronze_test",
"target_table": "customer_raw",
"target_config": {
  "cdc_load_strategy": "SCD1",
  "primary_keys": ["CustomerID"],
  "generate_hash_columns": true,
  "storage_format": "delta"
},
"dq_config": { "rules": [] },
"governance_tags": {
  "table_tags": { "domain": "finance", "compliance": "sox" },
  "column_tags": [
    { "column": "CustomerID", "tags": { "classification": "restricted", "mask": "PII" } }
  ]
}

resources/flowx_test_gov_001_tagging_job.yml's apply_governance_gov_001 task parameters:

notebook_path: ../notebooks/04_governance/04_apply_governance_and_egress.py
base_parameters:
  catalog: flowx
  dataflow_group_id: dfg_flowx_gov_001_tagging
  apply_abac: "true"
  capture_cdc_change_counts: "false"

capture_cdc_change_counts: "false" deliberately disables this notebook's unrelated Phase 10 SCD/CDC change-count capture for this job -- this scenario is about tag application only, and this flow's dataflow_id was never actually run through a pipeline update, so there is no meaningful "since the last run" change-count story to capture for it.

docs.title: Main execution flow
docs.text:
databricks bundle deploy --target dev
databricks bundle run flowx_test_100_job --target dev          # if not already run at least once
databricks bundle run flowx_test_gov_001_tagging_job --target dev

Task chain: setup_control_tables -> onboard_gov_001 -> apply_governance_gov_001.

docs.title: Expected results — simulation notes
docs.text:
SQL assertions (after a run, replace {catalog} with your actual target catalog):

-- table tags
SELECT tag_name, tag_value
FROM system.information_schema.table_tags
WHERE catalog_name = '{catalog}' AND schema_name = 'bronze_test' AND table_name = 'customer_raw';
-- expect: domain -> finance, compliance -> sox

-- column tags
SELECT column_name, tag_name, tag_value
FROM system.information_schema.column_tags
WHERE catalog_name = '{catalog}' AND schema_name = 'bronze_test' AND table_name = 'customer_raw'
  AND column_name = 'CustomerID';
-- expect: classification -> restricted, mask -> PII

-- data untouched -- same row count as scenario 100 last left it
SELECT count(*) FROM {catalog}.bronze_test.customer_raw;

This pass's actual verification status: see flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md for whether this job was actually run against the live workspace and what the real result was -- this document describes what should happen structurally; the status tracker records what did happen, if anything, each time this scenario is executed. (Per this project's build convention, that tracker is updated centrally in a later phase, not by this build itself.)

docs.title: Build notes / judgment calls
docs.text:
• No new pipeline, by design. TC-GOV-001 is explicitly a tags-application test, not an ingestion test -- per this build's own scope, no resources/flowx_test_gov_001_*_pipeline.yml is created. governance_tags has no dedicated control table and is applied purely as post-deployment DDL (docs/01_control_metadata_schema.md §1/§6), so a pipeline run was never a prerequisite for this scenario to exercise the real code path -- only the target table needs to already exist, which scenario 100's own table already does.
  • Reused scenario 100's customer_raw, not a new flowx_test_dq_004 table. Per this TC's own instructions, flowx_test_dq_004's table was checked first (flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md line for TC-DQ-004: "Partially Covered -- Scenario 100 exercises quarantine routing generally", i.e. no dedicated DQ-004 scenario/spec file exists yet in this repo as of this build), so scenario 100's own already-deployed {{catalog}}.bronze_test.customer_raw (TESTING_STATUS.md: "Executed -- Pass", re-verified 2026-08-29) is the simpler and only currently-real choice.
  • Genuine gap: this makes flowx_test_gov_001_tagging_job dependent on flowx_test_100_job having run at least once first in the shared dev workspace -- there is no job-level depends_on between the two bundle jobs (they're separate resources.jobs entries), so this ordering is a real, undeclared cross-job dependency, not enforced by the bundle itself. Flagged here rather than silently assumed.
  • New dataflow_group_id, not scenario 100's own dfg_zip_csv_dataload. Re-onboarding this flow under scenario 100's own group id would add a second ingestion_flow_spec row targeting the exact same physical table into the group scenario 100's own pipeline (dataflow.group.id: dfg_zip_csv_dataload) actually builds its DAG from -- risking a second, competing DLT node definition for customer_raw the next time that pipeline runs. A dedicated dfg_flowx_gov_001_tagging group id keeps this row completely outside that pipeline's own graph; it exists purely as a governance_tags_json carrier for apply_all_governance_tags to read.
  • source_config/target_config mirror scenario 100's own shape but are never executed. Since this flow is never run through a Lakeflow pipeline (no pipeline resource references dfg_flowx_gov_001_tagging), its source_config.path/target_config.cdc_load_strategy etc. only need to satisfy onboarding-time validation, not describe a real data flow -- they were set to mirror scenario 100's real, working df_zip_csv_file_ingest flow (flowx_testing/100_zipcsv_onbaording.json) for realism and to guarantee they pass spec_validator.py cleanly, not because they do anything at runtime.
  • capture_cdc_change_counts: "false". Left enabled (the notebook's own default), Phase 10 would still run harmlessly (capture_all_scd_change_counts never raises -- a per-flow failure is logged and skipped, per control_plane/post_deployment.py's own docstring) and would, incidentally, capture this table's full change history against this flow's own last_processed_cdc_version watermark. Disabled here to keep this job's scope crisply about governance tagging only, per this TC's own title.

docs.title: Test Pipeline: Governance Tag Application Idempotency (TC-GOV-002)
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md (Module 6, TC-GOV-002), flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md, 06_governance_integration.md (ground truth for the tags-only model this scenario exercises).

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Prove that re-running notebooks/04_governance/04_apply_governance_and_egress.py against a target table that already carries its governance tags is safe: no DDL conflict, no metadata lock contention, no corrupted or duplicated tag state. ALTER TABLE ... SET TAGS / ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN ... SET TAGS is a plain key-value upsert, not a ledgered operation -- see 06_governance_integration.md §4, which is why this framework carries no governance_applied_log control table or governance/idempotency.py module. This scenario is the dedicated, repeated-invocation proof of that design claim: run the exact same tagging pass three times in a row and confirm all three succeed, with the tag values unchanged after the third run.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Re-invoke apply_all_governance_tags (via the same notebook, same widget parameters) three times in strict sequence against the same already-onboarded dataflow group and the same already-materialized target table -- no new spec, no new pipeline, no new fixture data.
  • Each invocation is a full, independent ALTER TABLE ... SET TAGS re-execution (not a ledger-skip) -- the point is that the DDL itself is naturally idempotent, not that the framework detects "already applied" and no-ops.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• No new onboarding spec. This scenario reuses TC-GOV-001's exact same onboarded flow and tags:
  • Catalog: flowx (the {{catalog}} placeholder resolves to this for every resource in this repo)
  • Schema: bronze_crm
  • Target table: customer_raw
  • dataflow_group_id: dfg_gov_001_tagging
  • table_tags: {"domain": "finance", "compliance": "sox"}
  • column_tags: CustomerID -> {"classification": "restricted", "mask": "PII"}

See flowx_test_gov_001_tagging_job.yml / flowx_test_gov_001_tagging_pipeline.yml (TC-GOV-001) for the spec that onboards this group and the pipeline that materializes customer_raw in the first place. * notebooks/04_governance/04_apply_governance_and_egress.py -- unmodified; called with apply_abac/capture_cdc_change_counts left at their coded widget defaults (true/true), same as every other governance invocation.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• Three independent job task runs (apply_governance_run_1/2/3), each expected to end SUCCESS (exit code 0).
  • system.information_schema.table_tags for flowx.bronze_crm.customer_raw -- still exactly domain: finance, compliance: sox after the third run (unchanged from after the first).
  • system.information_schema.column_tags for the same table's CustomerID column -- still exactly classification: restricted, mask: PII after the third run.
  • No new control-table rows anywhere -- governance has no dedicated control table (01_control_metadata_schema.md §1), so "ran 3 times" leaves no ledger artifact to inspect; the only observable effect is the tag state itself, which must be identical before/after.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
resources/flowx_test_gov_002_idempotent_tag_job.yml -- three notebook_task entries, chained depends_on, each calling the identical notebook with the identical base_parameters:

base_parameters:
  catalog: flowx
  dataflow_group_id: dfg_gov_001_tagging

apply_abac and capture_cdc_change_counts are intentionally omitted from base_parameters -- the notebook's own widget defaults ("true"/"true") apply, matching how TC-GOV-001's own job invokes it, so this scenario tests genuine repeat invocation under normal parameters rather than a specially reduced configuration.

docs.title: Main execution flow
docs.text:
databricks bundle deploy --target dev
# TC-GOV-001's own job must have been run at least once first, so customer_raw exists and
# already carries its tags before this job's first task starts:
databricks bundle run flowx_test_gov_001_tagging_job --target dev
databricks bundle run flowx_test_gov_002_idempotent_tag_job --target dev

Task chain: apply_governance_run_1 -> apply_governance_run_2 -> apply_governance_run_3. No setup_control_tables/seed/onboard/pipeline tasks in this job on purpose -- this scenario is scoped narrowly to the tagging task's own repeat-invocation safety, not a re-test of onboarding or pipeline-build behavior (both already covered by TC-GOV-001 and, more generally, TC-ING-001/etc.).

docs.title: Expected results — simulation notes
docs.text:
Execution assertion (per flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md's own row for this test case): all 3 runs return exit code 0; tags remain active and uncorrupted in Unity Catalog.

-- Run before AND after this job, compare results -- expect byte-for-byte identical rows both times.
SELECT tag_name, tag_value
FROM system.information_schema.table_tags
WHERE catalog_name = 'flowx' AND schema_name = 'bronze_crm' AND table_name = 'customer_raw'
ORDER BY tag_name;
-- expect: compliance -> sox, domain -> finance (both times)

SELECT column_name, tag_name, tag_value
FROM system.information_schema.column_tags
WHERE catalog_name = 'flowx' AND schema_name = 'bronze_crm' AND table_name = 'customer_raw'
ORDER BY column_name, tag_name;
-- expect: CustomerID -> classification -> restricted, CustomerID -> mask -> PII (both times)

Job-run assertion: all three tasks (apply_governance_run_1, _run_2, _run_3) show SUCCESS in the Jobs UI / databricks jobs get-run output, with no AbacApplicationError in any task's logs.

This pass's actual verification status: see flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md for whether this job was actually run against the live workspace and what the real result was -- this document describes what should happen structurally; the status tracker records what did happen, if anything, each time this scenario is executed. (Per this project's build convention, that tracker is updated centrally in a later phase, not by this build itself.)

docs.title: Build notes / judgment calls
docs.text:
• Real gap: TC-GOV-001 did not exist in this repo at the time this scenario was built. flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md lists it as "Not Started," and no flowx_test_gov_001_tagging_* spec/resource files were present. Per this build pass's scope discipline, building TC-GOV-001 itself is out of bounds for this task (a separate, parallel build owns it). This job resource therefore references TC-GOV-001's expected coordinates -- catalog flowx, schema bronze_crm, table customer_raw, and dataflow_group_id dfg_gov_001_tagging -- inferred from flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md's own TC-GOV-001 row plus this repo's strict, universally-observed naming convention (every existing spec's dataflow_group_id is dfg_<the job name's own middle segment>, e.g. dfg_dq_001_warn for flowx_test_dq_001_warn_job, dfg_ing_001_zip_filter for flowx_test_ing_001_zip_filter_job). If TC-GOV-001 is ultimately built with a different dataflow_group_id, this job's base_parameters need a one-line update to match.
  • No new pipeline resource, no new onboarding spec, no new fixture data -- exactly per this task's own instructions: this scenario is entirely about the idempotency of one already-proven notebook call, not about DAG shape or ingestion behavior, so it adds only the one job resource.
  • Omitted setup_control_tables/seed/onboard/pipeline tasks. Every other job in this repo chains those first; this one deliberately does not, because doing so would make it a redundant re-test of TC-GOV-001's own onboarding/pipeline-build path rather than a focused test of repeat tagging invocation. This job's first task assumes customer_raw already exists and already carries TC-GOV-001's tags -- i.e. TC-GOV-001's own job must run at least once before this one.
  • apply_abac/capture_cdc_change_counts left at notebook defaults rather than pinned explicitly in base_parameters, so this scenario exercises the same code path TC-GOV-001's own job invokes, not a specially reduced one.

docs.title: Test Pipeline: Attribute Value Drift Detection (TC-REC-002)
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md (Module 7, TC-REC-002), flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md, 07_reconciliation.md.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Prove that the reconciliation engine's hash-based matcher correctly classifies a record present on both sides of a comparison, under the same match_keys, as VALUE_DRIFT the moment a compare_columns attribute differs -- as opposed to MISSING_IN_TARGET/MISSING_IN_SOURCE, which apply only when a key is absent from one side entirely. Customer C001 is landed on both sides with a different status value (SUSPENDED in the baseline, ACTIVE in the CDC feed) so the drift is unambiguous and attributable to exactly one column.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Two small ingestion flows, both source_type: "autoloader", plain CSV, cdc_load_strategy: "APPEND" (a raw landing table for reconciliation comparison, same convention already used by scenario 002/003's own zerobus_bronze/autoload_bronze -- see 02_cdc_load_strategies.md § APPEND):
  • df_rec_002_customer_baseline_ingest -> {{catalog}}.silver_crm.customer_baseline -- C001 @ status=SUSPENDED.
  • df_rec_002_customer_cdc_ingest -> {{catalog}}.silver_crm.customer_cdc -- C001 @ status=ACTIVE.
  • One reconciliation flow (recon_rec_002_customer_drift) comparing customer_baseline (source) against customer_cdc (target) on match_keys: ["customer_id"], compare_columns: ["status"], comparison_direction: "target_to_source" -- deliberately the audit-only direction, so this run never appends/mutates either table (see the flagged gap below for what this direction choice actually means for the VALUE_DRIFT assertion).

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• flowx_testing/037_rec_002_drift.json -- 2 ingestion flows + 1 reconciliation flow onboarding spec (no transformation_flows).
  • sample_data/flowx_testing/crm_usecase/customer_baseline_drift.csv (1 row) / customer_cdc_drift.csv (1 row) -- hand-authored, new fixtures (no existing seeded fixture carries this exact baseline-vs-CDC status drift shape on a shared key).
  • notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/03_seed_rec_002_drift_data.py -- a new, dedicated seed notebook (kept separate from every other scenario's own seed notebook) that provisions the crm schema and a dedicated landing_customer_drift Volume (baseline//cdc/ subfolders, so each ingestion flow gets its own Auto Loader incoming zone), then lands both fixtures.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• {{catalog}}.silver_crm.customer_baseline -- exactly 1 row, C001 @ status=SUSPENDED.
  • {{catalog}}.silver_crm.customer_cdc -- exactly 1 row, C001 @ status=ACTIVE.
  • {{catalog}}.config.reconciliation_run_log -- one row for recon_rec_002_customer_drift, matched_count=0, value_drift_count=1 (see 07_reconciliation.md: value_drift_count is a genuine independent aggregate, populated regardless of comparison_direction, since all four classifications are computed in the same join pass).
  • {{catalog}}.config.reconciliation_mismatch_log -- see the flagged gap immediately below for what this configuration actually writes here.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
flowx_testing/037_rec_002_drift.json's reconciliation flow:

{
  "reconciliation_id": "recon_rec_002_customer_drift",
  "source_config": {"type": "table", "table": "{{catalog}}.silver_crm.customer_baseline", "read_mode": "batch", "hash_precomputed": false},
  "target_configs": [
    {
      "target_id": "customer_cdc_target",
      "type": "table",
      "table": "{{catalog}}.silver_crm.customer_cdc",
      "read_mode": "batch",
      "hash_precomputed": false,
      "comparison_direction": "target_to_source"
    }
  ],
  "match_keys": ["customer_id"],
  "compare_columns": ["status"],
  "generate_surrogate_key": false,
  "error_handling": {"on_failure": "warn"}
}

append_target_table is correctly omitted -- it is only required when comparison_direction includes source_to_target (see 07_reconciliation.md § target_configs[]-only fields), and this flow never appends anywhere.

docs.title: Main execution flow
docs.text:
databricks bundle deploy --target dev
databricks bundle run flowx_test_rec_002_drift_job --target dev

Task chain: setup_control_tables -> seed_rec_002_drift_data -> onboard_rec_002 -> run_pipeline -> run_rec_002_reconciliation.

docs.title: Expected results — simulation notes
docs.text:
SQL assertions (after a run, replace {catalog} with your actual target catalog):

-- Both raw landing tables carry exactly one C001 row, drifted on status
SELECT status FROM {catalog}.silver_crm.customer_baseline WHERE customer_id = 'C001'; -- SUSPENDED
SELECT status FROM {catalog}.silver_crm.customer_cdc      WHERE customer_id = 'C001'; -- ACTIVE

-- reconciliation_run_log: value_drift_count reflects the drift regardless of direction
SELECT matched_count, value_drift_count, missing_in_target_count, missing_in_source_count
FROM {catalog}.config.reconciliation_run_log
WHERE reconciliation_id = 'recon_rec_002_customer_drift'
ORDER BY run_at DESC LIMIT 1;
-- expect: matched_count=0, value_drift_count=1, missing_in_target_count=1 (C001 counts as a
-- source_to_target "miss" in the aggregate -- see 07_reconciliation.md, value_drift_count is a
-- subset of missing_in_target_count), missing_in_source_count=0 (C001 is present on both sides,
-- so it is never MISSING_IN_SOURCE either)

-- reconciliation_mismatch_log -- see the flagged gap below for why this returns 0 rows as
-- literally configured
SELECT mismatch_type, match_key_values_json, differing_columns_json
FROM {catalog}.config.reconciliation_mismatch_log
WHERE reconciliation_id = 'recon_rec_002_customer_drift';

This pass's actual verification status: see flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md for whether this job was actually run against the live workspace and what the real result was -- this document describes what should happen structurally; the status tracker records what did happen, if anything, each time this scenario is executed. (Per this project's build convention, that tracker is updated centrally in a later phase, not by this build itself.)

docs.title: Build notes / judgment calls
docs.text:
• New fixtures, not a reuse. No existing seeded fixture carries a customer_id/status baseline-vs-CDC pair drifted on a shared key (sample_data/sample_recon_customer_master_*.csv is the closest existing shape, but it's a poc-catalog test_specs/spec_09_* fixture using R00N keys and a different drifted record, R003, not C001 -- reusing it would not satisfy this TC's own literal C001 assertion). 2 small new CSV fixtures (1 row each) and 1 new dedicated seed notebook were added.
  • APPEND, not a CDC strategy, for both ingestion flows. Neither customer_baseline nor customer_cdc needs upsert/history semantics -- they are raw landing tables whose only purpose is to feed the reconciliation comparison, the same pattern scenario 002/003 already established for zerobus_bronze/autoload_bronze (see 02_cdc_load_strategies.md § APPEND).
  • Genuine framework gap: comparison_direction: "target_to_source" cannot produce the VALUE_DRIFT row TESTING_PLAN.md's own row asks to verify. This test case's own task description explicitly specifies comparison_direction: "target_to_source" "so nothing gets mutated," then asks to verify a VALUE_DRIFT row for C001 in reconciliation_mismatch_log. Tracing reconciliation/appender.py::run_target_reconciliation (the actual dispatch logic, not just the doc prose) shows these two expectations are mutually exclusive as the engine exists today:
  • evaluate_source_to_target = comparison_direction in ("source_to_target", "both") gates the only code path that ever adds MISSING_IN_TARGET/VALUE_DRIFT rows to mismatch_frames (appender.py lines ~522-527).
  • evaluate_target_to_source = comparison_direction in ("target_to_source", "both") gates a separate path that only ever adds MISSING_IN_SOURCE rows (line ~528-531).
  • So comparison_direction: "target_to_source" alone never writes a VALUE_DRIFT row to reconciliation_mismatch_log — only source_to_target/both do. And since C001 exists on both sides here (just with a drifted status, not an absence), this flow's target_to_source path also finds zero MISSING_IN_SOURCE records — meaning reconciliation_mismatch_log genuinely receives 0 rows for this reconciliation_id as configured, exactly as literally specified.
  • Flipping to comparison_direction: "both"/"source_to_target" would produce the VALUE_DRIFT mismatch-log row this TC wants to verify -- but evaluate_source_to_target unconditionally appends C001's corrected baseline row (status=SUSPENDED) into append_target_table the moment missing_in_target_count > 0 (which VALUE_DRIFT alone already satisfies, since it's a documented subset of that count) -- i.e. it would mutate customer_cdc (leaving it with two C001 rows, ACTIVE and SUSPENDED, append-only), which directly contradicts this same TC's own "so nothing gets mutated" requirement.
  • There is no reconciliation configuration today that audits VALUE_DRIFT into reconciliation_mismatch_log without also performing the self-healing append. This is a real gap in reconciliation/appender.py's design (an audit-only VALUE_DRIFT log without a mutating append is not expressible via any combination of documented fields), not a mistake in how this spec was authored. Per this build's own scope discipline, the spec was built exactly as literally instructed (target_to_source) rather than silently switching to "both" to fake a passing assertion; the reconciliation_run_log.value_drift_count=1 assertion above is the one that will actually pass live -- the reconciliation_mismatch_log row-level assertion, as this TC's own verification logic describes it, will not, until this gap is addressed (e.g. a future audit-only VALUE_DRIFT logging mode independent of the append action).
  • No run_observability_task. Same reasoning as every other TC-* build in this pass (see e.g. 42_tc_cdc_003.md's identical note) -- observability is opt-in via a spec's own observability[] array, not wired in by default.

docs.title: Test Pipeline: Pre-Computed Hash Matcher (hash_precomputed) Plan Assertion (TC-REC-003)
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md (Module 7, TC-REC-003), flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md, 07_reconciliation.md § Hash-first matching, and why, 02_cdc_load_strategies.md § The hash-key/hash-value framework.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Prove that reconciliation_flows[].source_config/target_configs[].hash_precomputed: true genuinely reuses an already-materialized __framework_hash_key/__framework_hash_value pair instead of recomputing it inline, by:

  1. Building two independent CDC-dispatched targets ({{catalog}}.silver_sales.orders_src / orders_tgt), each carrying real, physically-stored __framework_hash_key/ __framework_hash_value columns (SCD1 + generate_hash_columns: true — see 02_cdc_load_strategies.md §4a).
  2. Reconciling them against each other with hash_precomputed: true on both sides.
  3. Showing, via a real EXPLAIN physical plan against the two persisted tables, exactly what matcher.py's single-column __framework_hash_key equi-join looks like once the hash columns are trusted as-is — and, by contrast, what the extra sha2(concat_ws(...)) expression node looks like when a hash has to be recomputed inline instead.

A deliberate scale-down from TESTING_PLAN.md's own description. TESTING_PLAN.md frames TC-REC-003 around "large datasets (1M rows)" and an "Execution completes within SLA" assertion. This build uses 24 rows per side instead — enough to prove the mechanism (the join genuinely runs on __framework_hash_key, the hash columns are genuinely reused rather than recomputed, and the matcher genuinely classifies MATCHED/VALUE_DRIFT/MISSING_IN_TARGET/ MISSING_IN_SOURCE correctly), not the performance claim. No SLA/timing assertion is made anywhere in this doc — it would not mean anything at 24 rows. See "Build notes / judgment calls" below for why this substitution is the right one.

docs.title: Where this is actually implemented (read before building or debugging this scenario)
docs.text:
Confirmed by reading reconciliation/matcher.py in full this pass:

  • prepare_dataset_for_matching(df, match_keys, compare_columns, hash_precomputed, ...) is the only place hash_precomputed is consulted. When True, it just asserts __framework_hash_key/__framework_hash_value are already present on df (raising FrameworkConfigError if not — defense in depth, since a hand-edited control-table row could claim hash_precomputed: true for a table that was never actually CDC-dispatched) and returns df unchanged. When False, it calls cdc/hashing.py::compute_hash_columns(df, match_keys, resolved_compare_columns) to add both columns via a fresh sha2(concat_ws('||', ...), 256) expression.
  • match_reconciliation_target(source_df, target_df, ...) — the function that actually joins — runs identically regardless of hash_precomputed: source_narrow.join(target_narrow, on=HASH_KEY_COLUMN, how="full_outer"). The join is always a single-column equality on __framework_hash_key. hash_precomputed does not change which column the join runs on — it changes whether that column arrives as a stored physical column (read straight off the table scan) or a freshly-computed expression evaluated immediately upstream of the join. This is the one nuance worth being precise about: the "cost avoidance" 02_cdc_load_strategies.md describes is a Project-node (the sha2(concat_ws(...)) expression) that hash_precomputed: true lets the matcher skip entirely — not a different join strategy or join key. See "Expected results" below for what this looks like in a real EXPLAIN plan.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Two ingestion_flows, each source_type: "autoloader" (plain CSV), cdc_load_strategy: "SCD1", primary_keys: ["order_id"], generate_hash_columns: true (explicit, though already the default for any CDC-dispatched strategy) — landing independently into {{catalog}}.silver_sales.orders_src and orders_tgt.
  • One reconciliation_flow (recon_rec_003_orders_precomputed_hash) comparing orders_src (source) against orders_tgt (target), both sides hash_precomputed: true, comparison_direction: "both" — both self-heals (source_to_target: append missing/drifted source rows into orders_tgt) and audits (target_to_source: report, never write, target-only rows).

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• flowx_testing/038_rec_003_precomputed_hash.json — 2 ingestion_flows, 1 reconciliation_flows, no transformation_flows.
  • sample_data/flowx_testing/rec_orders_usecase/orders_src_batch1.csv (24 rows) / orders_tgt_batch1.csv (24 rows) — hand-authored, deliberately not identical:
Rows orders_src orders_tgt Expected classification O2001–O2022 (22 rows) present, unchanged present, unchanged MATCHED O2023 status = PENDING status = DELIVERED (drifted) VALUE_DRIFT O2024 present absent MISSING_IN_TARGET (self-healed: appended into orders_tgt) O2099 absent present MISSING_IN_SOURCE (audit-only, never appended anywhere)
  • notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/03_seed_rec_003_precomputed_hash_data.py — a new, dedicated seed notebook (kept separate from every other scenario's own seed notebook) that provisions rec_orders_usecase's two landing Volumes and lands both fixtures.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• {{catalog}}.silver_sales.orders_src — 24 rows, each carrying __framework_hash_key = sha2(concat_ws('||', order_id), 256) and a __framework_hash_value over every other applicable column (generate_hash_columns: true, columns_to_check/columns_to_exclude both unset → every non-key, non-technical column is included, resolved at execution time).
  • {{catalog}}.silver_sales.orders_tgt — 24 rows (23 landed + 1 self-healed append from orders_src's O2024, once reconciliation runs), same hash-column shape.
  • {{catalog}}.config.reconciliation_run_log — one row for target_id: "orders_tgt": matched_count = 22, missing_in_target_count = 2 (1 MISSING_IN_TARGET + 1 VALUE_DRIFT, per this column's documented union semantic), value_drift_count = 1, missing_in_source_count = 1, appended_count = 2 (the genuinely missing O2024 and the drifted O2023, re-appended as a correction rather than mutated in place — the append-only CDC/Zerobus-bus model this framework's targets assume).
  • {{catalog}}.config.reconciliation_mismatch_log — 3 rows (O2023: VALUE_DRIFT, O2024: MISSING_IN_TARGET, O2099: MISSING_IN_SOURCE).

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
flowx_testing/038_rec_003_precomputed_hash.json's reconciliation flow:

{
  "reconciliation_id": "recon_rec_003_orders_precomputed_hash",
  "source_config": {
    "type": "table",
    "table": "{{catalog}}.silver_sales.orders_src",
    "read_mode": "batch",
    "hash_precomputed": true
  },
  "target_configs": [
    {
      "target_id": "orders_tgt",
      "type": "table",
      "table": "{{catalog}}.silver_sales.orders_tgt",
      "read_mode": "batch",
      "hash_precomputed": true,
      "comparison_direction": "both",
      "append_target_table": "{{catalog}}.silver_sales.orders_tgt"
    }
  ],
  "match_keys": ["order_id"],
  "compare_columns": ["status", "amount"],
  "generate_surrogate_key": false,
  "error_handling": {"on_failure": "warn"}
}

Both ingestion_flows[].target_config entries are identical (SCD1, primary_keys: ["order_id"], sequence_by_column: "order_date", generate_hash_columns: true, storage_format: "delta") — the two targets are independently CDC-dispatched, so each one's own __framework_hash_key/__framework_hash_value is computed by dq/quarantine.py (_apply_hash_and_surrogate_key_columns), not by the reconciliation flow itself; the reconciliation flow's hash_precomputed: true only ever consumes what already exists.

compare_columns: ["status", "amount"] at the reconciliation-flow level is independent of each target's own upstream comparison-column resolution (which, with no columns_to_check set, covers every applicable column) — it only scopes what mismatch_detail_df/reconciliation_mismatch_log.differing_columns_json reports per drifted record, and whether hash_equal is checked at all (non-empty → real hash-value equality; empty → forced true, key-presence-only matching). error_handling.on_failure: "warn" mirrors scenario 003's own choice, so a transient failure logs rather than hard-fails the job.

docs.title: Main execution flow
docs.text:
databricks bundle deploy --target dev
databricks bundle run flowx_test_rec_003_precomputed_hash_job --target dev

Task chain: setup_control_tables -> seed_rec_003_precomputed_hash_data -> onboard_rec_003 -> run_pipeline -> run_reconciliation.

docs.title: Expected results — simulation notes
docs.text:
SQL assertions (after a run, replace {catalog} with your actual target catalog):

-- Row counts
SELECT count(*) FROM {catalog}.silver_sales.orders_src;   -- expect: 24
SELECT count(*) FROM {catalog}.silver_sales.orders_tgt;   -- expect: 24 (23 landed + 1 self-healed)

-- reconciliation_run_log: the classification this scenario exists to prove
SELECT matched_count, missing_in_target_count, value_drift_count, missing_in_source_count, appended_count, status
FROM {catalog}.config.reconciliation_run_log
WHERE reconciliation_id = 'recon_rec_003_orders_precomputed_hash' AND target_id = 'orders_tgt'
ORDER BY run_at DESC LIMIT 1;
-- expect: matched_count=22, missing_in_target_count=2, value_drift_count=1,
--         missing_in_source_count=1, appended_count=2, status='SUCCESS'

-- reconciliation_mismatch_log: per-record detail
SELECT match_key_values_json, mismatch_type, differing_columns_json
FROM {catalog}.config.reconciliation_mismatch_log
WHERE reconciliation_id = 'recon_rec_003_orders_precomputed_hash'
ORDER BY detected_at DESC LIMIT 3;
-- expect: O2023/VALUE_DRIFT (status differs), O2024/MISSING_IN_TARGET, O2099/MISSING_IN_SOURCE

Plan assertion — what a hash-precomputed join genuinely looks like. This is the real check TESTING_PLAN.md asks for; run it directly against the two persisted tables (no notebook instrumentation needed, since both already carry real __framework_hash_key columns):

EXPLAIN
SELECT s.order_id AS src_order_id, t.order_id AS tgt_order_id, s.__framework_hash_key
FROM   {catalog}.silver_sales.orders_src s
FULL OUTER JOIN {catalog}.silver_sales.orders_tgt t
       ON s.__framework_hash_key = t.__framework_hash_key;

Expected physical plan shape (exact join strategy/exchange nodes will vary with Spark version and table size — at 24 rows Spark will likely pick a broadcast or sort-merge join either way — but the join condition and the absence of any hash-computing expression are the two load-bearing details):

== Physical Plan ==
*(3) SortMergeJoin FullOuter, (__framework_hash_key#123 = __framework_hash_key#456)
:- *(1) Sort [__framework_hash_key#123 ASC NULLS FIRST], false, 0
:  +- *(1) ColumnarToRow
:     +- FileScan delta silver_sales.orders_src[order_id#...,__framework_hash_key#123,...] ...
+- *(2) Sort [__framework_hash_key#456 ASC NULLS FIRST], false, 0
   +- *(2) ColumnarToRow
      +- FileScan delta silver_sales.orders_tgt[order_id#...,__framework_hash_key#456,...] ...

The join condition is a single (__framework_hash_key = __framework_hash_key) equality — never order_id or any multi-column match_keys condition — and __framework_hash_key comes straight off each FileScan delta node with no Project/sha2/concat_ws expression anywhere in the tree, because hash_precomputed: true trusts it as an already-materialized physical column.

Contrast — what the plan looks like when the hash has to be recomputed inline, i.e. what cdc/hashing.py::compute_hash_columns inserts upstream of the identical join when hash_precomputed: false (illustrated here directly against orders_src, recomputing __framework_hash_key from its own match_keys the same way prepare_dataset_for_matching would if it couldn't trust the stored column):

EXPLAIN
SELECT order_id, sha2(concat_ws('||', CAST(order_id AS STRING)), 256) AS recomputed_hash_key
FROM   {catalog}.silver_sales.orders_src;

Expected: a Project node — Project [order_id#..., sha2(concat_ws(||, cast(order_id#... as string)), 256) AS recomputed_hash_key#...] — sitting directly above the FileScan delta node. This is the exact expression node hash_precomputed: true lets the matcher skip on both sides of every reconciliation join, at any table size — the join itself (SortMergeJoin/BroadcastHashJoin on __framework_hash_key) is identical either way, which is also why hash-first matching "doesn't require precomputation to work" (07_reconciliation.md) — precomputation is purely this Project node's avoidance, not a different join mechanism.

This pass's actual verification status: see flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md for whether this job was actually run against the live workspace and what the real result was — this document describes what should happen structurally; the status tracker records what did happen, if anything, each time this scenario is executed. (Per this project's build convention, that tracker is updated centrally in a later phase, not by this build itself.)

docs.title: Build notes / judgment calls
docs.text:
• Scaled down from 1M rows to 24 rows per side — and the SLA claim is dropped, not approximated. TESTING_PLAN.md's original framing ("Execution completes within SLA") is a performance claim that only means something at real scale against real concurrent workload; asserting any timing number against a 24-row fixture would be theater, not verification. What a small fixture can genuinely prove — and what this doc asserts instead — is the mechanism: the join really runs on __framework_hash_key, the hash columns really come from a stored column rather than a recomputed expression, and the matcher's four-way classification really works. The EXPLAIN plan comparison above is the mechanism-level equivalent of the original SLA assertion.
  • Two independent ingestion flows, not one table read twice. hash_precomputed: true is only interesting to prove when both sides are genuinely separate CDC-dispatched targets, each with its own independently-computed __framework_hash_key — reconciling a table against itself would trivially match every row and never exercise VALUE_DRIFT/MISSING_* classification at all.
  • New fixture, not a reuse. No existing seeded fixture carries two independently-landed order populations with a deliberate drift/missing/extra mix under silver_sales.orders_src/ orders_tgt (the exact object names TESTING_PLAN.md itself specifies for this test case), so 2 small new CSV fixtures (24 rows each) and 1 new dedicated seed notebook were added — kept separate from TC-TRF-002's own sales_usecase/bronze_sales/silver_sales.all_global_orders fixtures and pipeline, which this scenario's tables sit alongside in the same silver_sales schema without overlapping (schema creation is idempotent CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS).
  • SCD1 chosen for both ingestion flows (not SCD2/FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC) — any CDC-dispatched strategy exercises the identical hash-generation code path (_apply_hash_and_surrogate_key_columns doesn't branch on which strategy triggered it); SCD1 is the simplest to reason about for a single-batch load with no history/delete-marker noise, consistent with TC-SEC-002's own choice for the same reason.
  • No DQ rules, no governance tags, no encryption — this scenario is scoped to the hash_precomputed matcher path specifically; DQ (TC-DQ-*), governance (TC-GOV-*), and encryption (TC-SEC-001/TC-SEC-003) are separate, already-tracked test modules.

docs.title: Test Pipeline: External Sink Dual Materialization & Plain ZIP Export (TC-SNK-001)
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, 23_lakeflow_sinks.md (the sink/external_sink mechanics this scenario exercises), 47_tc_trf_001.md (the 4-way join shape this scenario reuses), flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Prove target_type: "external_sink"'s dual-output contract end to end: a single transformation_flows entry both (1) materializes a real, governed, queryable Delta table via the unchanged register_main_and_quarantine_tables + CDC-dispatch path, and (2) additionally exports that same table's rows as a genuine Lakeflow sink artifact -- a plain, unencrypted ZIP archive -- via a second, independent dlt.create_sink(format="pgp_zip") + @dlt.append_flow reading dlt.read_stream(qualified_main_table) (engine/sink_registration.py::register_external_sink_export). Both outputs come from one pipeline update, not a separate post-deployment export job.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Reuses TC-TRF-001's own 4-way streaming/batch inner-join shape verbatim: 1 streaming Auto Loader fact table (assignments_raw, is_streaming: true) inner-joined against 3 batch-read dimension tables (employees_raw/departments_raw/projects_raw, is_streaming: false) -- see 47_tc_trf_001.md for the join-exclusion behavior (employee_id = 'E005' has no assignment row) this same fixture data also proves here, incidentally.
  • 4 ingestion_flows, all source_type: "autoloader", all target_type: "streaming_table", landing plain (unzipped) CSVs into this test case's own dedicated bronze tables (df_snk001_assignments_ingest -> bronze_ea.snk001_assignments_raw, and similarly for employees/departments/projects).
  • One transformation_flows entry (ts_snk001_ea_joined_assignments_sink), target_type: "external_sink", cdc_load_strategy: "APPEND" (the flow's own is_streaming resolves true because its snk001_assignments_raw source input is marked is_streaming: true -- notebooks/03_engine/03_lakeflow_declarative_pipeline.py's is_streaming = flow_row.target_type == "streaming_table" or any(input.is_streaming ...) -- which is exactly what satisfies register_external_sink_export's "main table must be a genuine Streaming Table" check for a non-streaming_table target_type):
SELECT a.employee_id, a.project_id, a.hours_allocated, e.employee_name, e.role, e.dept_id,
       d.dept_name, d.region, p.project_name, p.budget
FROM snk001_assignments_raw a
JOIN snk001_employees_raw e ON a.employee_id = e.employee_id
JOIN snk001_departments_raw d ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id
JOIN snk001_projects_raw p ON a.project_id = p.project_id
  • target_config.sink_config: format: "pgp_zip", staging path under egress_ea.export_zips/_staging/snk001/, post_export_archive.enabled: true writing to egress_ea.export_zips/output/snk001/ -- no secret and no pgp_encryption block, which is what makes this a plain, unencrypted ZIP export (contrast with spec_24_new_27_08_test_flagship.json's ts_flagship_customer_scd1_egress, the PGP-encrypted worked example in 23_lakeflow_sinks.md).

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• flowx_testing/039_snk_001_external_sink.json -- 4 ingestion_flows + 1 transformation_flows entry (no reconciliation_flows).
  • sample_data/flowx_testing/ea_usecase/{employees,departments,projects,assignments}.csv -- reused as-is, no new fixture needed (same 5-row join shape TC-TRF-001 already established: employees.csv has 5 rows E001-E005, assignments.csv has exactly 5 rows covering only E001-E004).
  • notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/03_seed_trf_001_4way_join_data.py (existing, reused as-is) -- provisions the ea schema's landing_assignments/landing_employees/ landing_departments/landing_projects/_schemas Volumes and lands the 4 CSV fixtures plain/unzipped.
  • notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/02_seed_flowx_testing_data.py (existing, reused as-is) -- provisions bronze_ea/silver_ea and, critically, the egress_ea schema and its export_zips Volume, which is where this test case's own sink stages and lands its ZIP output.
  • No new sample data and no new seed notebook were needed for this test case.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• {{catalog}}.silver_ea.snk001_ea_joined_assignments -- a real, queryable Delta table, exactly 5 rows (one per assignments.csv row), zero rows with employee_id = 'E005'.
  • One .zip file landing under {{catalog}}.egress_ea.export_zips/output/snk001/, named snk001_ea_joined_export_<batch_id>.zip (export_file_name_format in sink_config) -- a genuinely unencrypted archive (no .zip.pgp suffix, since pgp_encryption is absent from this spec), containing one JSON-lines-per-row staged file per output partition for that micro-batch.
  • {{catalog}}.bronze_ea.snk001_employees_raw still has all 5 employees (E001-E005) -- E005's absence is a property of the join output only.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
flowx_testing/039_snk_001_external_sink.json's one transformation_flows[] entry's target_config:

{
  "cdc_load_strategy": "APPEND",
  "storage_format": "delta",
  "sink_config": {
    "path": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/egress_ea/export_zips/_staging/snk001/",
    "format": "pgp_zip",
    "post_export_archive": {
      "enabled": true,
      "output_zip_path": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/egress_ea/export_zips/output/snk001/",
      "export_file_name_format": "snk001_ea_joined_export_{batch_id}"
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Build notes / judgment calls
docs.text:
• Genuine naming collision with scenario 001 -- resolved by renaming this test case's own targets, not scenario 001's. TC-SNK-001's own task detail names the literal target flowx.silver_ea.ea_joined_assignments -- but scenario 001 (flowx_test_001_zip_join_export_pipeline, already deployed) already owns a real, already-materialized external_sink flow against that exact three-part name, including the identical join SQL, the identical pgp_zip sink format, and the identical egress_ea.export_zips/_staging/ \/ egress_ea.export_zips/output/ Volume paths (see flowx_testing/001_zip_file_onboarding.json). Two different Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines cannot both declare a table/sink against the identical Unity Catalog object or write concurrently into the identical output directory with the same batch-numbered file name -- attempting either would risk a deployment-time table-ownership conflict or a runtime file-name collision between two unrelated pipelines' batch_0.zip outputs, not two independent, separately-verifiable test results. Per this build's scope discipline (never edit another test case's files), the fix is on this test case's own side, following the exact precedent 47_tc_trf_001.md already set for the same reason: every bronze/silver target is named snk001_<name> (bronze_ea.snk001_*_raw / silver_ea.snk001_ea_joined_assignments), and the sink's staging/output paths are scoped to a snk001/ subfolder and a snk001_-prefixed export_file_name_format -- still inside the exact same bronze_ea/silver_ea/egress_ea.export_zips schemas/Volume the task names, just disambiguated from scenario 001's own already-deployed objects and files. The join semantics, the CDC/DQ configuration, and the expected row-count/ZIP-presence assertions are otherwise exactly what the task describes.
  • Reused fixtures and seed notebooks, no new sample data. Both ingestion input (the 4 EA CSVs) and the required schema/Volume provisioning (ea/bronze_ea/silver_ea/egress_ea) are fully covered by two already-existing, idempotent seed notebooks (02_seed_flowx_testing_data.py, 03_seed_trf_001_4way_join_data.py), reused as-is in this test case's own job. No new CSV fixture and no new seed notebook were written.
  • pgp_zip chosen deliberately for the "plain ZIP export" requirement. The framework's sink_config.format enum is {"delta", "kafka", "pgp_zip"} -- pgp_zip is the only format that produces a real .zip file at all (delta/kafka write Delta/Kafka records, not an archive). Per 23_lakeflow_sinks.md, post_export_archive.secret and .pgp_encryption are both independently optional; omitting both (as this spec does) is what yields a genuinely plain, unencrypted .zip rather than an AES-password-protected or PGP-encrypted one -- this is the literal, real "plain ZIP export" this test case name calls for, not a naming coincidence with the format's own pgp_zip identifier.

docs.title: Test Pipeline: TC-SNK-002 -- Pure Sink Export Without Table Materialization
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md (Module 8, TC-SNK-002), flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md, 23_lakeflow_sinks.md (full sink/external_sink mechanics).

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Prove target_type: "sink" (engine/sink_registration.py::register_sink_target) writes a flow's streaming output directly to an egress Volume via a genuine dlt.create_sink + @dlt.append_flow -- and, critically, that no Delta table is ever registered in Unity Catalog for the sink itself. This is the structural distinction from target_type: "external_sink" (TC-SNK-001): external_sink materializes a real, governed table and exports it; sink never materializes anything on the clean/main side -- the flow's own staged (quarantine-filtered) @dlt.view feeds the sink directly. See 23_lakeflow_sinks.md for the full mechanics and the "sink" vs "external_sink" comparison table.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Land a small, 5-row IoT sensor readings CSV fixture and ingest it via Auto Loader into a genuine bronze streaming table, {catalog}.bronze_iot_snk002.sensor_readings_raw (cdc_load_strategy: "APPEND" -- immutable sensor readings, no dedup/history needed). This table is queryable -- it is the downstream sink flow that is not.
  • A same-spec transformation_flow (ts_snk_002_pure_sink_export) reads that bronze table as a streaming source_inputs entry and sets target_type: "sink" with sink_config: {"format": "delta", "path": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/egress_iot/partner_drops/"} -- writing every row straight to the partner egress Volume as Delta files, with no @dlt.table registered for this flow at all.
  • Needs no dependency on any other already-onboarded scenario -- its own job runs setup_control_tables -> seed -> onboard -> run_pipeline end to end from a clean environment.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• flowx_testing/040_snk_002_pure_sink.json -- one ingestion flow (df_snk_002_iot_sensor_ingest) + one transformation flow (ts_snk_002_pure_sink_export, the pure sink), no reconciliation_flows.
  • sample_data/flowx_testing/iot_usecase/sensor_readings_snk002.csv -- 5 IoT sensor readings (device_id, sensor_type, reading_value, event_ts, region) across 5 devices and 3 regions.
  • notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/03_seed_snk_002_pure_sink_data.py -- provisions {catalog}.iot_snk002 (landing schema + landing_sensor/_schemas Volumes), {catalog}.bronze_iot_snk002 (the bronze target schema), and {catalog}.egress_iot + its partner_drops Volume (the sink's actual write destination -- unlike a normal table target, this Volume is never auto-provisioned by the pipeline itself, so it must be created ahead of time, same as scenario 001/002/003's own egress_ea/export_zips precedent), then lands the fixture file into the incoming landing Volume.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• {catalog}.bronze_iot_snk002.sensor_readings_raw -- 5 rows, the genuine bronze table (plus the usual __framework_* technical-metadata columns).
  • /Volumes/{catalog}/egress_iot/partner_drops/ -- one or more Delta data files written directly by @dlt.append_flow -> dlt.create_sink(format="delta", ...), containing the same 5 rows' device_id/sensor_type/reading_value/event_ts/region columns.
  • No table named partner_drops_sink (or any other name) is ever registered under {catalog}.egress_iot in information_schema.tables -- the entire point of target_type: "sink" (register_sink_target never calls dlt.create_streaming_table/@dlt.table for the sink's own clean/main side; see 23_lakeflow_sinks.md).

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
flowx_testing/040_snk_002_pure_sink.json's pure-sink transformation flow (ts_snk_002_pure_sink_export):

{
  "flow_step_id": "ts_snk_002_pure_sink_export",
  "dataflow_id": "df_snk_002_iot_sensor_ingest",
  "target_catalog": "{{catalog}}",
  "target_schema": "egress_iot",
  "target_table": "partner_drops_sink",
  "target_type": "sink",
  "source_inputs": [
    {
      "input_name": "sensor_readings_for_sink",
      "table": "{{catalog}}.bronze_iot_snk002.sensor_readings_raw",
      "is_streaming": true
    }
  ],
  "transformation_sql": "SELECT device_id, sensor_type, reading_value, event_ts, region FROM sensor_readings_for_sink",
  "target_config": {
    "cdc_load_strategy": "APPEND",
    "sink_config": {
      "format": "delta",
      "path": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/egress_iot/partner_drops/"
    }
  }
}

target_catalog/target_schema/target_table are still required fields on the schema (used to build the internal sink node name _partner_drops_sink_sink and the append-flow name partner_drops_sink_sink_flow), but -- unlike every other target_type -- they never resolve to a real Unity Catalog object here; no CREATE SCHEMA/CREATE TABLE happens for egress_iot/partner_drops_sink at all. cdc_load_strategy is present (schema-required) but functionally inert for a "sink" flow -- it is never consulted for CDC dispatch, only carried as a label on the sink_registration structured log event.

Resources:

  • resources/flowx_test_snk_002_pure_sink_pipeline.yml -- flowx_test_snk_002_pure_sink_pipeline (catalog: flowx, schema: bronze_iot_snk002, serverless, dataflow.group.id: dfg_snk_002_pure_sink).
  • resources/flowx_test_snk_002_pure_sink_job.yml -- flowx_test_snk_002_pure_sink_job.
