docs.title: Test Pipeline: TC-SNK-003 — PGP Encrypted ZIP Sink Export with Secret Key
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md (Module 8, TC-SNK-003), flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md, 23_lakeflow_sinks.md (the full sink/external_sink mechanics this scenario exercises), 16_encryption_and_secrets.md (the PGP/secrets design), 35_tc_ing_005.md (the mirror-image scenario — PGP decryption on ingest, whose secret-provisioning pattern this doc reuses for PGP encryption on egress).

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Prove target_config.sink_config.format: "pgp_zip" with post_export_archive.pgp_encryption.enabled: true end to end, against a real disposable PGP keypair: a small monthly financial settlements batch is Auto Loader-ingested, materialized as a genuine, queryable Delta table (target_type: "external_sink"), and — inside the same Lakeflow Declarative Pipeline update — additionally exported as a PGP-encrypted ZIP archive via dlt.create_sink + @dlt.append_flow (engine/sink_registration.py::register_external_sink_export → archive/pgp_zip_sink.py). The recipient's public key is resolved from a genuine Unity Catalog secret at graph-definition time — not a literal key embedded in the spec. This scenario's realistic production framing: a bank must drop a monthly settlements extract into a partner's secure egress Volume, encrypted so that only the partner (holder of the matching private key) can ever read it.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• One ingestion flow (df_finance_settlements_ingest), source_type: "autoloader", cdc_load_strategy: "APPEND" — deliberately the simplest possible CDC strategy, since this scenario's whole point is the sink's PGP+ZIP export behavior, not CDC behavior (APPEND + autoloader still publishes a genuine Lakeflow Streaming Table, which is what register_external_sink_export requires of the main target before it will attach the export @dlt.append_flow — see 23_lakeflow_sinks.md).
  • target_type: "external_sink" — flowx.silver_finance.monthly_settlements is materialized as a real, governed, DQ-quarantined table exactly like any other target type, plus a second @dlt.append_flow reads that same table (dlt.read_stream) into a dlt.create_sink(format= "pgp_zip", ...).
  • sink_config.post_export_archive.pgp_encryption.enabled: true with only recipient_public_key_secret set (no sign_with_private_key_secret — this scenario doesn't exercise sign-then-encrypt, only plain recipient-only encryption) — resolved eagerly, driver-side, at graph-definition time by _resolve_secret_into_options, then passed through to archive/pgp_zip_sink.py's _PgpZipStreamWriter.commit() as an already-resolved plaintext value (pgp_recipient_secret_value), never re-resolved inside write()/commit() themselves — see that module's docstring for exactly why (commit()/abort() run in a separate streaming-sink runtime process with no working dbutils gateway).
  • No sink_config.post_export_archive.secret (AES ZIP password) — this scenario exercises PGP encryption only, not the additional/independent AES-ZIP-password layer pgp_zip also supports.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• flowx_testing/041_snk_003_pgp_zip_sink.json — the onboarding spec (one ingestion flow, no transformation/reconciliation flows).
  • sample_data/flowx_testing/finance_egress_usecase/monthly_settlements.csv — 5-row plaintext fixture (settlement_id, account_id, settlement_amount, currency, settlement_date, counterparty), landed as-is (no ZIP/PGP handling on the input side — that's deliberate, see Responsibilities above).
  • sample_data/flowx_testing/finance_egress_usecase/pgp_egress_keypair_public.asc / pgp_egress_keypair_private.asc — a dedicated, disposable, passphrase-less RSA-2048 PGP keypair generated specifically for this test scenario (via PGPy, the same library crypto/pgp.py wraps; generated locally with a one-off script and round-trip-verified against the framework's own pgp_encrypt/pgp_decrypt before committing) and committed to the repo. Zero real security value — it protects nothing but this scenario's own synthetic fixture, and represents the external partner's keypair: the framework only ever needs (and only ever gets, via UC secret) the public half, to encrypt outgoing exports; the private half is never uploaded as a secret anywhere in this bundle — it exists purely so this doc's own verification step can decrypt the exported archive back, standing in for the real partner's own private key.
  • notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/03_seed_snk_003_pgp_zip_sink_data.py — lands monthly_settlements.csv into the input landing Volume and provisions the finance_egress/ secure_drops schema+Volume the sink writes into (a sink's destination Volume is never auto-created by the pipeline itself, unlike the pipeline's own default catalog/schema).

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• {catalog}.silver_finance.monthly_settlements — 5 rows, in plaintext, exactly matching monthly_settlements.csv's content, plus the usual __framework_* technical metadata columns — a genuine, queryable Unity Catalog table (this is the "dual materialization" half of external_sink).
  • /Volumes/{catalog}/finance_egress/secure_drops/output/monthly_settlements_<batch_id>.zip.pgp — one PGP-encrypted, ASCII-armored archive per micro-batch. Decrypting it with the matching private key (pgp_egress_keypair_private.asc) yields a plain .zip whose entries are the micro-batch's rows as JSON-Lines (archive/pgp_zip_sink.py's staging format — not a re-serialized CSV; see _STAGED_FILE_SUFFIX/write()), covering all 5 settlement rows across however many micro-batches Auto Loader's single input file produces (typically one, since the whole fixture lands in one file).
  • No plaintext .zip intermediate ever persisted under secure_drops/output/ — commit() always removes the unencrypted intermediate immediately after PGP-wrapping it (see archive/pgp_zip_sink.py::commit).
  • information_schema.tables shows monthly_settlements as a real table (unlike TC-SNK-002's pure "sink" target type, which registers no table at all).

docs.title: Required prerequisite: provision the recipient public key as a UC secret
docs.text:
Manual, admin-audited step — not automated by this framework, following the exact same security-scope pattern 05_deployment_guide.md's own prerequisites section establishes for this project's other encryption keys, and the same pattern 35_tc_ing_005.md uses for its private key secret — here it's the public key that must be a secret, since encryption (not decryption) is what runs inside the pipeline. This step must run before flowx_test_snk_003_pgp_zip_sink_job's run_pipeline_task — the pipeline's sink registration will fail fast with SecretResolutionError until it does:

# Test-only, disposable PGP public key -- protects nothing real (see sample_data/
# flowx_testing/finance_egress_usecase/ header note). No passphrase, matching this project's
# other throwaway test keypairs.
databricks secrets put-secret security pgp_public_key_finance_egress_test \
  --string-value "$(cat sample_data/flowx_testing/finance_egress_usecase/pgp_egress_keypair_public.asc)"

The matching private key (pgp_egress_keypair_private.asc) needs no secret at all — the pipeline never decrypts anything on this path; it is only ever used locally (or by a real partner, in production) to decrypt the exported .zip.pgp archive, per the verification command below.

docs.title: Main execution flow
docs.text:
databricks bundle deploy --target dev
databricks secrets put-secret security pgp_public_key_finance_egress_test \
  --string-value "$(cat sample_data/flowx_testing/finance_egress_usecase/pgp_egress_keypair_public.asc)"
databricks bundle run flowx_test_snk_003_pgp_zip_sink_job --target dev

Task chain: setup_control_tables → seed_snk_003_pgp_zip_sink_data → onboard_snk_003 → run_pipeline_task.

docs.title: Expected results — verification logic
docs.text:
-- Exactly 5 plaintext rows, matching monthly_settlements.csv's known content
SELECT settlement_id, account_id, settlement_amount, currency, settlement_date, counterparty
FROM {catalog}.silver_finance.monthly_settlements
ORDER BY settlement_id;
-- expect: STL-9001..STL-9005, e.g. STL-9003 -> ACC-4003, 2100.00, EUR, 2026-07-31, Fabrikam Logistics

# Exported archive landed where post_export_archive.output_zip_path points, with a .zip.pgp
# extension (never a plaintext .zip left behind)
databricks fs ls dbfs:/Volumes/{catalog}/finance_egress/secure_drops/output/
# expect: monthly_settlements_<batch_id>.zip.pgp (no bare .zip files)

Decrypt-and-verify (documented here, not necessarily executed as part of this pass — see docs/35_tc_ing_005.md's identical "documented, not necessarily executed" convention for its own decrypt-side verification):

# Run locally (or in a notebook) with PGPy installed and the exported archive + private key
# fixture both available.
import pgpy, zipfile, io

with open("pgp_egress_keypair_private.asc") as f:
    private_key, _ = pgpy.PGPKey.from_blob(f.read())

with open("monthly_settlements_<batch_id>.zip.pgp", "rb") as f:
    message = pgpy.PGPMessage.from_blob(f.read())

decrypted = private_key.decrypt(message).message  # bytes/bytearray -- the plain ZIP's bytes
with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(bytes(decrypted))) as zf:
    print(zf.namelist())  # one JSON-Lines file per partition that had rows
    for name in zf.namelist():
        print(zf.read(name).decode("utf-8"))  # each line: one settlement row as JSON

Expect the decrypted ZIP's JSON-Lines entries to cover all 5 settlement rows (across however many partition files that micro-batch produced), each carrying settlement_id/account_id/ settlement_amount/currency/settlement_date/counterparty plus the framework's technical metadata columns — a faithful round trip of what {catalog}.silver_finance.monthly_settlements holds.

If the recipient public key secret hasn't been provisioned yet, or is malformed, the pipeline update fails fast at graph-definition time with a SecretResolutionError/FrameworkConfigError naming the secret coordinates — this is the expected, correct failure mode, not a bug to route around; it proves the framework never silently falls through to an unencrypted export.

This pass's actual verification status: see flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md for whether this job was actually run against the live workspace and what the real result was — this document describes what should happen structurally; the status tracker records what did happen.

docs.title: Known gaps / judgment calls
docs.text:
• Secret coordinates vs. TESTING_PLAN.md's aspirational naming: TESTING_PLAN.md's own TC-SNK-003 row names flowx_partner_scope/partner_pgp_pubkey (classic workspace secret-scope terminology). This build instead uses this project's real Unity Catalog three-level {secret_catalog, secret_schema, secret_key} shape — {{catalog}}, security, pgp_public_key_finance_egress_test — resolved via dbutils.secrets.get(catalog=, schema=, key=), exactly the same pre-existing terminology gap 35_tc_ing_005.md's own "Known gaps" section already documents for TC-ING-005 (which the current instructions explicitly said to follow). Not something newly introduced or resolved by this test case.
  • No separate run_observability_task: TESTING_PLAN.md's row lists a second job task, run_observability_task, for every TC-SNK-* scenario. No other already-built scenario in this repo (including TC-ING-005, TC-SNK-001's own real build, or scenario 004) adds a dedicated observability job task — structured JSON logging (observability/structured_logger.py's logged_operation context manager, wrapping sink_registration.py's own "sink_registration" event) fires automatically as a side effect of run_pipeline_task itself, with no separate task needed to "activate" it. This build follows that same established, real pattern rather than the plan's aspirational extra task.
  • Reused the TC-ING-005 secret-provisioning pattern, not its literal keypair: the task instructions said to reuse a real PGP keypair "the same way TC-ING-005 does" — read as reusing the approach (a disposable, passphrase-less, PGPy-generated RSA-2048 test keypair, committed to the repo, provisioned as a security-scope UC secret via a documented databricks secrets put-secret command), not literally reusing TC-ING-005's own pgp_test_keypair_*.asc bytes — those represent a different persona (the finance partner sending data to us, decrypted with a private-key secret) from this scenario's persona (us sending data to an egress partner, encrypted with a public-key secret). A new, dedicated keypair (pgp_egress_keypair_{public,private}.asc) was generated instead, matching TC-ING-005's own generation method exactly, and round-trip-verified locally (pgp_encrypt/pgp_decrypt against a ZIP payload) before being committed.
  • export_file_name_format: set to "monthly_settlements_{batch_id}" for a clearer exported filename than the default "batch_{batch_id}" — purely cosmetic, doesn't change any verification logic above.

docs.title: Test Pipeline: TC-OBS-001 -- In-Pipeline Structured JSON Logging Validation
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md (Module 9, TC-OBS-001), flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md, 25_dlt_observability_module.md (the separate, OTel-oriented observability engine -- not what this test case is about; see the Build notes below).

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Prove that every framework-level operation this pipeline exercises -- reading the ingestion source, staging/quarantine-routing, registering the target flow, and (post-deployment) capturing SCD/CDC change counts -- emits exactly one structured JSON log line via observability/structured_logger.py::log_flow_event, and that every one of those lines parses as valid JSON carrying a non-null business identifier and timestamp. This is deliberately a single minimal ingestion flow combining a quarantine-action dq_config rule with an SCD1 cdc_load_strategy, so all of ingestion_read / dq_staging / flow_registration / cdc_change_capture fire from one pipeline run instead of needing several separate scenarios to reach each code path.

Doc-drift note (read this before writing an assertion against this test case) -- the exact field-name discrepancy this build actually found reading structured_logger.py directly, per this build's own instruction not to invent field names. Both TESTING_PLAN.md's own Module 9 row and this test case's own brief describe the emitted payload as carrying timestamp_utc and pipeline_run_id. Neither name is what log_flow_event actually emits. Reading observability/structured_logger.py::log_flow_event (the sole place this payload is built) top to bottom, the real JSON object is:

{
  "timestamp": "2026-08-29T12:34:56.789012+00:00",
  "operation": "ingestion_read",
  "flow_id": "df_obs_001_structured_log_ingest",
  "status": "SUCCESS",
  "records_read": null,
  "records_written": null,
  "records_rejected": null,
  "records_quarantined": null,
  "duration_ms": 12.345,
  "error": null
}
  • The timestamp field is named timestamp, not timestamp_utc -- its value is UTC (datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat()), but the key itself has no _utc suffix. Assert against timestamp.
  • There is no pipeline_run_id field on this payload at all, in any operation this scenario reaches. __framework_pipeline_run_id is a real, current, __framework_-prefixed identifier in this codebase -- but it is a Delta table column stamped onto every row by dq/quarantine.py::add_quarantine_columns (visible on test_structured_log_raw's quarantined rows via a SELECT, see Expected results below), never a field inside this JSON log line. Use flow_id (always present, always non-null in every call site this scenario reaches) as this payload's own business-identifier assertion instead of pipeline_run_id.
  • Per-operation **extra fields actually merged in for the operations this scenario reaches: flow_registration carries target_table/target_catalog/target_schema/target_type/ cdc_load_strategy; ingestion_read carries staged_view_name; dq_staging carries target_table/is_streaming (plus records_read/records_rejected/records_quarantined only on the non-streaming branch -- see Outputs below for why this flow's own dq_staging event omits counts); cdc_change_capture carries target_table/cdc_load_strategy/ captured_version/inserted_count/updated_count/deleted_count (plus starting_version on a real, non-zero capture).

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Land 5 synthetic "event" rows (scaled down from any larger volume, per this project's "minimal, real, onboardable" convention) as a single plain CSV in /Volumes/{{catalog}}/ea/landing_obs_json_log/ -- 1 of the 5 (E003) has a NULL amount.
  • One ingestion_flow (df_obs_001_structured_log_ingest), source_type: "autoloader", targeting {{catalog}}.bronze_ea.test_structured_log_raw:
  • dq_config.rules: one action: "quarantine" rule (amount IS NOT NULL) -- this is what makes a quarantine table actually get created and populated (see 01_control_metadata_schema.md §5), which is what makes dq_staging's structured log event meaningful to check, not merely present.
  • target_config.cdc_load_strategy: "SCD1", primary_keys: ["event_id"] -- what makes this flow CDC-dispatched at all, which is the precondition for flow_registration's own cdc_load_strategy field being anything other than APPEND/TRUNCATE_AND_LOAD's no-op label, and for the downstream capture_cdc_change_counts_obs_001 job task's capture_all_scd_change_counts to find a real CDC-dispatched flow to report on.
  • A fourth job task, capture_cdc_change_counts_obs_001 (notebooks/04_governance/04_apply_governance_and_egress.py, capture_cdc_change_counts: "true", apply_abac: "false" since this spec's governance_tags is empty -- nothing to tag), chained after run_pipeline, exercises the fourth and last structured-log-emitting code path this test case cares about: control_plane/post_deployment.py:: capture_all_scd_change_counts runs DESCRIBE HISTORY/table_changes(...) against the now-materialized test_structured_log_raw and emits one operation: "cdc_change_capture" log line -- this must run as a separate, later job task, since a CDC target's post-update Delta commit version isn't knowable from inside the pipeline's own graph-definition code (see 02_cdc_load_strategies.md § Change-count capture via Change Data Feed).

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• flowx_testing/042_obs_001_json_log.json -- single-ingestion-flow onboarding spec (no transformation_flows/reconciliation_flows).
  • sample_data/flowx_testing/obs_usecase/structured_log_events.csv (5 rows: event_id, event_type, amount, event_ts) -- new fixture, see Build notes.
  • notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/03_seed_obs_001_json_log_data.py -- a new, dedicated seed notebook that provisions the already-established ea/bronze_ea schemas (idempotent, shared with several other test cases) plus a new landing_obs_json_log Volume, then copies the fixture CSV directly into it (no ZIP handling for this scenario).

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• {{catalog}}.bronze_ea.test_structured_log_raw -- 4 rows (E001, E002, E004, E005; E003 is quarantined).
  • {{catalog}}.bronze_ea.test_structured_log_raw_quarantine -- 1 row (E003), carrying a populated __framework_dq_failed_rule_ids (["dq_obs_001_amount_not_null"]), a populated __framework_record_id ("E003"), and a populated __framework_pipeline_run_id -- the real, current location of a per-row run identifier in this codebase, distinct from (and not to be confused with) the structured log line's own field set described above.
  • Structured JSON log lines (driver/cluster stdout for the pipeline update; the governance job task's own "Logs" tab for cdc_change_capture) -- see Expected results for exactly how to retrieve and assert against them. Because test_structured_log_raw is a genuinely streaming target, dq_staging's own log line for this flow lands via the streaming branch of dq/quarantine.py's _quarantine_table() closure -- is_streaming: true, no records_read/records_rejected/records_quarantined counts (a streaming DataFrame cannot be eagerly aggregated inside that closure; see that function's own docstring) -- so this scenario's real, countable quarantine assertion is the SELECT count(*) against test_structured_log_raw_quarantine above, not the dq_staging log line's own (absent) count fields.

Resources:

  • resources/flowx_test_obs_001_json_log_pipeline.yml -- flowx_test_obs_001_json_log_pipeline (catalog: flowx, schema: bronze_ea, serverless, dataflow.group.id: dfg_obs_001_json_log).
  • resources/flowx_test_obs_001_json_log_job.yml -- flowx_test_obs_001_json_log_job.

docs.title: Main execution flow
docs.text:
databricks bundle deploy --target dev
databricks bundle run flowx_test_obs_001_json_log_job --target dev

Task chain: setup_control_tables -> seed_obs_001_json_log_data -> onboard_obs_001 -> run_pipeline -> capture_cdc_change_counts_obs_001.

docs.title: Expected results -- simulation notes
docs.text:
Row counts (after a run, replace {catalog} with your actual target catalog):

SELECT count(*) FROM {catalog}.bronze_ea.test_structured_log_raw;
-- expect: 4

SELECT count(*) FROM {catalog}.bronze_ea.test_structured_log_raw_quarantine;
-- expect: 1

SELECT __framework_record_id, __framework_dq_failed_rule_ids, __framework_pipeline_run_id
FROM {catalog}.bronze_ea.test_structured_log_raw_quarantine;
-- expect: E003, ["dq_obs_001_amount_not_null"], <a non-null run/update id>

Log assertion -- how to actually retrieve these lines. structured_logger.py's own module docstring is explicit that Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines' event log has a fixed, closed set of event_type values with no documented API to inject a custom event -- so databricks pipelines get-update/an event-log query will never surface these lines; querying the event log is the wrong tool for this assertion. The real, inspectable surface is driver/cluster stdout:

  1. For the pipeline update itself (ingestion_read/dq_staging/flow_registration): open the pipeline's run in the Databricks UI (Jobs & Pipelines -> Pipelines -> flowx_test_obs_001_json_log_pipeline -> this update), open its cluster from the update's own compute link, and use the cluster detail page's Driver logs tab (stdout sub-tab) -- every logger.info/logger.warning/logger.error call this framework makes, including every log_flow_event line, lands there as one line of plain text containing the JSON payload.
  2. For the governance task's own cdc_change_capture line: since capture_cdc_change_counts_obs_001 is a plain job-task notebook run (not a Lakeflow Declarative Pipeline update), its stdout is available more directly: the Jobs UI's per-task Logs tab for that specific task run (Jobs & Pipelines -> Jobs -> flowx_test_obs_001_json_log_job -> this run -> capture_cdc_change_counts_obs_001 task -> Logs), or databricks jobs get-run-output --run-id <task_run_id>'s logs field via the CLI/SDK.
  3. Copy the driver/task log text into a local file and run it through a JSON-line parser, filtering to lines containing "operation": (every non-framework log line in that same stream will simply fail to parse as JSON and should be skipped, not treated as a failure of this test):
import json

parsed, failed = [], []
for line in open("driver_stdout.txt", encoding="utf-8"):
    line = line.strip()
    if '"operation":' not in line:
        continue  # not one of this framework's structured log lines
    try:
        parsed.append(json.loads(line))
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        failed.append(line)

assert not failed, f"{len(failed)} structured log line(s) failed to parse as JSON"
assert all(p.get("timestamp") and p.get("flow_id") for p in parsed), \
    "every structured log line must carry a non-null timestamp and flow_id"
operations_seen = {p["operation"] for p in parsed}
assert {"ingestion_read", "dq_staging", "flow_registration"} <= operations_seen  # pipeline-update lines
# "cdc_change_capture" is emitted by the separate governance task run -- check its own log
# stream (step 2 above) for that one operation name specifically.

Expect, at minimum, one line each for operation: "ingestion_read", "dq_staging", and "flow_registration" from the pipeline update's own driver log, and one "cdc_change_capture" line from the governance task's log -- each with a non-null timestamp/flow_id and status: "SUCCESS" (the log-level-mapping table in structured_logger.py's own docstring: SUCCESS -> logger.info, so all of these should appear at INFO level on a clean run).

This pass's actual verification status: see flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md for whether this job was actually run against the live workspace and what the real result was -- this document describes what should happen structurally; the status tracker records what did happen, if anything, each time this scenario is executed. This build phase deliberately does not run databricks bundle deploy/run itself -- a separate, later phase handles deployment/execution centrally across all test cases together.

docs.title: Build notes / judgment calls
docs.text:
• Field-name discrepancy, not a blocker. Both this TC's own brief and TESTING_PLAN.md's Module 9 row claim timestamp_utc/pipeline_run_id as the emitted fields. Reading observability/structured_logger.py::log_flow_event directly (per this build's own instruction to verify against that module, not invent names) shows the real field is timestamp (UTC-valued, not _utc-suffixed) and that pipeline_run_id is not a log-line field at all in the current codebase -- it's the unrelated __framework_pipeline_run_id Delta column dq/quarantine.py stamps onto quarantined rows. This doc's own verification section (above) asserts against the real field names; flagged here explicitly rather than silently building a test that would assert against fields the code never emits.
  • New fixture, not a reuse. No existing seeded CSV (checked every sample_data/ flowx_testing/*_usecase/ fixture) carries an event_id/amount/event_ts shape suited to a quarantine-plus-SCD1 combination without pulling in an unrelated business domain (CRM customers, EA departments, etc.), so one new 5-row CSV (sample_data/flowx_testing/obs_usecase/structured_log_events.csv) and one new dedicated seed notebook were added, following this project's existing per-TC fixture convention.
  • bronze_ea/ea schemas reused, landing Volume is new. {{catalog}}.ea/ {{catalog}}.bronze_ea already exist, idempotently provisioned by several other test cases (scenario 001, TC-ING-008, TC-TRF-001, TC-SNK-001) -- reused here rather than inventing a new schema pair, exactly as this task's own target-table instruction (flowx.bronze_ea.test_structured_log_raw) implies. The landing Volume (ea.landing_obs_json_log) is new and distinct from TC-ING-008's own ea.landing_csv, so this scenario's fixture never collides with that test case's own file. The target table name itself (test_structured_log_raw) does not collide with any other test case's own bronze_ea.* target (departments_raw/employees_raw/projects_raw/assignments_raw from scenario 001, departments_tech_metadata_raw from TC-ING-008, trf001_*_raw/snk001_*_raw from TC-TRF-001/TC-SNK-001).
  • A fourth job task added, beyond the usual setup -> seed -> onboard -> run_pipeline chain. This test case is specifically about proving every framework operation's structured log line parses as JSON, not just the ones a bare pipeline-update chain reaches on its own -- cdc_change_capture only ever fires from the separate, post-deployment governance task (see Responsibilities above), so capture_cdc_change_counts_obs_001 was added deliberately. This reuses the existing 04_apply_governance_and_egress.py notebook exactly as TC-GOV-001 does, just with apply_abac: "false" (this spec sets no governance_tags, so there is nothing to tag) and capture_cdc_change_counts: "true" (the one thing this task exists to exercise).
  • No run_observability_task. TESTING_PLAN.md's own "Proposed Pipeline & Job Architecture" column for TC-OBS-001 names a second run_observability_task step. Per TESTING_STATUS.md's own framing (TESTING_PLAN.md is a planned/aspirational matrix, not a literal build spec) and the precedent already set by docs/38_tc_ing_008.md's own build notes, that task is not built here: it would run the separate, observability[]-config-driven OTel/DLT-event-log engine (25_dlt_observability_module.md) that TC-OBS-002/OBS-003 are actually about, not the in-pipeline structured_logger.py stdout logging this test case targets -- TESTING_STATUS.md's own Module 9 row already notes "every scenario's pipeline run already emits structured JSON logs... as a side effect," confirming no dedicated observability job task is needed to exercise it.

docs.text: See also: Documentation index, flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md (Module 9), flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md, docs/25_dlt_observability_module.md, docs/27_dlt_observability_onboarding_reference.md.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Prove that the pre-existing batch DLT observability engine (notebooks/08_observability/08_dlt_observability_engine.py, observability/destination_dispatcher.py::dispatch_to_volume) genuinely writes a real, readable .jsonl.gz OTel export to a Unity Catalog Volume path — destination_type: "DATABRICKS_VOLUME" (confirmed the correct real value; not "UNITY_CATALOG_VOLUME", which some docs incorrectly say). This is deliberately the same batch engine scenario 100's own dlt_observability_job.yml already exercises — not this project's separate continuous streaming OTel design (observability_otel_streaming_pipeline, see docs/29_test_pipeline_otel_streaming.md), which is a materially different, additive capability out of scope here.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Reuse an already-onboarded pipeline as "the pipeline being observed" — no new Lakeflow pipeline resource is defined for this test case. This job reuses flowx_test_100_zipcsv_pipeline (dataflow.group.id = dfg_zip_csv_dataload), the same pipeline resources/dlt_observability_job.yml already wraps.
  • Add a second, TC-OBS-003-owned observability_config row — destination_id: "dest-obs-003-vol-export" — scoped to that same dataflow_group_id, additive alongside (not a replacement for) scenario 100's own pre-existing "dest-dbx-volume" row. destination_config.volume_path is /Volumes/{{catalog}}/observability/app_logs/, compression: "GZIP", file_format: "JSONL".
  • Run the observed pipeline, then 08_dlt_observability_engine.py, and confirm a real .jsonl.gz file lands under that volume path and decompresses to valid OTel-shaped ResourceLogs JSON lines.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• flowx_testing/043_obs_003_vol_export.json — this test case's own dedicated onboarding spec. Its observability[] array carries the new destination described above. Its dataflow_group_id (dfg_zip_csv_dataload) must match the observed pipeline's own dataflow.group.id configuration entry — observability/event_log_extractor.py:: resolve_dataflow_group_id resolves that group id straight from the Pipelines API at runtime (pipeline.spec.configuration["dataflow.group.id"]), independent of any control-table state, so this is the one value that has to line up for the new destination to actually be picked up by load_destination_configs when this pipeline's telemetry is dispatched.
  • Reuses scenario 100's already-seeded landing fixtures (/Volumes/{{catalog}}/landing/input/ customer*/, seeded via the existing customer*.zip fixtures scenario 100 already lands) — no new sample data was created for this test case.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• {catalog}.config.observability_config — one additional row, config_id = "obscfg_dfg_zip_csv_dataload_dest-obs-003-vol-export", enabled = true, destination_type = "DATABRICKS_VOLUME".
  • A new file at /Volumes/{catalog}/observability/app_logs/dfg_zip_csv_dataload/<run-date>/dfg_zip_csv_dataload_<run_pipeline_update task_run_id>.jsonl.gz (naming per destination_dispatcher.py::_volume_file_path — deterministic <dataflow_group_id>_<task_run_id>, one file per DATABRICKS_VOLUME destination per observability task run). Because scenario 100's own "dest-dbx-volume" destination is also enabled for this same dataflow_group_id, two files land side by side for the same run — one per destination row — both under the identical volume_path prefix; this is expected, not a collision (the dispatcher runs once per destination, and each destination's dispatch is independent — see destination_dispatcher.py::dispatch_all).
  • Each .jsonl.gz line, once gunzipped, is one {"resourceLogs": [...]} JSON object — one line per ResourceLogs entry (one per flow/update in the observed window).

docs.text:
flowx_testing/043_obs_003_vol_export.json's observability[] entry:

{
  "id": "dest-obs-003-vol-export",
  "enabled": true,
  "type": "DATABRICKS_VOLUME",
  "destination_config": {
    "volume_path": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/observability/app_logs/",
    "compression": "GZIP",
    "file_format": "JSONL"

}

Judgment call / real gap: onboarding/spec_validator.py::validate_spec requires at least one of ingestion_flows/transformation_flows/reconciliation_flows to be non-empty — an observability-only spec (empty flow arrays, only an observability[] array) is rejected outright ("At least one of 'ingestion_flows', 'transformation_flows', or 'reconciliation_flows' must be non-empty"), even though _validate_observability_destinations itself carries no such requirement. Rather than inventing new sample data or a new pipeline node just to satisfy this rule, this spec's ingestion_flows[] re-declares scenario 100's own "df_zip_csv_file_ingest" flow verbatim — identical dataflow_id, identical source_config/target_config/ dq_config. Confirmed safe: every onboarding/metadata_upsert.py::upsert_* function is a plain MERGE keyed on that flow's own natural id (dataflow_id here), so onboarding this spec is a no-op update against the exact row scenario 100's own spec already created — it neither duplicates nor drifts that row, and dataflow_group_spec.has_ingestion_flows/ has_transformation_flows (the only fields this could otherwise disturb) are pure metadata, read by nothing in notebooks/03_engine/03_lakeflow_declarative_pipeline.py. Confirmed against the real schema (onboarding_templates/onboarding_spec.schema.json) and the real validate_spec() function directly (not just the JSON Schema) — zero errors.

docs.title: Main execution flow
docs.text:
databricks bundle deploy --target dev
databricks bundle run flowx_test_obs_003_vol_export_job --target dev

Task chain: setup_control_tables → onboard_100 → onboard_obs_003 → run_pipeline_update → observability_export. Self-contained and idempotent — onboard_100 re-onboards scenario 100's own spec first, so this job runs correctly from a clean environment without depending on flowx_test_100_job/dlt_observability_job having already been run; re-running this job never accumulates duplicate control-table rows or extra Volume files beyond one new file per distinct run_pipeline_update task run.

docs.title: Expected results — verification logic
docs.text:
# Databricks notebook / Python cell, after a run
import gzip, json

base = "/Volumes/flowx/observability/app_logs/dfg_zip_csv_dataload"
run_date_dirs = dbutils.fs.ls(base)          # one subdir per UTC run date
for d in run_date_dirs:
    for f in dbutils.fs.ls(d.path):
        if f.name.endswith(".jsonl.gz"):
            local = f.path.replace("dbfs:", "")
            with gzip.open(local, "rt", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                for line in fh:
                    payload = json.loads(line)                       # must not raise
                    rl = payload["resourceLogs"][0]                  # strict OTel shape
                    attrs = {a["key"]: a["value"] for a in rl["resource"]["attributes"]}
                    assert "databricks.dataflow_group_id" in attrs
                    for scope_log in rl["scopeLogs"]:
                        for record in scope_log["logRecords"]:
                            assert record["timeUnixNano"]
                            assert isinstance(record["severityNumber"], int)
                            assert "body" in record
            print(f.path, "OK")

-- Confirm the new destination row was onboarded
SELECT config_id, destination_id, enabled, destination_type, destination_config_json
FROM flowx.config.observability_config
WHERE dataflow_group_id = 'dfg_zip_csv_dataload'
ORDER BY destination_id;
-- expect 2 rows: 'dest-dbx-volume' (scenario 100's own) and 'dest-obs-003-vol-export' (this test)

-- Ad hoc Spark SQL read of the exported JSONL straight off the Volume (auto-detects .gz)
SELECT
  filter(resourceLogs[0].resource.attributes, a -> a.key = 'databricks.dataflow_group_id')[0].value.stringValue AS group_id,
  filter(resourceLogs[0].resource.attributes, a -> a.key = 'databricks.dataflow_id')[0].value.stringValue AS dataflow_id
FROM json.`/Volumes/flowx/observability/app_logs/dfg_zip_csv_dataload/*/*.jsonl.gz`;

Pass criteria: observability_export task completes SUCCESS; exactly one new .jsonl.gz file per enabled DATABRICKS_VOLUME destination appears under /Volumes/{catalog}/observability/app_logs/dfg_zip_csv_dataload/<today>/; every file decompresses cleanly and every line parses as valid JSON matching the {"resourceLogs": [...]} shape asserted by otel_payload_builder.py::validate_resource_logs before dispatch.

This pass builds the artifacts only — per this batch's scope discipline, deployment/execution against the shared dev workspace is handled by a separate, later centralized phase across all 45 test cases; see flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md for whether this job has actually been run yet and what the real result was.

docs.title: Test Pipeline: Continuous Day-1 to Day-2 Incremental Ingestion Cycle (TC-FLT-002)
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md (Module 10, TC-FLT-002), flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md, 02_cdc_load_strategies.md § SCD1.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Prove that a triggered (non-continuous) Lakeflow Declarative Pipeline genuinely resumes an incremental Auto Loader ingestion cycle across two separate pipeline updates -- not just that dlt.apply_changes sorts a single mixed batch correctly within one run. Day-1 lands an initial seed load and the pipeline is run once; only afterward does Day-2 land a batch of attribute updates to existing rows plus a couple of brand-new rows, and the pipeline is run a second time. Under cdc_load_strategy: "SCD1", the Day-2 updates must overwrite the matching rows in place (no duplicates, no history kept) while the Day-2 inserts must land as genuinely new rows -- so the final row count is day1_count + new_count, not day1_count + day2_count, since every Day-2 row that shares a customer_id with Day-1 is an upsert, not an additional row.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• One ingestion_flow (df_flt_002_customer_lifecycle_ingest), source_type: "autoloader", target_config.cdc_load_strategy: "SCD1" -- SCD1 is valid directly on an ingestion flow, so this scenario needs no separate transformation step.
  • primary_keys: ["customer_id"], sequence_by_column: "updated_at" -- the latest value per customer (by updated_at) wins on every upsert.
  • Two CSV "day" extracts landed into the same Auto Loader incoming path, but on two genuinely separate job runs of the seed step, with a real pipeline update run in between:
  • lifecycle_day1.csv -- 10 customers (CUST501-CUST510), the initial seed load.
  • lifecycle_day2.csv -- 3 of those same customer_ids (CUST501, CUST505, CUST509) re-sent with changed city/tier and an advanced updated_at (an update, under SCD1), plus 2 brand-new customer_ids (CUST511, CUST512) appearing for the first time (a plain insert).
  • Scaled down from the TESTING_PLAN.md-suggested 1,000/150/50 to 10/3/2 -- the ratio (existing rows updated vs. brand-new rows inserted, both a small minority of the total) is what this scenario proves, not the absolute row count.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• flowx_testing/044_flt_002_lifecycle.json -- single-ingestion-flow onboarding spec (no transformation_flows/reconciliation_flows).
  • sample_data/flowx_testing/crm_usecase/lifecycle_day1.csv (10 rows) / lifecycle_day2.csv (5 rows: 3 updates + 2 inserts) -- new fixtures, hand-authored (see Build notes).
  • notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/03_seed_flt_002_lifecycle_data.py -- a new, dedicated seed notebook that provisions the crm/silver_crm schemas and landing_lifecycle/_schemas Volumes, then lands one stage's CSV file per invocation (stage widget, day1 or day2) into /Volumes/{{catalog}}/crm/landing_lifecycle/incoming/ -- deliberately not both at once, since the whole point of this scenario is two separate triggered updates, not one batch containing both days' data.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• {{catalog}}.silver_crm.dim_customer_lifecycle -- the real SCD1 target, a genuine Lakeflow Streaming Table regardless of its declared target_type (dlt.apply_changes requires one). After the Day-1 run: exactly 10 rows. After the Day-2 run: exactly 12 rows (10 + 2 new, not 10 + 5) -- CUST501/CUST505/CUST509 overwritten in place with their Day-2 city/tier values, CUST502-CUST504/CUST506-CUST508/CUST510 unchanged from Day-1, CUST511/CUST512 newly present.
  • __framework_hash_key/__framework_hash_value and delta.enableChangeDataFeed = "true" on the target (every SCD1-dispatched target gets both, per 02_cdc_load_strategies.md § the hash-key/hash-value framework).

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
flowx_testing/044_flt_002_lifecycle.json's one ingestion_flows[] entry:

"target_config": {
  "cdc_load_strategy": "SCD1",
  "primary_keys": ["customer_id"],
  "sequence_by_column": "updated_at"
}

source_config.path: /Volumes/{{catalog}}/crm/landing_lifecycle/incoming/ (Auto Loader CSV, schema_location auto-derived under /Volumes/{{catalog}}/crm/_schemas/dim_customer_lifecycle/).

docs.title: Main execution flow
docs.text:
databricks bundle deploy --target dev
databricks bundle run flowx_test_flt_002_lifecycle_job --target dev

Task chain: setup_control_tables → seed_day1_customers → onboard_flt_002 → run_pipeline_day1 → seed_day2_customers → run_pipeline_day2.

The drop-day2-in-and-rerun sequence, explained. seed_day1_customers (the seed notebook with stage=day1) lands only lifecycle_day1.csv; run_pipeline_day1 then triggers the pipeline's first update, which Auto Loader discovers and ingests as its very first batch -- 10 inserts, since the target starts empty. Only once that update has fully committed does seed_day2_customers (stage=day2) land lifecycle_day2.csv into the same incoming path. run_pipeline_day2 then triggers a second, independent pipeline update: Auto Loader's own checkpoint means it discovers only the newly-arrived lifecycle_day2.csv file (it already processed lifecycle_day1.csv on the prior update and will not re-read it), and dlt.apply_changes upserts those 5 rows against the already-materialized 10-row target -- 3 keys match and overwrite in place, 2 keys are new and insert. This two-separate-runs structure is what actually exercises "yesterday's load, today's incremental delta," as opposed to a single run that happens to see a pre-mixed batch of both days' data at once (which would prove apply_changes's sequencing but not a real triggered-pipeline day-over-day cycle).

docs.title: Expected results — simulation notes
docs.text:
SQL assertions (after both runs, replace {catalog} with your actual target catalog):

-- Final row count: day1_count (10) + new_count (2) = 12, not day1+day2 (15)
SELECT count(*) FROM {catalog}.silver_crm.dim_customer_lifecycle;
-- expect: 12

-- Updated rows reflect Day-2 values
SELECT customer_id, city, tier
FROM {catalog}.silver_crm.dim_customer_lifecycle
WHERE customer_id IN ('CUST501', 'CUST505', 'CUST509')
ORDER BY customer_id;
-- expect: CUST501 -> San Francisco, GOLD
--         CUST505 -> Miami, GOLD
--         CUST509 -> Seattle, SILVER

-- Untouched Day-1 rows are unchanged
SELECT customer_id, city, tier
FROM {catalog}.silver_crm.dim_customer_lifecycle
WHERE customer_id = 'CUST502';
-- expect: Austin, SILVER (Day-1 value, never resent on Day-2)

-- Brand-new Day-2 customers are present exactly once
SELECT customer_id FROM {catalog}.silver_crm.dim_customer_lifecycle
WHERE customer_id IN ('CUST511', 'CUST512')
ORDER BY customer_id;
-- expect: 2 rows

-- No history/duplicates: SCD1 keeps exactly one row per key
SELECT customer_id, count(*) FROM {catalog}.silver_crm.dim_customer_lifecycle
GROUP BY customer_id HAVING count(*) > 1;
-- expect: 0 rows

This pass's actual verification status: see flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md for whether this job was actually run against the live workspace and what the real result was -- this document describes what should happen structurally; the status tracker records what did happen, if anything, each time this scenario is executed. (Per this project's build convention, that tracker is updated centrally in a later phase, not by this build itself.)

docs.title: Build notes / judgment calls
docs.text:
• New fixtures, not a reuse. No existing seeded fixture matches this scenario's exact requirement (a specific small set of existing keys updated plus a couple of brand-new keys, landed across two genuinely separate pipeline runs), so 2 new CSV fixtures and 1 new dedicated seed notebook were added, following the same pattern established by flowx_test_cdc_004_scd2_job (03_seed_cdc_004_scd2_data.py) rather than extending 02_seed_flowx_testing_data.py. Note that sample_data/flowx_testing/crm_usecase/ already holds an unrelated customer_scd1_day1.csv/customer_scd1_day2.csv pair (a different, single-row delete-focused fixture for another test case in this same batch) -- this scenario deliberately uses its own lifecycle_day1.csv/lifecycle_day2.csv names to avoid touching that other test case's files.
  • Scaled down, ratio preserved. TESTING_PLAN.md's own text names 1,000 seed / 150 updates / 50 new; this build uses 10 / 3 / 2 instead, keeping "a small minority of rows updated, a smaller minority newly inserted, most rows untouched" as the actual property under test rather than the absolute scale.
  • Two real pipeline-update tasks against one pipeline, not one. Unlike most other scenarios in this batch (which land all their fixture data before a single triggered update), this job's task chain runs run_pipeline_day1 and run_pipeline_day2 as two separate pipeline_task job tasks, both pointed at the same flowx_test_flt_002_lifecycle_pipeline, with seed_day2_customers landing the Day-2 file strictly in between them. This is a deliberate, necessary departure from the land-everything-then-run-once convention -- TC-FLT-002's entire premise (a real day-over-day incremental cycle across separate triggered runs) would not be exercised by a single run that happens to see both days' files at once.
  • No run_observability_task. TESTING_PLAN.md's own "Proposed Pipeline & Job Architecture" column for TC-FLT-002 names a second run_observability_task step, but consistent with every other real scenario built in this batch, observability is opt-in (wired via a spec's own observability[] array plus a separate job) and not part of this scenario's minimal build.

docs.title: Test Pipeline: TC-PRM-001 -- Parameterized Dynamic Volume & File Paths
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md, flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md, 17_onboarding_template_reference.md §3.4.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Prove transformation/parameters.py::substitute_path_parameters -- the new capability added this session that extends ${param} runtime substitution into path/URI-shaped fields (source_config.path/schema_location), not just SQL text. Until this pass, ${param} substitution only existed for transformation_sql/reconciliation's transform_sql/ filter_condition via the SQL-literal-quoting substitute_dynamic_parameters -- a string parameter used there comes back single-quoted, which would corrupt a filesystem path (/Volumes/x/'2026-08-28'/y is not a valid path). substitute_path_parameters is the sibling function this scenario exercises: it renders every value via plain str(), never quoted, and runs directly against the raw JSON text of source_config_json/target_config_json, before json.loads(...) -- see notebooks/03_engine/03_lakeflow_declarative_pipeline.py's generate_ingestion_flow, which calls it on both fields before the config dict is ever built.

This is a runtime substitution (re-read fresh from PIPELINE_PARAMETERS on every pipeline update), unlike the one-time {{catalog}}/{{env}} substitution onboarding/spec_loader.py applies once, forever, at onboarding time -- the two mechanisms are independent and both appear in this scenario's spec: {{catalog}} resolves to flowx when the spec is onboarded; ${data_domain}/${batch_date} resolve to finance_ops/2026-08-28 fresh every time the pipeline updates.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• One ingestion_flow (df_prm_001_daily_txns_ingest), source_type: "autoloader", plain CSV, cdc_load_strategy: "APPEND" -- landing raw daily transaction rows into {{catalog}}.bronze_finance.daily_txns_raw, no dedup, no CDC dispatch.
  • Top-level pipeline_parameters: {"data_domain": "finance_ops", "batch_date": "2026-08-28"}, referenced twice: source_config.path uses both ${data_domain} and ${batch_date}; source_config.schema_location uses ${data_domain} alone -- proving the same parameter substitutes correctly across two different fields, not just once incidentally.
  • Land the fixture CSV directly under the literal, fully-resolved path (/Volumes/flowx/finance_ops/landing/2026-08-28/) the substitution is expected to produce, so Auto Loader only finds the file if the substitution genuinely ran correctly end to end -- a wrong resolution (e.g. a literal ${data_domain} left unsubstituted, or the wrong value) means Auto Loader finds nothing, a visible failure rather than a silent false pass.
  • Verify __framework_source_file_name on the landed rows names a file under that exact resolved path -- the concrete, queryable proof the engine actually read from the parameter-resolved location and not some other path.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• flowx_testing/045_prm_001_path_param.json -- ingestion-only onboarding spec (no transformation_flows/reconciliation_flows), one flow: df_prm_001_daily_txns_ingest.
  • sample_data/flowx_testing/finance_usecase/daily_txns_batch1.csv -- 4 daily transaction records (TXN1001-TXN1004, two sharing account_id: ACC5001).
  • notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/03_seed_prm_001_path_param_data.py -- a new, dedicated seed notebook (widgets: catalog, data_domain, batch_date, the latter two defaulting to the spec's own pipeline_parameters values so the landed path and the pipeline's resolved path stay in lockstep). Provisions {catalog}.finance_ops / {catalog}.bronze_finance schemas and finance_ops.landing / finance_ops._schemas Volumes, then lands the fixture at /Volumes/{catalog}/{data_domain}/landing/{batch_date}/daily_txns_batch1.csv.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• {{catalog}}.bronze_finance.daily_txns_raw -- 4 rows, with txn_id, account_id, amount, currency, txn_date, plus the usual __framework_* technical-metadata columns (capture_technical_metadata defaults true, and is set explicitly here). No quarantine table (dq_config.rules is an empty list).
  • __framework_source_file_name on every row resolves to a path containing finance_ops/landing/2026-08-28/daily_txns_batch1.csv -- the assertion this scenario exists to make.
  • Auto Loader's own schema_location (/Volumes/flowx/finance_ops/_schemas/daily_txns_raw/) is created under the ${data_domain}-resolved path too, proving the same placeholder resolves consistently across both source_config fields in one pipeline update.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
flowx_testing/045_prm_001_path_param.json's one ingestion flow -- the part of this spec that is actually new/interesting:

"pipeline_parameters": {
  "data_domain": "finance_ops",
  "batch_date": "2026-08-28"
},
"ingestion_flows": [{
  "source_type": "autoloader",
  "target_catalog": "{{catalog}}",
  "target_schema": "bronze_finance",
  "target_table": "daily_txns_raw",
  "target_type": "streaming_table",
  "source_config": {
    "path": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/${data_domain}/landing/${batch_date}/",
    "format": "csv",
    "schema_location": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/${data_domain}/_schemas/daily_txns_raw/",
    "reader_options": {"header": "true", "cloudFiles.inferColumnTypes": "true"},
    "capture_technical_metadata": true
  },
  "target_config": {"cdc_load_strategy": "APPEND", "storage_format": "delta"}
}]

Note the two-layer substitution order: {{catalog}} is replaced with flowx by onboarding/spec_loader.py::substitute_environment_placeholders once, at onboarding time, before the JSON is ever parsed into the control tables -- so the control table's source_config_json column already reads /Volumes/flowx/${data_domain}/landing/${batch_date}/ the moment onboarding completes. ${data_domain}/${batch_date} are left untouched at that point and only resolve every time the pipeline updates, via generate_ingestion_flow's call to substitute_path_parameters against PIPELINE_PARAMETERS (itself re-read fresh from GROUP_ROW.pipeline_parameters_json on every pipeline update, not cached from onboarding time) -- so changing pipeline_parameters in the control table (e.g. re-onboarding with a new batch_date for the next day's batch) changes where the next pipeline update reads from, with no code change and no need to touch source_config again.

Resources:

  • resources/flowx_test_prm_001_path_param_pipeline.yml -- flowx_test_prm_001_path_param_pipeline (catalog: flowx, schema: bronze_finance, serverless, dataflow.group.id: dfg_prm_001_path_param).
  • resources/flowx_test_prm_001_path_param_job.yml -- flowx_test_prm_001_path_param_job.

docs.title: Main execution flow
docs.text:
databricks bundle deploy --target dev
databricks bundle run flowx_test_prm_001_path_param_job --target dev

Task chain: setup_control_tables -> seed_prm_001_path_param_data -> onboard_prm_001 -> run_prm_001_pipeline.

docs.title: Expected results -- simulation notes
docs.text:
SQL assertions (after a run, replace {catalog} with your actual target catalog):

-- Exactly 4 rows landed
SELECT count(*) FROM {catalog}.bronze_finance.daily_txns_raw;
-- expect: 4

-- The actual proof this scenario exists for: __framework_source_file_name resolves to the
-- ${data_domain}/${batch_date}-substituted path, not a literal "${data_domain}"/"${batch_date}"
-- string and not some other path
SELECT DISTINCT __framework_source_file_name FROM {catalog}.bronze_finance.daily_txns_raw;
-- expect every value to contain: .../finance_ops/landing/2026-08-28/daily_txns_batch1.csv

-- Equivalent, more mechanical assertion for scripted verification
SELECT count(*) FROM {catalog}.bronze_finance.daily_txns_raw
WHERE __framework_source_file_name LIKE '%/finance_ops/landing/2026-08-28/%';
-- expect: 4 (equals total row count -- every row's source file is under the resolved path)

-- Row content, unaffected by the path parameterization itself
SELECT txn_id, account_id, amount, currency, txn_date
FROM {catalog}.bronze_finance.daily_txns_raw ORDER BY txn_id;
-- expect:
--   TXN1001 | ACC5001 | 250.75   | USD | 2026-08-28
--   TXN1002 | ACC5002 | 89.10    | USD | 2026-08-28
--   TXN1003 | ACC5001 | 15000.00 | USD | 2026-08-28
--   TXN1004 | ACC5003 | 42.50    | USD | 2026-08-28

Negative check, if you want to actively rule out a "silently reads the wrong path" false pass: land a decoy file under the unsubstituted literal path (/Volumes/flowx/$%7Bdata_domain%7D/landing/$%7Bbatch_date%7D/ is not even a valid Volume path component, so this isn't practically constructible -- the stronger real-world check is simply that Auto Loader finds zero files, and the pipeline update either idles or errors, if the fixture is landed under any path other than the exact resolved /Volumes/flowx/finance_ops/landing/2026-08-28/ -- which is exactly why this scenario's seed notebook computes that path from the same data_domain/batch_date values the spec declares, rather than hardcoding a path string independently that could silently drift out of sync).

This pass's actual verification status: see flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md for whether this job was actually run against the live workspace and what the real result was -- this document describes what should happen structurally; the status tracker records what did happen, if anything, each time this scenario is executed. This build phase deliberately does not run databricks bundle deploy/run itself -- a separate, later phase handles deployment/execution centrally across all test cases together.

docs.title: Build notes / judgment calls
docs.text:
• New fixture, new dedicated seed notebook. No existing seeded fixture lands data under a ${param}-resolved, date-partitioned Volume path, so one small new 4-row CSV fixture (sample_data/flowx_testing/finance_usecase/daily_txns_batch1.csv) and one new seed notebook (03_seed_prm_001_path_param_data.py) were added, following this repo's established one-seed-notebook-per-scenario convention (e.g. 03_seed_ing_007_standardize_data.py) rather than editing the shared 02_seed_flowx_testing_data.py.
  • APPEND, not a CDC strategy. This scenario is scoped to proving path parameterization, not CDC/dedup behavior -- APPEND needs no primary_keys and keeps the spec minimal, matching several other single-flow ingestion scenarios' own choice (e.g. TC-ING-007).
  • No DQ rules, no governance tags, no encryption, no transformation/reconciliation flows. Scoped narrowly to the one new capability under test.
  • schema_location only carries ${data_domain}, not ${batch_date}. Auto Loader's schema tracking location is conventionally stable per source (not per landing batch), so only the domain-level parameter applies there -- this also incidentally proves the substitution engine handles a partial parameter set per field correctly (not every declared pipeline_parameter needs to appear in every path field).

docs.title: Test Pipeline: Parameterized DQ Rule Expressions (TC-PRM-004)
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md (Module 11, TC-PRM-004), flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md, 17_onboarding_template_reference.md §3.4 / §4.7.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
TESTING_PLAN.md's TC-PRM-004 describes a dq_config rule whose expression itself contains ${param} placeholders ("txn_amount <= ${max_allowed_txn_limit} AND txn_date >= '${cutoff_date}'"), substituted from pipeline_parameters the same way transformation_sql and reconciliation's filter_condition/transform_sql already are.

This build pass confirmed that mechanism does not exist in the framework today. Before writing this spec, every call site of substitute_dynamic_parameters/substitute_path_parameters was located by grepping onboarding/spec_validator.py, transformation/parameters.py, transformation/inputs.py, reconciliation/appender.py, reconciliation/dataset_reader.py, control_plane/repository.py, and control_plane/ddl_definitions.py -- and, separately, dq/ was grepped directly (dq/quarantine.py, dq/expectations.py) for any ${/pipeline_parameters reference at all: zero matches. dq_config.rules[].expression is passed straight through, verbatim, into the native Lakeflow expectation / quarantine-flag expression -- no substitution pass ever touches it. 17_onboarding_template_reference.md §3.4 independently confirms this in prose: ${param} substitution is wired into transformation_sql, reconciliation's filter_condition/transform_sql, and source_config/target_config path fields only, and explicitly calls out that it is "Not wired into dq_config or observability_config.destination_config.volume_path."

So this test case cannot be built as literally described in TESTING_PLAN.md -- there is no configuration that makes ${max_allowed_txn_limit}/${cutoff_date} resolve inside a DQ rule expression today. What can be built, and is built here, is the same rule with the same two literal values (50000 / 2026-01-01) hand-copied into the expression instead of the placeholders, proving the quarantine-action mechanics genuinely work for a two-condition AND boundary expression, while documenting the missing substitution path as a real, independently-confirmed framework gap rather than a build mistake.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• One ingestion_flow (df_prm_004_txns_validated_ingest), source_type: "autoloader", cdc_load_strategy: "APPEND" -- the simplest load strategy, so the flow stays focused on DQ rule/parameter behavior only (same convention as TC-DQ-001/002/004).
  • pipeline_parameters: {"max_allowed_txn_limit": 50000, "cutoff_date": "2026-01-01"} is declared on the spec for structural fidelity to TESTING_PLAN.md's own TC-PRM-004 shape, even though nothing in this ingestion-only spec (no transformation_flows/reconciliation_flows) ever consumes it -- dq_config can't, and there's no other flow type here that could.
  • dq_config.rules[] carries exactly one rule, valid_txn_bounds: "txn_amount <= 50000 AND txn_date >= '2026-01-01'", action: "quarantine" -- the literal-value stand-in for the placeholder expression TESTING_PLAN.md describes.
  • 8 fixture rows (see Inputs) deliberately split across all four combinations of the rule's two conditions -- pass-both, fail-amount-only, fail-date-only, fail-both -- so the test proves quarantine routing works for either half of the combined AND expression independently, not only the amount bound TESTING_PLAN.md's own simplified SQL assertion checks.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• flowx_testing/046_prm_004_dq_param.json -- single-ingestion-flow onboarding spec (no transformation_flows/reconciliation_flows).
  • sample_data/flowx_testing/txns_usecase/txns_dq_param.csv (8 rows, columns txn_id, account_id, txn_amount, currency, txn_date, merchant) -- new fixture, added alongside this test case's build (see Build notes). Placed in the existing txns_usecase/ fixture domain directory (established by TC-DQ-002) rather than a new one, since both scenarios share the same transaction-feed domain.
  • notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/03_seed_prm_004_dq_param_data.py -- a new, dedicated seed notebook (kept separate from 02_seed_flowx_testing_data.py and every other test case's own seed notebook) that provisions the txns/bronze_txns schemas and landing_dq_param/_schemas Volumes, then copies the fixture CSV directly into the landing Volume (no ZIP handling needed).

  • {{catalog}}.bronze_txns.txns_validated_quarantine -- exactly 4 rows (TXN-P002, TXN-P003, TXN-P005, TXN-P007), each carrying __framework_dq_failed_rule_ids containing valid_txn_bounds, __framework_dq_failure_reasons naming the failed expression, and __framework_record_id populated from txn_id (record_id_column).
  • The pipeline's own expectation/quarantine metrics show 4 of 8 evaluated rows quarantined against valid_txn_bounds.

(Per this project's build convention, that tracker is updated centrally in a later phase, not by this build itself.)

docs.title: Build notes / judgment calls
docs.text:
• The core finding of this test case is a framework gap, not a build workaround. ${param} substitution inside dq_config.rules[].expression is not implemented anywhere in the currently-deployed code -- confirmed by grepping every substitute_dynamic_parameters/ substitute_path_parameters call site (none touch dq/quarantine.py or dq/expectations.py) and independently corroborated by 17_onboarding_template_reference.md §3.4's own prose. As literally specified, TESTING_PLAN.md's TC-PRM-004 (${max_allowed_txn_limit}/${cutoff_date} inside the DQ expression) is not buildable today. This spec instead uses the same two values as literals in the expression, which faithfully exercises the quarantine mechanics the test case cares about, while pipeline_parameters is retained on the spec (unused) purely to keep the spec's shape recognizable against the plan.
  • New fixture, not a reuse. No existing CSV fixture has both a txn_amount and txn_date column combination exercising this rule's exact boundary values, so one new 8-row CSV (txns_dq_param.csv) and one new dedicated seed notebook were added, reusing the existing txns_usecase/ fixture-domain directory (established by TC-DQ-002) rather than creating a new domain directory, since both scenarios share the same transaction-feed use case.
  • 8 rows, 4/4 pass/quarantine split, covering all four condition combinations. Chosen over a larger volume so the split is trivially checkable by row count while still proving the AND expression's two halves are each independently capable of triggering quarantine (not just the amount bound, which is all TESTING_PLAN.md's own SQL assertion for this test case checks).
  • cdc_load_strategy: "APPEND". Same convention as every other DQ-focused test case (TC-DQ-001/002/004) -- the simplest load strategy, so nothing about CDC dispatch is in play while the DQ rule/parameter behavior is what's actually under test.

docs.title: Test Pipeline: TC-PRM-005 — Parameterized Egress Sink Paths & Export File Naming
docs.text: See also: Documentation index, flowx_testing/TESTING_PLAN.md (Module 11, TC-PRM-005), flowx_testing/TESTING_STATUS.md, 17_onboarding_template_reference.md §3.4 (the ${param} substitution mechanics this scenario exercises), 23_lakeflow_sinks.md (full sink_config/external_sink mechanics), 63_tc_snk_003.md (the sibling pgp_zip sink scenario this one's target_config shape is modeled on), 67_tc_prm_001.md (TC-PRM-001 — the same substitute_path_parameters feature exercised on an ingestion source's source_config.path instead of a sink target), 68_tc_prm_004.md (TC-PRM-004 — the other ${param}-in-a-non-SQL-field scenario built this same pass, with its own "declared but not substitutable" gap; contrast with this scenario, where the placeholders genuinely resolve).

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Prove transformation/parameters.py::substitute_path_parameters — this session's new ${param}-in-path-fields feature — on a sink target's target_config.sink_config, not just an ingestion source's source_config (that's TC-PRM-001; see flowx_testing/045_prm_001_path_param.json and 67_tc_prm_001.md). A small ACME Corp export-staging batch is Auto Loader-ingested and, inside the same Lakeflow Declarative Pipeline update, additionally exported as a ZIP archive via a genuine dlt.create_sink(format="pgp_zip") + @dlt.append_flow. pipeline_parameters: {"client_code": "ACME_CORP", "export_tier": "GOLD"} are substituted into sink_config.path and post_export_archive.output_zip_path fresh on every pipeline update — never at onboarding time — so the egress Volume path is resolved dynamically per client, a realistic multi-tenant egress shape (each client gets its own Unity Catalog Volume, {catalog}.egress.{client_code}).

This scenario also deliberately demonstrates a second, wholly unrelated templating mechanism living right next to the first one — archive/pgp_zip_sink.py's export_file_name_format, a plain Python str.format() template with its own placeholders ({batch_id}/{timestamp}), resolved at commit time by the sink's driver-side writer directly from the microbatch id and the UTC clock. See "Known gaps / judgment calls" below for exactly why these two mechanisms are kept separate in this build, contrary to TESTING_PLAN.md's own drafted row for this test case.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• One ingestion flow (df_prm_005_acme_export_ingest), source_type: "autoloader", cdc_load_strategy: "APPEND" — deliberately the simplest CDC strategy, since this scenario's whole point is path/filename parameterization, not CDC behavior (APPEND + autoloader still publishes a genuine Lakeflow Streaming Table, which target_type: "external_sink" requires of the main target before it will attach the export @dlt.append_flow — every CDC strategy except SCD3 satisfies this).
  • target_type: "external_sink" — flowx.silver_exports.acme_export_staging is materialized as a real, governed, queryable Delta table exactly like any other target type, plus a second @dlt.append_flow reads that same table into a dlt.create_sink(format="pgp_zip", ...).
  • sink_config.path (staging) and sink_config.post_export_archive.output_zip_path (final egress destination) both carry ${client_code}/${export_tier} placeholders — resolved against this spec's own pipeline_parameters by substitute_path_parameters, applied to the raw target_config_json text before json.loads(...), so both fields resolve in a single pass:
  • sink_config.path: "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/egress/${client_code}/_staging/${export_tier}/" → /Volumes/flowx/egress/ACME_CORP/_staging/GOLD/
  • post_export_archive.output_zip_path: "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/egress/${client_code}/output/" → /Volumes/flowx/egress/ACME_CORP/output/
  • No post_export_archive.pgp_encryption block — unlike TC-SNK-003, this scenario exports a plain (unencrypted) .zip, keeping the test focused on path/filename parameterization rather than encryption.
  • export_file_name_format: "acme_export_{batch_id}_{timestamp}" — the pre-existing str.format() mechanism, using only its own supported placeholders ({batch_id}, {timestamp}), never ${client_code}/${export_tier}.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• flowx_testing/047_prm_005_sink_param.json — the onboarding spec (one ingestion flow, no transformation/reconciliation flows).
  • sample_data/flowx_testing/acme_export_usecase/acme_export_staging.csv — 5-row plaintext fixture (export_id, client_code, export_tier, account_ref, amount, export_date), landed as-is. Its own client_code/export_tier column values happen to match the spec's pipeline_parameters (both ACME_CORP/GOLD) for a coherent scenario narrative, but this is purely cosmetic — path resolution is driven entirely by pipeline_parameters, never by row data.
  • notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/03_seed_prm_005_sink_param_data.py — lands acme_export_staging.csv into the input landing Volume (exports_ingest.landing) and provisions the per-client sink output Volume (egress.ACME_CORP) — a sink's destination Volume is never auto-created by the pipeline itself, unlike the pipeline's own default catalog/ schema (here flowx.silver_exports).

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• {catalog}.silver_exports.acme_export_staging — 5 rows, in plaintext, exactly matching acme_export_staging.csv's content, plus the usual __framework_* technical metadata columns — a genuine, queryable Unity Catalog table (the "dual materialization" half of external_sink).
  • /Volumes/{catalog}/egress/ACME_CORP/output/acme_export_<batch_id>_<timestamp>.zip — one plain (unencrypted) archive per micro-batch, landed in the client-code-parameterized Volume path. Its entries are the micro-batch's rows as JSON-Lines (archive/pgp_zip_sink.py's staging format), covering all 5 export rows across however many micro-batches Auto Loader's single input file produces (typically one).
  • information_schema.tables shows acme_export_staging as a real table (unlike a pure "sink" target type, which registers no table at all — see TC-SNK-002).

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
flowx_testing/047_prm_005_sink_param.json's one ingestion flow's target_config:

"target_config": {
  "cdc_load_strategy": "APPEND",
  "storage_format": "delta",
  "sink_config": {
    "path": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/egress/${client_code}/_staging/${export_tier}/",
    "format": "pgp_zip",
    "post_export_archive": {
      "enabled": true,
      "output_zip_path": "/Volumes/{{catalog}}/egress/${client_code}/output/",
      "export_file_name_format": "acme_export_{batch_id}_{timestamp}"
    }
  }
}

{{catalog}} is resolved once, at onboarding time, by onboarding/spec_loader.py. ${client_code} and ${export_tier} are resolved fresh on every pipeline update, by substitute_path_parameters, from pipeline_parameters: {"client_code": "ACME_CORP", "export_tier": "GOLD"} at the top of the same spec — the two substitutions are independent mechanisms that happen to compose in the same string. {batch_id}/{timestamp} in export_file_name_format are resolved later still, at commit time, by archive/pgp_zip_sink.py::_PgpZipStreamWriter._render_export_file_name — a third, completely separate resolution step, never touched by either of the above.

databricks bundle run flowx_test_prm_005_sink_param_job --target dev

Task chain: setup_control_tables → seed_prm_005_sink_param_data → onboard_prm_005 → run_pipeline_task.

-- Exactly 5 plaintext rows, matching acme_export_staging.csv's known content

FROM {catalog}.silver_exports.acme_export_staging
ORDER BY export_id;

# resolved to -- a plain .zip, never .zip.pgp (no pgp_encryption block was configured)
databricks fs ls dbfs:/Volumes/flowx/egress/ACME_CORP/output/
